Maximum award per project is $2.5 million. $5 million in FY 2026 funding is available, with up to 3 projects selected (maximum one award per jurisdiction). Application fee is $2,500.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public housing authorities and county governments partnering with housing developers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction and acquisition or rehabilitation of rental housing including apartment buildings, townhouses, single-family homes, single room occupancy buildings, and shared housing facilities. Purchase of existing privately owned housing to increase housing production.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide—all Maryland counties. Projects must be located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a public housing authority or county government partnering with a housing developer, or a county in conjunction with a PHA or developer acquiring existing housing
Sponsor must have an ownership interest in the project's ownership entity, as demonstrated by an organizational chart and/or partnership agreement
Projects must provide mixed-income, cross-subsidized housing

At least 20% of units must be set aside for households with gross annual income of 50% or less of area median income, or at least 40% of units for households with gross annual income of 60% or less of area median income
Proposed projects must be ready for occupancy within two (2) years of the award selection date
Projects must meet all threshold criteria established in the Multifamily Rental Financing Program Guide
Affirmative Fair Housing Marketing Plan (AFHMP) required using form HUD-935.2A
Tenant selection policy must be submitted prior to closing and must meet Department requirements
Compliance with federal and state fair housing and equal opportunity laws required
No tenant displacement without cause in the 12 months prior to application submission except for renovation in compliance with approved relocation plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Virtual information session held March 11, 2026 at 12 p.m. for questions about the program. 2. Submit application fee of $2,500 (check payable to 'Community Development Administration') separately to: Community Development Administration, Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, Post Office Box 2524, Landover Hills, MD 20784. 3. Complete full Application Submission Package including: Housing Innovation Pilot Program Application Form, CDA Form 202 Multifamily Rental Financing Application (dated February 2025), Certifications, Threshold Checklist, Applicant Self-Scoring form, Organizational Chart, and all required exhibits. 4. Application forms must not be retyped or modified. All information must be completed or marked not applicable. 5. Submit one complete electronic application via Procorem WorkCenter by May 18, 2026 at 12:00 p.m. Each section, attachment, and exhibit must be clearly tabbed. Include copy of fee check with application submission. 6. DHCD staff reviews for completeness; incomplete submissions will not be processed. 7. Complete proposals are submitted to scoring committee (may include state and local government agencies). 8. Proposals ranked by score; highest-scored selected and recommended to CDA Director for approval, then Secretary for final approval and allocation. 9. If two competing applications from same jurisdiction, they are ranked within jurisdiction by elements and points, with number of units as tiebreaker. 10. Waiver requests available and must be submitted at least 15 days prior to application deadline (by May 4, 2026) using Waiver Request Form on DHCD website.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program for Maryland residents who make their homes more accessible by adding accessibility features. Eligible applicants can receive up to 50% of renovation costs back, up to a maximum of $5,000 per year.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Applicants can receive a tax credit equal to up to 50% of their home renovation costs, with a maximum credit of $5,000 per year. The credit applies to renovations completed in the previous tax year that add accessibility features to the applicant's own home, a family member's home, or a rental property. DHCD can approve up to $1,000,000 in tax credits per year; if demand exceeds this amount, individual credits may be reduced proportionally. If approved, applicants receive a tax credit certificate by August 31st of the current calendar year and must file an amended tax return (Form 502X) with the DHCD tax credit certificate attached to claim the credit.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1st of the current calendar year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who have completed home renovations that add accessibility features for themselves, family members, or rental properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The tax credit can be used to offset Maryland tax liability for home renovation costs that include accessibility features such as no-step entrances, grab bars, handrails, chairlifts, elevators, roll-in showers, accessible parking spaces, rocker panel light switches, accessible door hardware, visual/auditory alarms for individuals with sensory disabilities, lever water controls, accessible kitchen appliances and workspaces, bathroom mirrors within reach ranges, slip-resistant floors, accessible storage, and other modifications that improve home accessibility.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is available statewide to all Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Be a Maryland resident
File taxes in Maryland for the same calendar year you made the renovations
Have proof of payment for home renovations that include accessibility features
Submit a completed application to DHCD with supporting documentation
Completed renovations must have occurred during the previous tax year
Provide receipts, invoices, and before-and-after photos as proof of expenses
Applicants must not have received funds or tax credits from other sources for the same renovation project
Only one application for services may be submitted per household
Applicants must keep documentation and provide it upon request to verify funds were used for intended purposes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, complete your home renovation and file your taxes for the year the renovation was completed. Then, submit your completed application and supporting documentation (detailed invoices, proof of payment, pre-renovation pictures, post-renovation pictures, and other supporting documentation/permits) by June 1st of the current calendar year. Submit your application by email to DHCD.SLP_Documentation@Maryland.gov or by mail to: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs- Independent Living Tax Credit Application, Attention: SLP Intake Team, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. DHCD will review your application and notify you by August 31st of the current calendar year. If approved, file an amended tax return (Form 502X) with the DHCD tax credit certificate attached to claim the credit. A representative from DHCD may contact you to gather additional information during the review process.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides loans to help homeowners and rental property owners install or repair indoor plumbing systems in residential properties that are structurally sound.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans with interest rates ranging from 0% to 6% based on the applicant's ability to pay and household income. Interest rates are 4.5% to 6.0% for households at 80% of median income, 0% to 4.5% for households at 60% of median income, and 0% for households at or below 50% of median income. Maximum loan amount is $50,000. Maximum loan term is 30 years. Deferred loans are available to borrowers at or below 50% of median income if necessary for project feasibility. Deferred amounts or portions of deferred amounts may be forgiven annually for families with incomes at or below 30% of the statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of single-family homes and owners of rental residential properties with household incomes at or below 80% of the statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wells, septic tanks and drain fields, piping from septic system into the residential building, connection expenses to public water or sewer systems including fees and assessments, plumbing fixtures and equipment including handicapped fixtures, additions and modifications required to provide private space for toilet and bath facilities, sand mound systems, purification systems, cost of percolation tests, and alternative and innovative septic and water systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties. Loans are generally processed directly by local governments for properties within their jurisdiction. For Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area income limit purposes, the following counties are included: Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, and Prince George's. All other Maryland counties use the Rest of State income limits.
requirements_list: Owner-occupants of single-family homes must have an income at or below 80% of the statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income (based on household size and location)
Owners of rental residential properties must ensure units will be occupied by income-eligible households
Properties must be structurally sound
Single-family homes must be owner-occupied and have inoperative or unsafe plumbing
Applicants must provide photo ID (driver's license, passport, military ID, etc.)
Proof of home ownership through deed and current mortgage statement required
Current property tax bill and homeowners insurance policy declaration page required
Flood insurance policy copy if applicable
Lowest qualifying bid from licensed Maryland tradesperson identifying repairs, not more than 60 days old
Total bids should not exceed $50,000
Bids must include photographs documenting the issues and contractor's phone number and email
Contractor must provide current MHIC License or trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance, Letter of Good Standing, and W-9 form
Income verification through paystubs, Federal Income Tax Returns, bank statements, or award letters for benefits
For properties built before 1978, lead-based paint disclosure and notification required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact their local housing office by county or the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Special Loan Programs at (301) 429-7409 (within Baltimore area), (877) 218-8101 (toll-free), or (844) 369-4150. Applicants must complete the Maryland Home Rehabilitation Program Application and submit with required documentation including income verification, proof of home ownership, property information, contractor bid with scope of work, and contractor documentation. Completed applications and supporting documentation should be submitted by email to DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov or by mail to: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. Loans are originated, packaged and closed by the Special Loan Program's network of local administering agencies, which includes county housing and community development offices, nonprofit organizations, and local banks.

structured_extraction.program_name: Lead Hazard Reduction Loan and Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps make Maryland homes safer by removing or reducing lead hazards in owner-occupied single family homes and rental properties. The program provides grants and loans to eligible applicants, including owner-occupants, for-profit sponsors, nonprofit sponsors, and licensed childcare facilities. The program is administered by DHCD using both state funds and federal funds from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development's Office of Lead Hazard Control and Healthy Homes.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $25,000 per eligible property for lead hazard reduction services. Amortizing loans available at 0%-7% interest for 20-year terms, and deferred loans available at 0% interest for 20-year terms. Grants require a 20% match for for-profit sponsors and 10% for nonprofit sponsors and owner-occupants with income above 80% of median. Owner-occupants with limited incomes (below 80% of median) have no match requirement. Maximum unit assistance is $25,000; maximum annual sponsor assistance for grants is $100,000. Deferred loans available only if underwriting shows no affordability to repay loan or property does not have sufficient equity. Loan interest rates: 0%-4.5% for households at or below 60% of median income; 4.5%-6.0% for households at or below 80% of median income. Licensed and accredited lead abatement contractor must perform services. Lead clearance testing is required upon completion.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 1, 2029
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners, landlords, for-profit sponsors, nonprofit sponsors, and licensed residential childcare facilities with incomes up to 80% of Area Median Income (AMI), with more favorable terms available for those at 60% or below of AMI. Licensed day care centers are also eligible to apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Lead hazard reduction and abatement activities including door and window treatments and replacement, floor treatments, paint removal, stabilization and repainting, encapsulation, enclosure, and specialized cleaning to meet risk reduction standards and lead dust clearance standards. Services must be performed by licensed and accredited lead abatement contractors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Grants require location in target areas or use of innovative lead hazard reduction treatments. For amortizing and deferred loans, income limits vary by household size and region: Washington DC PMSA (Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, Prince George's counties) and Rest of State. Loans are available regardless of location.
requirements_list: Property must be in Maryland
Property must have been built before 1978 or have confirmed lead-based paint presence
Applicant must be a Maryland resident if owner-occupant
Owner-occupant must own and occupy the dwelling as a principal residence
Property must be a single family home or rental property (1-4 units for sponsors)
Units must be in need of lead hazard reduction activity
Units must be structurally sound upon completion of lead hazard reduction activity
Units must be registered with the Maryland Department of the Environment Lead Poisoning Prevention Program
Licensed childcare facilities may be eligible
Income limits apply: 80% of Area Median Income (AMI) for standard programs; 60% of AMI for favorable interest rates; 50% or 30% of AMI may qualify for deferred payments

For grants: applicant must be in target area or plan to utilize innovative lead hazard reduction treatment; underwriting must show no affordability to repay loan or property does not have sufficient value to secure debt
For amortizing loans: 0%-7% interest rates based on income level and ability to repay over 20 years
For deferred loans: only available if underwriting shows no affordability to repay
Match requirement for grants: 20% for for-profit sponsors, 10% for nonprofit sponsors, 10% for owner-occupants with income above 80% of median
For-profit sponsors must pay all fees and charges; nonprofit sponsors and owner-occupants of limited income may include fees in financing
Licensed and accredited lead abatement contractor must perform services
Clearance testing is required upon completion of work
Applicant must provide bid from licensed Maryland tradesperson or company

For rental properties: tenant income must be limited or lower income; compliance with relocation requirements if displacement necessary; clearance testing required and property must be occupied by families of limited income upon completion
If children under age 6 or pregnant women reside in or regularly visit the property, special considerations apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact Special Loan Programs at 301-429-7409, toll-free 877-218-8101, or email DHCD.SpecialLoans@maryland.gov to obtain application materials. 2. For owner-occupants: Complete the Single Family Housing (Maryland Home Rehabilitation Program) application form and provide required income verification, home ownership documentation, and contractor bids. 3. For sponsors (nonprofits and for-profits): Complete the Sponsor Application Form and provide organizational documents, financial statements, and project details. 4. Submit completed application with all required documentation to DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov or mail to: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. 5. Required documentation includes: proof of income (paystubs, tax returns, benefit letters), proof of home ownership (deed, mortgage statement, property tax bill, homeowners insurance declaration page), photo ID, lead testing results, contractor bid with photos and MHIC license, Certificate of Liability Insurance with $1 million per occurrence limits, Letter of Good Standing, and W-9 form. 6. Incomplete applications will not be processed. 7. Underwriting will evaluate affordability to repay and property value. 8. Clearance testing will be required upon completion of work.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development issues tax-exempt bonds on behalf of counties, municipalities, and their agencies to finance community infrastructure projects. The program provides long-term capital financing with advantageous terms, reduces issuance costs through economies of scale, and helps local governments navigate the complexities of tax-exempt bond financing to support economic development and provide community services.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Community Development Administration issues tax-exempt bonds and loans the bond proceeds to local governments. The interest rate on the loans is based on market conditions at the time of bond sale and is tied to the rate attained on the pooled bond issue. Local governments repay the debt and pay their pro-rata share of the pooled bond issuance costs. Each participant pledges its full faith and credit to secure payment. The loan term is set by the local government but cannot exceed the useful life of the project or thirty years, whichever is less. The program is available for projects ranging from $150,000 to $10 million or more. Technical assistance is also available to help local governments complete the application.
structured_extraction.program_audience: All Maryland counties, municipalities, and their agencies with legal authority to construct, operate, and maintain projects, pledge security for and repay loans, and pledge income tax payments and shared revenue from the State.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Street lighting, landscaping, sidewalks and public space improvements; public safety vehicles and equipment; water production, treatment, storage and distribution systems; storm water control and sewer collection and treatment facilities; government office and meeting facilities; police, fire, transportation, education, health, recreation, maintenance and other service related facilities; and refinancing of existing debt for eligible projects. All projects must support an essential physical element of a municipality's public service system to support economic development and provide community services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties and municipalities are eligible.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland county, municipality, or their agency
Must have legal authority to construct, operate, and maintain the proposed project
Must have legal authority to pledge security for and repay the proposed loan
Must have legal authority to pledge income tax payments and various other shared revenue from the State
Project must support an essential physical element of a municipality's public service system
Project must meet federal tax law requirements
Project must be undertaken by or on behalf of a local government, including its agencies
Loan term cannot exceed the useful life of the project or thirty years, whichever is less
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The local government completes an application that provides information similar to what a bond rating agency would require to evaluate creditworthiness. When bonds are issued is influenced by the volume and frequency of participation by local governments. Technical assistance is available to help local governments complete the application. Those requesting technical assistance may submit an Expression of Interest form outlining the proposed project or specific questions.

structured_extraction.program_name: MEER: Maryland Emergency Education Relief Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to K-12 schools, libraries, and anchor institutions to close the digital divide for students and school staff by providing internet access or devices needed to connect to classrooms. The program helps communities improve broadband access, adoption and utilization.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $350,000 covering eligible program costs for qualifying expenses and projects. The program provided awards ranging from approximately $34,000 to $250,000 for specific projects including digital access initiatives, broadband access projects, and community technology centers.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Funding period: September 1, 2021 to September 15, 2022
structured_extraction.program_audience: K-12 schools, libraries, anchor institutions, community organizations, and government agencies
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Internet access, devices and equipment needed for students and school staff to connect to classrooms, broadband infrastructure projects, and community digital access initiatives
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - all Maryland counties eligible
requirements_list: Eligible applicants include Schools, Libraries, Anchor Institutions, and Community Organizations
Funding for qualifying expenses and projects completed between September 1, 2021 and September 15, 2022
Projects must address digital divide and broadband access gaps

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development provides funding to assist Maryland's designated and affiliate Main Street Maryland communities and Baltimore City's designated Main Street neighborhoods in building capacity to achieve their community revitalization and economic development goals in designated Sustainable Community areas throughout the state.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Main Street Improvement Program (MIP) Grant awards provide allocated funds to eligible grantees as follows: Designated Main Street Maryland Communities with full accreditation on their annual assessment receive approximately $33,000 each. Designated Main Street Maryland Communities accredited as affiliate receive approximately $25,000 each. Main Street Maryland Aspiring Communities receive approximately $12,000 each. Final amounts are contingent upon General Assembly approval during the FY2027 legislative session. Grants support operating expenses only, including salary, professional services contracts, technology costs, market and business recruitment strategies, marketing and advertising, placemaking initiatives, and other costs related to administering the Main Street program. Capital project costs are not supported through MIP. Funding match is not required. All projects and activities should be completed within one year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, March 20, 2026 at 5:00 PM (EDT)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Designated and Aspiring Main Street Maryland communities and Baltimore City's designated Main Street neighborhoods
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grants support operating expenses only, including salary, professional services contracts, technology costs, market and business recruitment strategies, marketing and advertising, placemaking initiatives, and other costs related to administering the Main Street program. All projects and activities should be completed within one year. Requested funds should support projects and activities that align with the applicant's annual work plan and contribute to the community's transformation strategy. Capital project costs are not supported.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland's designated and affiliate Main Street Maryland communities and Baltimore City's designated Main Street neighborhoods in designated Sustainable Community areas throughout the state.
requirements_list: Only designated and aspiring Main Street Maryland communities are eligible
Grants can be used for operating expenses only; capital project costs are not supported
Projects and activities must align with applicant's annual work plan
Projects and activities must contribute to community transformation strategy
All projects and activities should be completed within one year
Funding match is not required
Organization profile must include all required documents before application submission

Current Operating Assistance Grant Program awardees must be in full compliance with all existing award agreements, including meeting all reporting deadlines and submitting all required final reports and payment requests from prior awards

Nonprofit applicants must submit evidence of nonprofit status (Bylaws, Articles of Incorporation, IRS Determination Letter), evidence of good standing (Md. State Department of Assessments and Taxation), and evidence of charitable registration (Md. Secretary of State)
First-time applicants must contact a project manager for eligibility verification and system access
New organizations should request access and submit organizational documents at least two weeks before the application deadline
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the DHCD Project Portal at https://projectportal.dhcd.state.md.us/. To access the portal, register as a new user and complete the registration request form, which may take up to 72 hours for approval. Ensure your organization profile includes all required documents before submitting your application. First-time applicants must contact a project manager for eligibility verification and system access. New organizations should submit organizational documents at least two weeks before the application deadline to expedite processing. Applications missing required documents may be disqualified. All applications must be submitted online; late applications will not be accepted. Training documents, including a program overview and step-by-step application guide, are available in the DHCD Project Portal. A virtual application training session is scheduled for Tuesday, March 3, 2026 from 1-2 PM EDT. Individual technical assistance sessions are available by scheduling online via Calendly. Upon award, awardees must execute an Award Agreement through DocuSign within five business days of receipt. The authorized signatory for your organization must sign the agreement. Funds cannot be drawn down until after execution and all Special Conditions have been met. Following award execution, awardees should draw down at least 50% of awarded funds within six months of the award execution date. All awarded funds must be drawn down by the award agreement's expiration date. Progress reports are due at 6 months from the grant agreement execution date or whenever a payment request is submitted. A final report is due no later than 30 days after the award agreement's expiration date and must include certification of completion, visual documentation (before and after pictures preferred), financial reconciliation, compliance verification, and results documentation. All progress reports must be submitted electronically through the DHCD Project Portal.

structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive downtown revitalization program created to strengthen the economic potential of Maryland's traditional main streets and neighborhoods.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A comprehensive downtown revitalization program that provides support to strengthen the economic potential of Maryland's traditional main streets and neighborhoods.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Communities with traditional main streets and neighborhoods in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Downtown revitalization and economic strengthening of traditional main streets and neighborhoods
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: An emergency loan program that provides financial assistance to small businesses affected by disasters. The program is only available when activated by the Secretary of the Department of Housing and Community Development for specific disaster events.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans available for renovations, repairs and replacement of furniture, fixtures and equipment, inventory replacement, loss of revenues, operating and leasing expense assistance, and other costs associated with business recovery including working capital.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based small businesses and nonprofit organizations located in commercial spaces that have been affected by disasters and meet eligibility criteria.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Renovations, repairs and replacement of furniture, fixtures and equipment, inventory replacement, loss of revenues or operating and leasing expense assistance, and other costs associated with business recovery including working capital.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must be located in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Howard County, Frederick County, or Washington County and show evidence of damage or loss associated with qualifying disaster events.
requirements_list: Maryland-based small business or nonprofit organization
Business located in commercial space
Located in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Howard County, Frederick County, or Washington County
Show evidence of damage or loss associated with qualifying disaster events
Proof of insurance status required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development Neighborhood BusinessWorks Program to inquire about application procedures when the program is activated for a specific disaster.

structured_extraction.program_description: A credit enhancement program that helps small businesses in Priority Funding Areas get loans by establishing a loan loss reserve fund. Private lenders, borrowers, and the State of Maryland each contribute to the reserve, which protects lenders if loans default. This enables lenders to approve loans that fall slightly outside their normal credit guidelines.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participating lenders enroll loans ranging from $10,000 to $1,000,000. Lenders, borrowers, and the state each contribute to a reserve account, typically 1.5 percent from the lender and borrower each, matched by a 3 percent contribution from the program, totaling 6 percent of the loan amount. The reserve protects the lender if the loan defaults. Early loans (the first $2 million of enrolled loans per lender) may draw additional reserves on subsequent loans if needed, provided remaining claim balance does not exceed 75 percent of reserve account balance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, including nonprofit organizations, located in Maryland's Priority Funding Areas
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital, expansion, equipment, inventory, and other business purposes. Loan proceeds cannot finance passive real estate ownership, residential or transient living facilities, institutional facilities like hospitals or colleges, adult entertainment or certain service establishments, or sectarian religious instruction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Priority Funding Areas approved by the Maryland Department of Planning under the Smart Growth Act of 1997.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland small business, including nonprofit organizations
Business must be located in a Priority Funding Area
Loan amount must range from $10,000 to $1,000,000
Project cannot involve passive real estate ownership
Project cannot be residential or transient living facilities
Project cannot be institutional facilities like hospitals, colleges, or fire stations
Project cannot involve adult entertainment, check cashing, gambling, liquor stores, massage parlors, pawn shops, gun shops, tanning salons, or tattoo parlors
Loan proceeds cannot further sectarian religious instruction
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A small business applies to a participating lender. The lender underwrites and enrolls the loan if it meets program criteria. The lender, borrower, and program each contribute to a reserve account. The lender submits a one-page enrollment form to the program. If the loan defaults, the lender files a one-page claim form after exhausting normal collection methods.

structured_extraction.program_description: MEAP helps eligible Maryland households repair or replace heating, cooling, and water heating systems at no cost. The program operates year-round and is federally funded to make homes more comfortable.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants to repair or replace non-functioning heating, cooling, and water heating systems at no cost to eligible households. Applicants must have household income below 200 percent of the Federal Poverty Level. Specific work eligible for assistance is determined based on a home assessment and funding availability. The maximum initial deposit is 33% of the total project cost.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible Maryland homeowners with household income below 200 percent of the federal poverty level who have non-functioning heating, cooling, and/or water heating systems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repair or replacement of heating, cooling, and water heating systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland. Special flood assistance available in Allegany or Garrett County for homes affected by flooding.
requirements_list: Household income must be lower than the limits based on household size (200% Federal Poverty Level)
Have a non-functioning heating, cooling, and/or water heating system
Currently approved to receive Energy Assistance payments from Maryland Department of Human Services qualifies for expedited intake
Own or rent the property (renters may have additional requirements)
Provide copy of most recent electric utility bill
Provide proof of last 30 days GROSS household income
Provide copy of Social Security card(s) for all household members
Provide copy of Photo ID for the applicant
If mobile home owner: provide copy of title or bill of sale for the home to prove ownership
Complete Zero Income Form for any household member 18 years or older claiming no income
May have medical condition requiring functioning heating, cooling, or water heating systems (physician's letter required)
For homeowners applying for general repairs: provide Supplemental Financial Information, Tax Affidavit, and Credit Pull Consent
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the DHCD Energy & Repair Programs Application and submit all required documents to Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, Attn: Weatherization, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706. Instructions for completing and returning the application are located on the first page of the application. For quick application eligibility (with certain benefit programs), submit Client Information, Household Information, Energy Consent Form, and copy of most recent electric utility bill plus proof of program benefits. For standard application, submit all pages including Client Information, Household Information, Energy Consent Form, utility bill, proof of income, Social Security cards, Photo ID, and Zero Income Forms if applicable. Once eligibility is determined, a local agency will contact you to schedule a home assessment. The local agency will evaluate your service needs and discuss results with you. A contractor will then be scheduled to complete the recommended work. Incomplete applications missing required documentation cannot be processed.

structured_extraction.program_description: Funding program that supports commercial facade improvement projects to enhance the marketability and appearance of downtowns and Main Street areas in revitalized communities. The program provides funding to assist qualified businesses with improving the exterior of their buildings and facilities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Capital grants to assist qualified businesses located in Sustainable Communities with improving the exterior facades of their buildings or facilities. FY2026 budgeted funding is $5 million. Local governments and community development organizations apply for the program to capitalize a grants fund and develop an application process for businesses to improve their building facades. Awardees develop and enforce their own local program guidelines, which must include criteria for rating qualified businesses and awarding grants. The FAAP (Financial Assistance and Application Processing) fee does NOT apply to Maryland Facade Improvement Program awards.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: July 2, 2025 at 2:59 PM (FY26 application round closed)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and nonprofit community development organizations seeking funding to capitalize grants funds and develop application processes for businesses to improve their building facades in designated revitalization areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital costs related to the improvement of exterior facades for business buildings and facilities within Sustainable Communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within Sustainable Community boundaries in Maryland. Awardees should provide an address at time of application confirmed to be in the Sustainable Community. If award funds support a project with addresses to be determined, awardees should provide addresses and evidence of target area eligibility as they are identified during the life of the award. Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to verify Sustainable Community boundaries.
requirements_list: Project must be located within a Sustainable Community boundary
Commercial facade improvement focus
Capital project with at least 15-year shelf life
Local program guidelines must include criteria for rating qualified businesses and awarding grants
Awardee must develop and enforce local program guidelines
Organizations must be in good standing with SDAT and Maryland Charitable Organizations Registration
Current awardees must be in compliance with terms and conditions of existing award agreements
New organizations must register as users in the Project Portal at least 2 weeks before application deadline (by June 11 for FY26)
Organizations with previous year funding required to be current on reporting and program requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register as a new user in the Project Portal (approval may take up to 72 hours; new user registration deadline is June 11). Upload required organizational documents to your profile including: Signed Disclosure Authorization and Certification, IRS W-9 Form, operating budget for current fiscal year, most recent independent financial audit or prior calendar year IRS Form 990, articles of incorporation, bylaws, IRS tax exempt determination letter, current board of directors list, evidence of Certificate of Good Standing from SDAT, Maryland Charitable Organizations Registration letter, and corporate diversity addendum. Submit application through the Project Portal by the application deadline with all required supporting documents including evidence of site control, documentation of funding commitments, cost estimates, program guidelines, Sustainable Communities map evidence, photos, and construction/renovation plans if applicable. Maryland Historical Trust review is required for all capital projects prior to disbursement of funds. FY26 application period opened May 28, 2025 and closed July 2, 2025 at 3:00 PM. Review period: Summer 2025. Award recommendations: Fall 2025. Award announcements: Fall/Winter 2025. 50% of awarded funds must be drawn down by the first anniversary date of the award. Award term is 2 years.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Housing Counseling Fund supports non-profit and local government organizations that provide housing counseling services and free or low-cost legal assistance. Awards are made annually on a competitive basis.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual competitive grants provide operating support for housing counseling programs including homebuyer education, pre-purchase counseling, foreclosure counseling, rental counseling, and financial capability coaching. Grants also support non-profit legal services providers that assist homeowners concerned about foreclosure and renters concerned about eviction.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Closed
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations and local government agencies that provide housing counseling and legal assistance services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating support for housing counseling programs including homebuyer education, pre-purchase counseling, foreclosure counseling, rental counseling, and financial capability coaching. Support for non-profit legal services providers assisting homeowners concerned about foreclosure and renters concerned about eviction.
requirements_list: Must be a non-profit organization or local government agency
Must provide housing counseling services or free or low-cost legal assistance
Grantees must submit a quarterly progress report by the fifteenth of the month following the end of each quarter of the grant term.
Priority funding consideration is given to HUD-approved housing counseling agencies with HUD-certified counselors on staff.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted on a competitive basis. To apply, email the program team at mhcf.dhcd@maryland.gov to request an application. Grantees are required to submit quarterly progress reports by the fifteenth of the month following the end of each quarter of the grant term.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides affordable loans to homeowners to address critical health and safety issues and bring properties into compliance with building codes and standards. It helps owner-occupants of single-family homes make necessary repairs and improvements.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans are available with interest rates based on household income and ability to repay. The maximum loan is generally $50,000, or up to 110% of home equity, whichever is less. Interest rates range from 0% to 6% depending on income level. The maximum loan term is 30 years. Loans exceeding $5,000 or with deferred payments are secured by a mortgage (deed of trust recorded on property). There is a minimum loan amount of $5,000. Households with incomes at or below 50 percent of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income may qualify for deferred principal and interest payments if necessary for project feasibility. Applicants with incomes at 60% of area median income qualify for 0%-4.5% interest rates. Applicants with incomes at 80% of area median income qualify for 4.5%-6.0% interest rates. The maximum initial deposit from contractors is 33% of total project cost.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of single-family homes whose household income does not exceed 80 percent of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mold remediation, gas leak repair, roof repair and replacement, gutters, asbestos abatement, vermiculite removal, lead abatement, combustion appliance repair and replacement, chimney repair, foundation and sub-space waterproofing and drainage including bulk water mitigation by drain tile and sump pump, radon mitigation, electrical hazard and knob-and-tube removal, electrical upgrades for electrification (100A to 200A upgrades), plumbing issues, water and well repairs, septic and sewer work, windows and doors for health and safety or water intrusion and security, structural repair (atrophy, rot, insect damage, settling, storm-related), accessibility improvements for disabled persons and seniors (chair lifts, handicap ramps, bars, railings, doors), fall prevention measures (handrails, rubber treads, bathroom grab bars), HVAC replacement for end of service life, ductwork upgrades and installations (primarily for solid fuel-burning households, mainly in Allegany and Garrett counties), building shell stabilization (repair/replace missing sheetrock on exterior walls, point up deteriorated masonry that allows for water infiltration), and pest treatments (rats, roaches, mice).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties. Local government housing offices process loan requests for properties within their jurisdiction. The Washington, D.C. PMSA includes Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties and has different income limits.
requirements_list: Household income cannot exceed 80 percent of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income
Property must be an owner-occupied single-family home (duplexes, townhomes, condos, and manufactured homes are excluded)
Applicant must be the owner-occupant; renters and tenants are not eligible
Property must be the applicant's primary residence
If others are named on the deed but do not occupy the property, proof must be provided that they live elsewhere (copy of driver's license, utility bill, notarized statement, or other evidence)
If a person on the deed is deceased, a copy of the death certificate must be provided
Applicant must provide a work proposal from a licensed and insured Maryland Home Improvement contractor or other trade professional, dated within the past 60 days
Applicant must provide photographs documenting the health and safety issues
Contractor must provide current Maryland Home Improvement Contractor (MHIC) License or applicable trade license (Electrical, Plumbing, HVAC, etc.)
Contractor must provide Certificate of Liability Insurance (current with per occurrence limits equal to or greater than $1,000,000)
Contractor must provide Letter of Good Standing from Maryland licensing authority
Contractor must provide completed and signed W-9 form with contractor's address where payments will be sent
Applicant must provide photo ID for applicant and any co-applicant (driver's license, passport, military ID, etc.)
Applicant must provide copy of deed and current mortgage statement
Applicant must provide copy of most recent Property Tax Bill
Applicant must provide copy of Declaration Page of Homeowners Insurance Policy
Applicant must provide copy of Flood Insurance Policy if applicable
Applicant must provide most recent two months' worth of paystubs (8 for weekly pay, 4 for bi-weekly pay) for each employed household member, or letter verifying employment signed by employer
Applicant must provide most recent 2 years' worth of complete Federal Income Tax Returns
Applicant must provide most recent 2 months' worth of bank statements
If income from Social Security, disability, pension, or public assistance, must provide copies of award letters and current statements verifying gross income
If reporting no income, must include signed and notarized Zero Income Statement
If not required to file Federal Income Tax Return, must provide signed affidavit explaining reason for each year
For health and safety repairs, applicant may apply for supplemental funding with additional financial documentation
No minimum credit score requirement
Cannot assist if there is active bankruptcy or foreclosure; both must be dismissed for minimum of 2 years before assistance can be provided
Work must meet critical health and safety needs requirements
Total repair costs should not exceed $50,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact your local county housing office or the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Special Loan Programs at (301) 429-7409, (301) 429-7564 (Baltimore area), or toll-free 877-218-8101. 2. Obtain at least one detailed estimate (bid) from a licensed Maryland Home Improvement Contractor or other licensed trade professional within the past 60 days for health and safety repairs needed. Include photographs documenting the issues in the bid. 3. Ensure the contractor completes the Bid Cover Page and provides all required documentation: current MHIC or trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance, Letter of Good Standing, and signed W-9 form. 4. Gather all required income verification documents (paystubs, tax returns, bank statements, benefit letters, etc.). 5. Gather all required property ownership documentation (photo ID, deed, mortgage statement, property tax bill, homeowners insurance declaration page, flood insurance if applicable). 6. Complete the Maryland Housing Rehabilitation Program application with all required information including applicant/co-applicant information, income details, housing expenses, assets, liabilities, personal debt history, demographic data, and lead-based paint notification receipt. 7. For applications including health and safety repairs, complete Supplemental Financial Information page with additional financial details. 8. Submit completed application and all required documents to: Email: DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov OR Mail: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. 9. Local government housing rehabilitation offices process loan requests for properties within their jurisdiction. 10. Program staff will review the bid and all documentation to verify work meets health and safety requirements and contractor meets state requirements. 11. Upon approval, applicant must sign: Commitment letter, Rehabilitation contract, Construction agreement, and W-9 form. 12. Once all agreements are signed, funding is disbursed according to project timeline.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide initiative that reduces interest rates on loans for certified Minority Business Enterprises and Small Businesses by up to 2% when they obtain qualifying loans from participating banks.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible borrowers can receive up to a 2% discount on interest rates for term loans obtained from participating banks. The Maryland State Treasurer's Office deposits an amount equal to the loan amount from the issuing bank and accepts a reduced interest rate on that deposit. Loans can be combined with other loan programs. Loan terms cannot exceed 10 years, and points charged by the lender cannot exceed 1% of the loan amount.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Certified Minority Business Enterprises and Small Businesses in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Loan proceeds must be used for projects or activities located in Maryland. Funds cannot be used for the furtherance of sectarian or religious purposes or instruction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects or activities must be located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Borrower must be a certified minority business enterprise in good standing with the Maryland Department of Transportation, or a small business in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Borrower must notify the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development prior to obtaining qualifying loans from enrolled financial institutions
Borrower must obtain loan from a participating lender designated by the Maryland State Treasurer's Office
Loan must be a term loan or fixed-rate loan with one disbursement
Loan terms cannot exceed 10 years
Points charged by the lender cannot exceed 1% of the loan amount
Loan proceeds must be used for projects located in Maryland

Borrower must remain in good standing as a certified Minority Business Enterprise or small business with the State of Maryland to receive the interest rate reduction benefit for the full term of the loan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: An eligible applicant or participating lender submits a brief application via the Internet or paper form to the Linked Deposit Program, administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. After verifying the applicant's eligibility, the department forwards the application to all enrolled banks or notifies the lender of the borrower's eligibility. The borrower contacts participating banks to complete full application requirements. Banks underwrite the requested loan according to their standard underwriting with an interest rate up to 2% less than the standard rate. Upon loan approval and acceptance by the borrower, the bank enrolls the loan in the Linked Deposit Program. Participating lenders include Bank Annapolis, Industrial Bank, and Columbia Bank.

structured_extraction.program_description: A direct payment program that provides qualified renters with an annual tax credit of up to $1,000.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct check payment of up to $1,000 per year for qualified renters.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified renters in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To help offset rental housing costs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a qualified renter

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Small Business Development Financing Authority (MSBDFA) Equity
structured_extraction.program_description: Assists businesses in socially and economically disadvantaged areas with equity investments for expansion and growth.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Equity investments ranging from $25,000 to $1,000,000 in the form of preferred stock, common stock, warrants, partnership interests, and other equity-like structures. Requires minimum 1:1 private capital match.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses in socially and economically disadvantaged areas seeking equity investments for expansion and growth.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equity investments for business expansion and growth.
requirements_list: Minimum 1:1 private capital match

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Small Business Development Financing Authority - EPIP Loan
structured_extraction.program_description: Assists businesses in socially and economically disadvantaged areas to obtain working capital, equipment, or contract financing.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $25,000 to $1,000,000. Requires minimum 1:1 private capital match with lender holding 20% at risk.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses in socially and economically disadvantaged areas seeking loans for working capital, equipment, or contract financing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital, equipment, or contract financing.
requirements_list: Minimum 1:1 private capital match
Lender must have 20% at risk

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program administered by Maryland that expands access to capital to small businesses. The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development offers flexible loans and equity investments to small businesses across the state, with special focus on projects with significant community impacts including job retention or creation, child care access, fresh food access, and community revitalization. It partners with the Maryland Department of Commerce and the Maryland Technology Development Corporation, focusing on communities with many small, micro, and socially and economically disadvantaged businesses.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_prioritized_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct loans of $500,000 to $5 million (total project costs cannot exceed $20 million) with flexible terms up to 30 years. Loans available in senior or subordinate positions. Interest rates determined by underwriting analysis. Minimum 1:1 private capital match required. Funds can be used for: (1) Costs to sustain or expand a small business, such as purchasing machinery or equipment, and working capital; and (2) Owner-occupied real estate acquisition or renovation (renovation projects must be at least 51% owner-occupied upon completion; new construction must be at least 60% owner-occupied upon completion). Also supports capital access programs, loan participations, loan guarantees, collateral support, and venture equity programs. Program Fees: $250 application fee, $250 closing fee, and 1% origination fee. The program does not offer grants.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses with fewer than 500 employees, particularly those with limited opportunities for growth, including socially and economically disadvantaged individuals and micro-businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business expansion and growth, including machinery and equipment purchases, working capital, and owner-occupied real estate acquisition or renovation. Also supports capital access programs, loan participations, loan guarantees, collateral support, and venture equity programs. Funds cannot be used for passive real estate investment, debt refinancing with same lender, tax repayment, equity buyouts (except majority ESOPs or worker co-ops), lobbying activities, federally guaranteed loans, or prohibited refinancing of tenant improvement loans.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide, with focus on communities and areas with high concentrations of small, micro, and socially and economically disadvantaged businesses.
requirements_list: Fewer than 500 employees
Not 100% residential (mixed-use projects may qualify)
Minimum 1:1 private capital match
Minimum loan amount of $500,000 and maximum of $5 million
Total project costs cannot exceed $20 million
Personal guarantees required from owners with greater than 20% equity interest
Adequate collateral required

Business cannot be: adult entertainment facilities, check cashing facilities, gambling facilities, gun shops, liquor stores, massage parlors, pawn shops, tanning salons, tattoo parlors, or cannabis businesses
Information provided must be accurate and complete
Applicants must comply with all federal, state, and local laws including environmental, labor, and anti-discrimination regulations
Special focus given to projects with significant community impacts including job retention or creation, child care access, fresh food access, and community revitalization
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can apply directly with SSBCI lending partners or use the application portal at https://apps.dhcd.state.md.us/nbwapplication. Eligible private capital lenders must be licensed in Maryland to offer small business lending and must be active in lending to Maryland-based small businesses. Non-bank lenders, non-credit unions, or non-CDFIs must be approved by the Department of Housing and Community Development. Email dhcd.businesslending@maryland.gov for a consultation about whether SSBCI is the right solution for your business. Technical assistance is available through the MD Business Opportunity Center and F3Tech SEDI Program. All applications are subject to underwriting and final DHCD approval; program participation does not guarantee loan approval or funding.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Town Manager Circuit Rider Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides grants to small town and city governments to hire professional staff to work as circuit riders. These staff members provide assistance with specific municipal functions and activities across multiple towns.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual funding is determined by General Assembly appropriation each year. Grant funds pay for salary and fringe benefits for circuit rider staff over a two year period.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Varies annually - eligible governments are notified at the opening of the competition and when applications are due
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small municipalities with populations of 5,000 or less, and the sponsors (municipal, county, regional governmental, or private organizations) that apply on their behalf
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Salary and fringe benefits for circuit rider professional staff who provide administrative support and assistance with municipal functions and activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Eligible municipalities must be within reasonable proximity to each other within a circuit of two or more municipalities.
requirements_list: Municipal or county government, regional governmental organization, or private organization must sponsor the circuit
Circuit must consist of two or more municipalities within reasonable proximity to each other
Each municipality in the circuit must have a population of 5,000 or less
Applicants are evaluated based on need, proposed accomplishments, and financial commitment
Existing circuits are also evaluated on past performance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Funding is provided through a competitive process each year. Eligible governments are notified when the competition opens and when applications are due. Applications are evaluated based on need, proposed accomplishments, financial commitment and support, and existing circuits are also evaluated on past performance. Technical assistance is available for interested governments and sponsors.

structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides flexible financing for starting, rehabilitating, or expanding businesses and nonprofits that offer healthy food options, particularly those sourcing fresh food from Maryland farmers, in designated food desert areas and Sustainable Communities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_prioritized_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Flexible financing through the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Neighborhood BusinessWorks program for start-up, rehabilitation, or expansion of food businesses and nonprofits.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses and nonprofits offering healthy food options in food deserts and Sustainable Communities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Start-up, rehabilitation, or expansion of businesses and nonprofits offering fresh and healthy foods
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be located in a designated Food Desert Area or Sustainable Community in Maryland
requirements_list: Located in a designated Food Desert Area or Sustainable Community
Offer healthy food options including fresh fruits and vegetables
Preference for sourcing fresh food from Maryland farmers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through selected community-based lending intermediaries who recruit, capitalize, and support food-related enterprises in underserved communities.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program that helps microentrepreneurs start and expand small businesses by providing flexible financing. The program works through community-based microlenders called intermediaries that originate and administer loans and provide training and technical assistance. Loans are provided to local Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) which then lend to small businesses in Maryland communities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Microenterprise loans up to $50,000 with interest rates up to 12%; loan terms cannot exceed 5 years. Collateral is required and may include personal guarantees, liens on business assets, and pledges of accounts. No prepayment penalties apply. Loans are provided through local CDFIs and community-based microlenders acting as intermediaries.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on rolling basis; contact for additional information
structured_extraction.program_audience: Microentrepreneurs seeking to start or expand small businesses with no more than 5 employees and annual revenue not exceeding $500,000. Loans are administered through Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) and community-based microlenders.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital, marketing, planning, feasibility studies, real estate acquisition down payment, minor renovations, minor leasehold improvements, machinery and equipment, and other costs associated with opening or expanding a small business.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in designated Sustainable Communities and Priority Funding Areas throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Business must be a retail, manufacturing, or goods and services related business
Located in a designated Sustainable Community area
Annual revenue cannot exceed $500,000
Not more than 5 employees at time of application
Collateral required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the intermediary microlender directly to receive an application. Intermediary partners include Baltimore Community Lending, Enterprise Development Group, Latino Economic Development Center, Maryland Capital Enterprises Inc., and Prince George's Financial Service Corporation. The program accepts applications on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides tax-exempt bond financing for construction, acquisition, and rehabilitation of multifamily rental housing for families with limited incomes. Bonds provide both construction and permanent financing and can be combined with federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax-exempt bonds and notes provide construction and permanent financing for multifamily rental housing projects. Multiple financing options are available including FHA-CDA Risk Sharing (40-year maturity), GNMA MBS (40-year maturity), Freddie Mac Tax Exempt Loans (17-year maturity), Cash Collateral structures (2-year construction period), and FNMA MBS Collateral for Tax Exempt Bonds (17-year maturity). Interest rates vary by financing structure; estimated all-in permanent rates range from approximately 5.77% to 6.82% depending on the option selected. Loan terms are generally 30 to 40 years for permanent financing. A first lien position is generally required. Loans must be insured or have other forms of credit enhancement acceptable to the program. The program participates in the Federal Housing Administration/Housing Finance Agency Risk Sharing Program. Construction period financing is available for 20-24 months with interest capitalization. Principal and interest are amortized over 35-40 year permanent loan periods depending on the financing structure selected.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and nonprofit developers building or rehabilitating multifamily rental housing
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction, acquisition, and rehabilitation of multifamily rental housing containing a minimum of five units. Loans may refinance existing high interest rate private loans if the refinance accompanies housing rehabilitation. Projects must consist of complete independent dwelling units.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide
requirements_list: Projects must contain a minimum of five units
Rental housing may be new construction, acquisition, and rehabilitation of existing housing
Projects using tax-exempt bond financing must contain complete independent dwelling units
Projects financed with tax-exempt bonds must comply with the Maryland Qualified Allocation Plan to receive unallocated 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits
All loans must be insured or have other forms of credit enhancement acceptable to the program

Sponsors must make either 20 units available to households earning 50 percent or less of area median income, or 40 percent of units available to households earning 60 percent or less of area median income
For Tax/TE financing, GNMA loan must have HUD/GNMA credit enhancement via Section 221(d), 220, or other similar HUD programs; FHA Risk Sharing with CDA is not eligible for this structure
A MAP Lender must be engaged by the borrower for GNMA financing
Bond proceeds must be sufficient to satisfy the 50% test for Tax Credits
Full amount of Bonds must be secured 100% by cash collateral
Projects using Tax Credits are subject to risk associated with monthly changes to the Tax Credit Percentage
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Housing Development Programs or specific loan officers to discuss financing structures and submit applications. For projects using Tax/TE financing structures, unrated private placement bonds require CDA approval of the purchasing entity and compliance with bankruptcy and risk acknowledgment requirements. Rated bond transactions require a bankruptcy opinion meeting rating agency requirements. A TEFRA Public Hearing may be required for certain projects. Prospective borrowers should discuss their specific project structure with CDA staff to determine the most appropriate financing option and required documentation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Multifamily Energy Efficiency and Housing Affordability Program (MEEHA) - EmPOWER
structured_extraction.program_description: MEEHA EmPOWER provides grants or loans to reduce electric or gas consumption in affordable multifamily rental housing developments. The program funds energy efficiency measures and limited health and safety repairs in projects that reduce energy consumption. The program also includes the MEEHA Greenhouse Gas Reduction Program (GHGRP) for electrification of covered buildings under Maryland's Building Energy Performance Standards.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: EmPOWER provides either grants or loans with 0% interest and deferred payments. Funding is allocated at $134.9 million for calendar years 2024-2026. Projects receive funds during construction as work is completed and verified through a requisition process, with DHCD inspecting a sample of installed measures and processing payment within 4-5 weeks. For rehabilitation projects, funding is provided on a per-unit basis with different tiers based on affordability compliance periods. Tier 1 funding applies to projects with a minimum of 5 years of affordability at 80% AMI or below. Tier 2 funding applies to projects with a minimum of 15 years of affordability. GHGRP funding is limited to $15,000 per unit for eligible covered buildings.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of affordable multifamily rental housing developments seeking to reduce energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduce electric or gas consumption through energy efficiency measures including HVAC systems, insulation, fenestration, lighting, domestic hot water systems, air sealing, and appliances. Electrification measures to replace fossil fuel systems with electric equipment. Limited health and safety or incidental repairs in projects completing measures that reduce electric or gas consumption. Gas reducing measures allowed only for projects in Baltimore Gas and Electric Company (BGE) or Washington Gas Light Company (WGL) utility territory. Electrification costs cannot exceed 10% of total funding for electrification measures. Health and safety and incidental repair costs combined cannot exceed 10% of total energy efficiency measure funding.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties eligible. Gas reducing measures are allowed only if the customer is in Baltimore Gas and Electric Company (BGE) or Washington Gas Light Company (WGL) utility territory. GHGRP applies to covered buildings under Maryland's Building Energy Performance Standards.
requirements_list: A minimum of 20% of households must be at 80% Area Median Income (AMI) or less for a minimum of 5 years for EmPOWER projects (Tier 1)
A minimum of 20% of households must be at 80% Area Median Income (AMI) or less for a minimum of 15 years for EmPOWER projects (Tier 2)
For GHGRP, a minimum of 51% of units must be at or below 80% AMI for a minimum of 15 years
Project must demonstrate readiness to proceed
Project must show energy savings and reduction of greenhouse gases
All building sizes and configurations eligible including single family units as a group project, individually metered, or master metered buildings

For GHGRP, single building must have gross floor area of 35,000 sq ft or more (excluding parking garages) OR two or more buildings with combined gross floor area of 35,000 sq ft or more served by same electric/gas meter or heating/cooling systems
Rehabilitation projects must complete energy audit by approved Qualified Energy Professional from DHCD's QEP List
Energy audit must comply with BPI Multifamily Building Analyst standards and be comprehensive whole building analysis
Post-retrofit building must meet current ASHRAE 62.2 ventilation standards
Mandatory measures must be included unless waiver granted on case-by-case basis
Air sealing in accessible locations is mandatory
Insulation in gabled attics below R-19 is mandatory if accessible
Insulation in crawlspace, basement rim joist, ceiling, and walls is mandatory if no insulation exists defining building envelope
HVAC replacement is mandatory when existing equipment is past useful life
Accessible duct sealing is mandatory
Energy Conservation Measures must be submitted with actual contractor bids including materials, equipment, and installation costs
Qualified Energy Professional submits funding request on behalf of project owner through MINT or Rehab Funding Request Form
Projects must maintain affordability compliance throughout respective affordability period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit MEEHA Application and supporting documents (application form, commercial utility bills, customer consent form, property deed, SDAT checks, MBE Plan, ACH Direct Deposit Form, affordability proof, W-9 Form) to MultifamilyEnergy.dhcd@maryland.gov. 2. Application is reviewed by a program team member for completeness and eligibility. 3. Once approved, project owner commissions a Qualified Energy Professional from DHCD's QEP List to complete an energy audit (for rehabilitation projects) or energy certification review (for new construction). Energy audit must comply with BPI Multifamily Building Analyst standards and include sampling of 10% of units minimum or 5 units minimum, whichever is greater. 4. Qualified Energy Professional completes energy audit, determines recommended Energy Conservation Measures (ECMs), obtains contractor bids, and submits Funding Request to DHCD on behalf of project owner through MINT or Rehab Funding Request Form. 5. DHCD reviews funding request and validates measure eligibility and funding amounts against established maximums. 6. DHCD creates a funding agreement and regulatory agreement (if affordability agreement does not exist). 7. After all parties sign the funding agreement, project is cleared to begin construction. 8. During construction, project submits requisitions with supporting documentation for work completed. 9. DHCD inspects a sample of installed measures to verify proper installation and processes payment within 4-5 weeks upon approval. 10. After construction completion, project enters affordability monitoring period where DHCD monitors compliance with affordability requirements for the duration of the affordability period (minimum 5-15 years depending on funding tier).
