structured_extraction.program_name: Multifamily Energy Efficiency and Housing Affordability Program (MEEHA) - Greenhouse Gas Reduction Program (GHGRP)
structured_extraction.program_description: MEEHA GHGRP provides grants to reduce direct greenhouse gas emissions in multifamily rental housing by replacing fossil fuel equipment with electric equipment and implementing building energy conservation and alternative energy generating systems.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: GHGRP provides grants only (no loans). Program allocation is $8.75 million in fiscal year 2024, and $5 million each in fiscal years 2025 and 2026. Projects can qualify for up to $15,000 per dwelling unit, with a project cap of $1.25 million. Funding covers: measures that enable direct greenhouse gas reductions, replacement of fossil fuel-fired equipment with electric equipment, energy efficiency and conservation improvements (excluding fossil fuel-fired equipment), incidental repairs to change fossil fuel infrastructure to electric infrastructure, alternative energy generating systems such as solar photovoltaics. Funds are provided during construction as work is completed and verified through a requisition process, with DHCD inspecting a sample of installed measures and processing payment within 4-5 weeks. Annual energy use benchmarking reports must be provided to DHCD for a minimum of two (2) years after construction completion.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of affordable multifamily rental housing developments with existing buildings of 35,000 gross square feet or more. Projects must house at least 51% of tenants at or below 80% Area Median Income (AMI).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduce direct greenhouse gas emissions through replacing fossil fuel equipment with electric equipment, building energy conservation measures, alternative energy generating systems (such as solar photovoltaics), incidental repairs to change fossil fuel infrastructure to electric infrastructure, and energy efficiency and conservation improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - all Maryland counties
requirements_list: Single building must have gross floor area of 35,000 sq ft or more (excluding parking garages), OR two or more buildings with combined gross floor area of 35,000 sq ft or more (excluding parking garage area) served by the same electric or gas meter or same heating/cooling system
A minimum of 51% of households must be at 80% Area Median Income (AMI) or less for a minimum of 15 years

Projects must have at least 15 years of affordability restrictions in place; if no initial regulatory agreement exists or current affordability restrictions have fewer than 15 years remaining, property must accept regulatory restrictions for at least 15 years
Minimum of 20% of units must be at or below 80% AMI (minimum 5 years for Tier 1 funding) or minimum of 51% of units at or below 80% AMI (minimum 15 years for Tier 2/GHGRP funding)
Project must demonstrate readiness to proceed
Project must show energy savings and reduction of greenhouse gases
Property owner must provide utility account information and authorize utility providers to release energy use data to DHCD
Applicant must have legal authority to sign application on behalf of property owner
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Set up an Energy Star Portfolio Manager account and generate a benchmarking report following MDE and/or EPA guidelines. 2. Submit completed MEEHA Application and supporting documents to MultifamilyEnergy.dhcd@maryland.gov, including Portfolio Manager baseline report, third party verification report (sample), commercial utility bills (electric and gas if applicable), customer consent form to obtain energy use information, grantee signature block, project deed with legal description, SDAT property ownership check, SDAT status check (owner), SDAT status check (grantee if different from owner), Minority Business Enterprise Plan Form, ACH Direct Deposit Form, proof of affordability (regulatory agreement or tax covenant), and W-9 Form for the grantee. 3. Application is reviewed by a program team member. 4. Once approved, project owner engages a Qualified Energy Professional from DHCD's QEP List to complete an energy audit (must comply with BPI Multifamily Building Analyst standards). 5. Qualified Energy Professional submits Energy Audit Report and Funding Request to DHCD on behalf of project owner, including greenhouse gas emissions reductions data using specified conversion factors and estimated costs. 6. DHCD reviews and creates a funding agreement. 7. After all parties sign the funding agreement, project is cleared to begin construction. 8. During construction, project submits requisitions with supporting documentation on a monthly basis; DHCD Project Manager conducts meetings and visual inspections monthly to track progress. 9. DHCD inspects a sample of installed measures and processes payment. 10. After construction completion, project enters affordability monitoring period where DHCD monitors compliance and project must provide annual energy use benchmarking reports for a minimum of two years.

structured_extraction.program_name: NBW Loan Participation Program (SSBCI Neighborhood BusinessWorks)
structured_extraction.program_description: A below-market-rate loan program designed to help small businesses acquire or renovate owner-occupied real estate, purchase machinery and equipment, or expand operations. The program provides loans up to $5 million with flexible terms for working capital and real estate needs. Funded through the State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI), the program prioritizes very small businesses and socially and economically disadvantaged individuals located in CDFI Investment Areas.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: SSBCI portion of loan ranges from $350,000 to $5,000,000. Senior or junior debt available. Up to 30 percent program match. Interest rate determined by underwriting analysis. Flexible loan terms up to 30 years depending on use and loan amount. Flexible applicant cash contribution required. Personal guarantees and collateral required. Prepayment lockout period may apply. Private capital match target of 4:1 (80-20) for non-SEDI or VSB, and 2.3:1 (70-30) for SEDI or VSB. Minimum required private capital match of 1:1.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses operating in Maryland with less than 500 employees. Priority given to very small businesses with fewer than 10 employees and SEDI (Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individuals) who own or operate for-profit or nonprofit Maryland-based small businesses. Local governments are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Owner-occupied real estate acquisition or renovation, mixed-use projects combining residential and commercial uses, machinery and equipment, working capital, and other costs associated with sustaining or expanding a small business. Manufacturing, service providers, retail, office, or mixed-use projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must be located or to be located in a CDFI Investment Area in Maryland.
requirements_list: Less than 500 employees
Proof of private capital match with target private capital to SSBCI funds match of 4:1 (80-20) for non-SEDI/VSB or 2.3:1 (70-30) for SEDI/VSB
Minimum required private capital to SSBCI funds match of 1:1
Business located or to be located in a CDFI Investment Area
Business viability and potential impact on the neighborhood
Readiness to proceed
Satisfactory cash flow and collateral
Priority given to very small businesses (fewer than 10 employees) and SEDI owned and operated businesses
For-profit or nonprofit; local governments not eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete an SSBCI Neighborhood BusinessWorks loan application package through the online portal at https://apps.dhcd.state.md.us/nbwapplication. Upon loan approval, applicant receives a commitment letter from the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. Loan approval requires applicants to meet underwriting guidelines. Applicants must execute necessary legal documents prior to loan disbursement. Application fee of $250 and closing fee of $250 apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: Exclusively designed for Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) to re-lend capital to small businesses, targeting socially and economically disadvantaged individual business owners, very small businesses, and businesses in CDFI Investment Areas. The program issues SSBCI loans to CDFIs to be matched with private capital and relent to small businesses throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: SSBCI Loans of $2,000,000 to $15,000,000 to CDFIs for relending to small businesses. SSBCI Loans bear interest at 0%-2% with terms up to 7 years and annual renewal options thereafter. CDFIs must leverage private capital match with a goal of 4:1 (80-20) for non-SEDI businesses and those with 10 or more employees, and a targeted private capital match to SSBCI funds ratio of 2.3:1 (70-30) for SEDI businesses or those with fewer than 10 employees. Each SBL to end-borrowers cannot exceed $250,000 unless prior written approval is granted. Interest rate to SBL Borrowers cannot exceed 18%. SBL terms cannot exceed 5 years unless for acquisition of assets with longer useful lives. CDFIs must have 20 percent at risk. Combined origination fee and points maximum 1%. Application fee maximum $100. No prepayment penalties allowed. Risk of loss is shared between DHCD and Lender on a loan-by-loan basis with SSBCI funds in top loss position.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing - Applications processed on first-come, first-served basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) only. Priority given to SEDI (socially and economically disadvantaged individual-led) businesses and very small businesses with fewer than 10 employees located in CDFI Investment Areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: CDFIs relend funds to small businesses for: working capital, marketing/planning/feasibility studies, real estate acquisition down payments, minor renovations, minor leasehold improvements, machinery and equipment acquisition, and other costs associated with opening or expanding a small business.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland with focus on CDFI investment areas. Priority given to businesses located or locating in CDFI Investment Areas.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Community Development Financial Institution certified and in good standing with the State and Internal Revenue Service
Must demonstrate financial stability and committed resources

Must have experience in administering small business loan programs including origination, credit and compliance underwriting, loan servicing, post-closing asset management and monitoring, and compliance with reporting requirements
Must demonstrate ability to leverage eligible required private capital as a match to SSBCI funding
Must demonstrate capacity to comply with SSBCI Statutes, Regulations and Policies and DHCD requirements
Must be ready to provide adequate resources and staff to start making SBLs within 90 days of closing the SSBCI Loan
Must have ability to provide technical assistance to SBL Borrowers
Must have outreach capabilities to very small businesses (less than 10 employees) and SEDI-led businesses or businesses in CDFI Investment Areas
Funds used for re-lending to small businesses only
Must maintain monthly, quarterly and annual reports reflecting SSBCI Loan balance, private match fund balance, SBLs, leveraged follow-on capital and other SSBCI related activity
Must provide post-closing access to records for DHCD asset management and federal auditors
Must not discriminate in origination, underwriting, servicing or administration based on race, color, religion, sex, handicap, familial status or national origin
Lender cannot act as participant, have security interest or be stakeholder in any SBL Borrowers

SBL Borrowers limited to small businesses (under 500 employees), retail businesses, manufacturing businesses, goods and services related businesses, home-based businesses, and non-profit organizations
Goal of 4:1 private capital match for non-SEDI businesses and those with 10 or more employees
Targeted private capital match to SSBCI funds ratio of 2.3:1 (70-30) for SEDI businesses or those with fewer than 10 employees
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: CDFIs submit the SSBCI NBW Loan to Lender Application form to DHCD. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis. The application requires documentation of organization capacity and experience, financial stability, lending program details including demographic, geographic and industry targets, outreach capabilities to very small businesses and SEDI-led businesses, loan product details, reporting capabilities, technical assistance provisions, and any outstanding liabilities. Required documentation includes most recent Annual Report, Annual Financial Statement, 501(c)(3) organizational documents, and last 3 years of organization tax returns. Once approved, Lender receives a commitment letter from DHCD reflecting total SSBCI Loan commitment amount, required private capital match, and proposed SBL funding timetable. SSBCI Loans must be closed in accordance with terms, conditions and documentation provided by Maryland Office of the Attorney General.

structured_extraction.program_description: An equity investment program dedicated to funding and supporting early-stage businesses in Maryland with high potential for job growth. The program provides bridge financing to help companies reach their next equity raise after they have already secured initial investment and demonstrated traction. Funded through the State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: SSBCI provides venture debt on at least a pari passu (equal priority) basis with private capital match. SSBCI funds must cause and result in the private capital match. Venture debt rates with repayment in principal and interest or convertible notes. Target SSBCI portion of venture debt ranges from $500,000 to $2,500,000. Aggregate funding round must be less than $20,000,000. Minimum required private capital match to SSBCI funds ratio of 1:1, with target matching private capital to SSBCI funds greater than 2:1. Typical bridge rounds exceed $2,000,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early-stage businesses in Maryland with high potential for job growth that have already raised equity from early-stage investors and are seeking additional investors. Most companies are positioned to scale and need bridge financing to achieve milestones. Typical bridge rounds exceed $2,000,000. Priority given to very small businesses with fewer than 10 employees and SEDI owned and operated businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bridge financing to help early-stage companies reach their next equity raise and scale operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Less than 500 employees
Minimum required private capital match to SSBCI funds ratio of 1:1
Target matching private capital to SSBCI funds greater than 2:1
Existing paid-in capital greater than $2,000,000 or revenues greater than $1,000,000
Already raised equity from early-stage investors
High potential for job growth
Priority given to very small businesses (fewer than 10 employees) and SEDI owned and operated businesses
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants should email dhcd.ssbci@maryland.gov to inquire about the program and application process.

structured_extraction.program_name: National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: Funding program that supports strategic economic development and revitalization projects in the National Capital region of Maryland, focusing on capital projects that drive economic growth and community improvement. The program provides competitive funding for strategic investment in local housing and businesses to encourage healthy, sustainable communities with a growing tax base and enhanced quality of life.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive funding for strategic investment in local housing and businesses. Award amounts vary; FY26 available funding is $8.6 million in capital and $200,000 in operating funds. Capital projects must have approximately 15-year shelf life. Operating costs support community revitalization activities. Beginning FY2026, a non-refundable Financial Assistance and Application Processing (FAAP) Fee of 4% of the awarded funds will be charged and included in the award project/program budget. The Department may also structure awards as loans or recoverable grants secured by Promissory Note and Deed of Trust, particularly for projects receiving $500,000 or more.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: July 2, 2025 at 3:00 PM (FY26 application round closed)
structured_extraction.contact_name: Jean Cannon, Program Officer (Region 6: Southern Maryland)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and nonprofit community development organizations in the National Capital region seeking funding for strategic economic development and housing projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects and limited operating costs that support community revitalization activities and the goals and objectives outlined in a target area's Sustainable Communities Action Plan. Eligible uses include property acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, architectural and engineering designs, site development, public infrastructure improvements, and community revitalization activities. Funds support local housing and business development to create healthy, sustainable communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Sustainable Communities in the National Capital region of Maryland, specifically: (1) In Prince George's County, at least in part, within the boundary created by Interstate 495 in the State and the District of Columbia; OR (2) In Montgomery County, within an Enterprise Zone or the boundary created by Prince George's County, Maryland Route 200, Interstate 270, Interstate 495 to the Maryland state line, and the District of Columbia. Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to verify project eligibility.
requirements_list: Project must be located in a Sustainable Community within the National Capital region as defined
Capital project with at least 15-year shelf life
Must support economic development and revitalization goals outlined in local Sustainable Communities Action Plan
Applicant must be eligible organization type: local government or nonprofit community development organization
Current awardees must be in compliance with terms and conditions of current award agreements and in good standing
New user account requests must be submitted by June 11 (two weeks before application deadline)
Site control documentation required
Evidence of committed financial resources and private-sector leverage
Project readiness to proceed must be demonstrated
Proposed budget must be specific regarding expenditures
50% of awarded funds must be drawn down by the first anniversary date of the award
Proposed timeline for 2-year award term must be provided
Organizations must provide race/ethnicity demographic information for Board of Directors and Senior Staff
All required legal exhibits and supporting documents must be submitted by application deadline
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Register as a new user in the Project Portal (new user deadline is June 11; approval may take up to 72 hours). Identify organization, project location, and interested funding program. Contact your regional project manager (Jean Cannon for Southern Maryland region at 410-209-5806 or jean.cannon@maryland.gov) to verify eligibility and authorize access. 2. Upload required organizational documents to your profile (see legal exhibits and supporting documents requirements). 3. Complete application in Project Portal including project information, proposed budget, timeline, readiness assessment, and project impact data sheet. Answer at least one question on the FY26 Project Impact Data Sheet to quantify results. 4. Submit all required attachments including evidence of site control, funding commitments, cost estimates, photographs, and Sustainable Communities map verification. 5. Submit complete application through Project Portal by July 2, 2025 at 3:00 PM. Applications received after deadline will not be considered. FY26 application period opened May 28, 2025 and closed July 2, 2025. Review Period: Summer 2025. Award Recommendations: Fall 2025. Award Announcements: Fall/Winter 2025. Award Agreement Drafting and Execution: Winter 2025. Active Award Management: 2-Year Award Term.

structured_extraction.program_description: The National Housing Trust Fund is an affordable housing production program that increases and preserves the supply of decent, safe, and sanitary affordable housing for extremely low-income and very low-income households.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HTF funds may be used as broadly and flexibly as permitted by federal regulations to address the unique underwriting needs of each project. Forms of assistance include equity investments, interest-bearing loans or advances, non-interest-bearing loans or advances, deferred payment loans, grants, and other forms of assistance approved by HUD. Ninety percent (90%) of the HTF annual allocation is used for production, preservation and rehabilitation of affordable rental housing through acquisition, new construction, reconstruction, or rehabilitation of non-luxury housing with suitable amenities. The Department retains ten percent (10%) of the HTF annual allocation for allowable administrative and planning expenses. Operating cost assistance may be provided but no more than one-third of the state's annual HTF allocation and must be fully utilized within 5 years of award. Projects funded through a non-competitive, first-ready first-served basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Extremely low-income (ELI) households with incomes at or below 30% Area Median Income (AMI) or at or below the poverty line, and very low-income (VLI) households, including homeless families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development hard costs, acquisition costs, related soft costs, relocation costs, and operating cost assistance for production, preservation, and rehabilitation of affordable rental housing through acquisition, new construction, reconstruction, or rehabilitation of non-luxury housing with suitable amenities. Projects must serve extremely low-income households and maintain a minimum 30-year affordability period for rental housing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. For new construction projects, sites must be located in Priority Funding Areas (PFAs) under Maryland's Smart Green and Growing Initiative, including incorporated municipalities, areas between Baltimore beltway and City limits and Washington DC beltway and boundary, Sustainable Communities, enterprise zones, county-designated PFAs, and certified heritage areas within locally designated growth areas.
requirements_list: Market assessment demonstrating current demand for housing units being developed
Site control extending at least 180 calendar days after application date
Capital Needs Assessment for acquisition/rehabilitation projects documenting remaining useful life of all major systems
Phase I Environmental Site Assessment (ASTM standard) for multifamily projects; single family housing does not require Phase I ESA
Evidence that public water, sewer, electric, gas, telephone, internet, and cable services are available at project sites
Proper zoning for intended use; documentation of zoning change status if required
Letter from local government certifying new construction projects are located in Priority Funding Area
Anticipated Development Schedule demonstrating readiness to proceed
Minimum 5% vacancy rate underwriting; Department reserves right to reject projects requiring 10% or more vacancy
Annual operating expenses between $4,000-$7,000 per unit per year (waivers available for small projects up to 40 units, master-metered utilities, or unusual circumstances)
Minimum $300 per unit per year in reserves for replacement deposits
Operating reserves equal to 3-6 months of underwritten operating expenses, debt service, and reserve deposits
Rents projected to increase no more than 2% annually; operating expenses projected to increase at least 3% annually
Minimum debt service coverage ratio of 1.15 in first year of stabilized operations
Market Study prepared by independent professional experienced with affordable multifamily housing in Maryland; not more than 6 months old
Developer with demonstrated relevant experience and qualifications; record of accomplishment during past 5 years with similar projects
Financial statements for 3 fiscal years prior to application plus interim statements through previous quarter for sponsor, owner, guarantor, and general partner/managing member
Compliance with 24 CFR Part 93 and HUD Housing Trust Fund Interim Rule requirements
Historic preservation compliance: activities must meet Secretary of Interior Standards if on National Register or eligible properties
Farmland: project activities must not convert unique, prime, or statewide/locally significant agricultural properties
Airport zones: projects not permitted in runway protection zones or military airfield clear/accident zones
Coastal Barrier Resource System: no projects in CBRS units
Coastal zone management: development must be consistent with State coastal zone management plan
Floodplains: avoid 100-year floodplain construction when practicable; if necessary, elevate to base flood elevation or floodproof to 1 foot above BFE
Wetlands: no draining, dredging, channelizing, filling, diking, impounding or related activities; no adverse impacts to wetlands
Contamination: all properties free of hazardous materials, toxic chemicals, gases, and radioactive substances
Noise: internal noise levels no more than 45 decibels; external levels 65 dB or less acceptable; 65-75 dB acceptable with mitigation; 75 dB or greater require sound attenuation
Endangered species: avoid actions that jeopardize continued existence of designated species
Wild and scenic rivers: avoid inconsistent activities
Safe drinking water: lead-free pipes, solder, and flux required
Sole source aquifers: avoid sites and activities with contamination potential
Archaeological resources: consult with affected tribes/descendant communities if discovered; comply with Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act
Explosives and hazards: compliance with 24 CFR Part 51, Subpart C separation distance standards
For-profit or non-profit organizations with demonstrated financial capacity and experience
Capacity to own, construct, rehabilitate, manage and operate affordable multifamily rental housing
Familiarity with federal, state, and local housing program requirements
Certification of compliance with HTF program requirements for entire project period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: HTF projects are selected by the Department for funding consideration subject to availability of funds. Applications are reviewed for eligibility and evaluated using Threshold Criteria. HTF funds are awarded to eligible projects through a non-competitive, first-ready first-served basis. HTF funds may be requested by a Sponsor as part of a project application or Department staff may, in consultation with a sponsor, propose use of HTF funds during project review and underwriting. HTF funds are used to complement and work in conjunction with ongoing Department housing programs to leverage other project funding, make projects financially feasible, and increase the number of ELI households served in state-funded projects. HTF funds may be used with projects utilizing RHFP, LIHTC, MBP, STHGP, and other Department programs, or with non-Department housing program funds from state, federal, local/public, or private sources. HTF may not be used with funding sources that cannot be combined with HTF (e.g., Public Housing per 24 CFR §93.203). Successful recipients receive a Notice of Award stating Department's intent to award HTF funds. The Department requires all applications contain a description of eligible activities to be conducted with HTF funds. Projects must comply with Site and Neighborhood Standards at 24 CFR §93.150 for new construction. All rehabilitation projects must meet applicable HTF rehabilitation standards and 24 CFR §93.301(b) requirements. The HTF program requires the Department to commit funds within 24 months of HUD's execution of the HTF grant Agreement.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Department's Community Development Administration issues bonds to fund loans for business projects through the Neighborhood Business Works (NBW) program. A business project qualifies if it is located in a priority funding area or Sustainable Communities and is acquired, owned, developed, constructed, reconstructed, rehabilitated or improved for the purposes of carrying on a business, whether or not for profit. The program has been financing small businesses in Maryland for over 20 years and currently manages a portfolio of 158 loans with an aggregate outstanding principal balance in excess of $20 million.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Bonds are issued to fund senior and subordinate loans, or a combination of both, for business projects including: (1) Construction and permanent financing for commercial and mixed-use projects; (2) Acquisition or refinance of stabilized commercial and mixed-use projects; (3) Non-profit facility loans for acquisition, rehabilitation and new construction of facilities for occupancy and/or use by qualified 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations. For-profit borrowers must contribute minimum 10% equity; non-profit borrowers minimum 5% equity. Maximum loan-to-value (CLTV) financing is 90% for for-profit borrowers and 95% for non-profit borrowers (with CDA-MHF top loss coverage up to 30%), or maximum 100% CLTV with senior loan up to 70% LTV and subordinate loan from State-appropriated capital. All loans require minimum 1.50 debt service coverage ratio (DSCR) throughout loan life. Upfront financing fees range from 0.5% to 1%, plus $25,000 for DHCD legal counsel and normal real estate and loan closing fees.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and non-profit businesses seeking financing for projects in priority funding areas and Sustainable Communities. Includes small businesses, developers, and qualified 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, permanent financing, construction financing, refinancing and rehabilitation of commercial and mixed-use real estate; non-profit facility acquisition, rehabilitation and new construction. Projects must demonstrate revitalization impact on the community including elimination of blight, catalytic redevelopment stimulus, and job retention or creation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Priority Funding Areas as defined in Section 5-7B-02 of the State Finance and Procurement Article or in Sustainable Communities as defined in Section 6-205 of DHCD's Article, per Title 5, Subtitle 13 of the Economic Development Article, or per Section 7-101 of the Transportation Article. All Maryland counties are eligible.
requirements_list: Project must be located in a Priority Funding Area or Sustainable Communities
Project must be acquired, owned, developed, constructed, reconstructed, rehabilitated or improved for carrying on a business
For non-profit facilities, must be for occupancy and/or use by qualified 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations
For-profit borrowers: minimum 10% equity or total cost contribution; non-profit borrowers: minimum 5% equity or total cost contribution
Loan-to-value (CLTV) financing: maximum 90% for for-profit (with CDA-MHF top loss coverage up to 30%) or 95% for non-profit borrowers
Debt service reserve equal to 6 months of maximum annual debt service required
Minimum pro-forma 1.50 DSCR throughout life of loan (1.25 DSCR minimum for non-CDA loans with MHF credit enhancement unless underwriter determines otherwise)
Industry-standard underwriting criteria including credit worthiness of borrower, market position, adequacy of collateral, and soundness of business plan and management team
Collateral must be valued by qualified professional appraiser acceptable to CDA, MHF and debt investors
All projects evaluated based on revitalization impact including elimination of blight, catalytic redevelopment stimulus, and job retention or creation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit an online application to the Community Development Administration. All CDA business loan underwriting is reviewed and recommended for approval by the 7-member Housing Finance Review Committee (HFRC) comprised of three DHCD employees (including Deputy Secretary as Chairman), one executive branch employee outside DHCD, and three public members with expertise in investment/commercial banking, lending, real estate development, mortgage insurance, community development, or affordable housing. All loans over $250,000 are also reviewed by the 5-member NBW Loan Review Committee. CDA business lending underwriters perform loan underwriting using industry-standard criteria including analysis of credit worthiness, market position, collateral adequacy, and business plan soundness. Construction projects receive engineering staff review of architectural and engineering plans, field monitoring, and assurance procedures. Asset management and compliance monitoring occurs quarterly for interim financial information and annually for audited information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program offering flexible financing to help new or expanding small businesses and nonprofit organizations in designated neighborhood revitalization areas, including existing commercial districts and town centers. These loans typically serve as first money in or gap financing to ensure that small businesses with capital needs access the funds to bring their visions to life. The program works with banks, community development financial institutions (CDFIs), and mixed-use developers to help entrepreneurs turn business plans into operating businesses.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_prioritized_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans up to $5 million with interest rates determined by underwriting analysis and market conditions. Flexible loan terms up to 30 years depending on loan size and underwriting. Applicants must contribute a minimum of 10 percent cash based on total project cost. Personal guarantees and collateral are required. Program fees include: $250 application fee, $250 closing fee, and 1% origination fee.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Program operates on a first-come, first-serve basis. Applications currently exceed available funds until July 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based small businesses with 500 or fewer employees and nonprofit organizations whose projects promote investment and contribute to broader community revitalization efforts seeking to start or expand commercial operations in designated neighborhood revitalization areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Real estate acquisition, construction, or rehabilitation; leasehold improvements; machinery and equipment purchases; working capital (as part of total project costs); market, planning, or feasibility studies; other costs associated with opening or expanding a small business. Note: Construction projects are reviewed by the Maryland Historical Trust and Codes Administration prior to funding.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within Sustainable Communities, Priority Funding Areas, Opportunity Zones in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, or Wicomico counties, Transit-Oriented Development areas designated by the Maryland Department of Transportation, or BRAC Revitalization and Incentive Zones.
requirements_list: Borrower must be a Maryland-based small business with 500 or fewer employees or a nonprofit organization

Project must be located in a targeted geography (Sustainable Community, Priority Funding Area, Opportunity Zone in specific counties, Transit-Oriented Development area, or BRAC Revitalization and Incentive Zone)
Project must demonstrate viability and positive impact on neighborhood
Appropriate debt service levels
Sufficient collateral
Personal guarantee required
Positive net operating income (NOI)
Strong business plan
10 percent applicant cash contribution required (based on total project cost)

Ineligible projects include: residential or speculative developments (except mixed-use projects with qualifying commercial components), facilities such as community halls, fire stations, hospitals, colleges or universities, adult entertainment facilities, gambling facilities, check cashing facilities, gun shops or liquor stores, massage parlors, pawn shops, tanning salons, tattoo parlors, or cannabis businesses
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete a full NBW loan application with all items listed in the application checklist. Submit the application to the Business Lending Team via the online portal following a pre-application consultation. The team will review your application and conduct underwriting analysis. If the application is approved, additional documentation will be required to finalize and close the loan.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding to local jurisdictions and their ISP partners to extend existing broadband service to unserved areas. The program is administered through the Office of Statewide Broadband and was funded through the American Rescue Plan Act. Program is currently closed and not accepting applications.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants between $50,000 and $500,000 covering 70-90% of capital construction costs with 10-30% match required based on project density. Match percentage is determined by the average number of households per mile for wired projects (fewer than 8 households per mile requires 10% match, 8-14 households per mile requires 20% match, 15+ households per mile requires 30% match) or average households per tower for wireless projects (fewer than 40 households per tower requires 10% match, 40-69 households per tower requires 20% match, 70+ households per tower requires 30% match). Matching funds may come from the local jurisdiction and/or ISP partner and can include cash contributions or, for ISPs, in-kind capital construction costs. Program is currently closed and not accepting new applications.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: December 23, 2021 (Program closed - not accepting applications)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions (counties or municipalities) and their Internet Service Provider partners seeking to expand broadband service to unserved residents and businesses
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs to extend existing broadband service to unserved areas, including: construction of facilities to deploy broadband service at required speeds to all end users within the project area; middle mile infrastructure directly necessary to provide service to end users including interconnections between non-contiguous service areas; electronics necessary to deliver service including optical line terminals, optical network terminals, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radio equipment, antennae, access points, modems, and necessary equipment shelters. Grant funds may not be used for engineering design services (except as allowed in match), land or tower purchases, building construction or renovation (except as allowed in match), operating expenses, or duplication of existing broadband service.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland, excluding areas that have received prior state grant funding. Project areas must be unserved, defined as lacking terrestrial, fixed internet service at speeds above 25 Megabits per second (Mbps) download and/or 3 Mbps upload and/or with latency above 50 milliseconds.
requirements_list: Local jurisdiction must be the applicant and fiscal agent with an Internet Service Provider partner
Projects must serve unserved areas lacking terrestrial fixed internet service at speeds above 25 Mbps download and/or 3 Mbps upload and/or with latency above 50 milliseconds

Minimum network requirements: 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload speeds with maximum latency of 50 milliseconds at served subscriber locations (exceptions allowed with ISP certification for geographic, topographic, or cost reasons, with scalability requirement to 100 Mbps symmetrical)
70-90% grant coverage with 10-30% match required based on project density
Match must be from identified sources committed by local jurisdiction and/or ISP partner
All equipment must be new and non-depreciated
Applicant must have strong incumbent ISP partner with means and desire to provide service
Project area must be identified with graphical maps showing properties to be served and infrastructure to be constructed
GIS shapefiles, KMZ, or KML files required showing project area and infrastructure
Detailed line-item capital construction budget required with quantity and cost breakdown
Projects must be completed by December 31, 2023
Local jurisdiction must enter into partnership agreement with ISP partner prior to funding agreement with Department
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the Grant Application Form for the Neighborhood Connect Broadband Project. 2. Prepare Executive Summary describing the unserved area, how it was chosen, problems residents face, and how the project will alleviate those problems and provide enhanced opportunities. 3. Identify the ISP Partner and describe assistance or cooperation the local jurisdiction will offer. 4. Provide statement of experience of senior team from both applicant and ISP partner. 5. Submit detailed Network Design and Construction description including network speed, latency, backhaul methods, pole-attached vs. underground infrastructure for wired networks or tower information for wireless networks, and final facility ownership details. Include GIS files showing project area and infrastructure. 6. Provide Subscriber Profile with demographic data, projected subscriber take rate, and estimate of unserved households and businesses. 7. Submit Subscriber Costs and Limitations listing ISP partner service options, costs, and any limitations including data caps. 8. Provide detailed line-item Capital Construction Budget using the provided form showing all major construction work, equipment, and costs. 9. Submit Project Schedule with proposed timeline assuming Summer 2022 start, key milestones, and description of subscriber connection approach. 10. Submit one electronic PDF copy of complete Response to osb.md@maryland.gov with 'Neighborhood Connect', local jurisdiction name, and Project Name in subject line on or before December 23, 2021. 11. Include with submission: budget as both PDF and Excel spreadsheet; GIS shape/KMZ/KML file delineating served properties named to identify PFSA; separate GIS file or layer showing broadband infrastructure (line or tower locations); all items combined in single ZIP file with clearly identified filenames. 12. Identify any proprietary or confidential information in Response. 13. Applications evaluated on 25-point scoring system based on: Need for Service and Project Benefits (up to 5 points), Match Contribution Source (up to 6 points), Network Delivery Speed (up to 10 points), and Subscriber Options (up to 4 points). 14. Awards facilitated beginning April 2022 on high-to-low score basis as funding permits.

structured_extraction.program_description: Matching grants support the operating costs of certified Neighborhood Housing Services corporations that work with residents, financial institutions, community organizations, local governments, and the State to stabilize and improve the housing market in targeted low- and moderate-income neighborhoods. These organizations provide homeownership opportunities, home rehabilitation, homebuyer education and counseling, and community-organizing activities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each eligible Neighborhood Housing Services corporation may apply for a matching grant up to $50,000 that does not exceed one-third of its annual operating budget. Umbrella corporations may apply for a grant for each program under their supervision up to $50,000 that does not exceed one-third of the annual operating budget of that program. The state grant must be matched by funds from local governments, private businesses, and individual contributions.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible applicants are Neighborhood Housing Services (NHS) corporations certified by the Neighborhood Reinvestment Corporation, serving low- and moderate-income households in targeted neighborhoods.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating costs of Neighborhood Housing Services corporations that provide homeownership opportunities, closing cost assistance, homebuyer education and counseling, home rehabilitation for ownership and rental, and community-organizing activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in neighborhoods served by certified Neighborhood Housing Services corporations including Baltimore City, Baltimore County, and West Side, Church Street, and Camden neighborhoods in Salisbury, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a Neighborhood Housing Services corporation approved and certified by the Neighborhood Reinvestment Corporation
Local political subdivision must agree to financially support the local Neighborhood Housing Services corporation
Local political subdivision must participate on the corporation's board of directors
Grant amount cannot exceed $50,000
Grant amount cannot exceed one-third of annual operating budget
The state grant must be matched by funds from local governments, private businesses, and individual contributions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Poverty Solutions Team in the Division of Neighborhood Revitalization for information about the application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: A strategic and targeted investment designed to expand access to healthy and fresh foods in Maryland communities experiencing food insecurity by providing direct grants to eligible food retailers, supporting the development, stabilization, and expansion of retail outlets in areas where residents have limited or no access to nutritious food options.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_prioritized_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $25,000 to $150,000, with up to $2 million total funding available. Applicants may also request supplemental loan funding through DHCD's Neighborhood BusinessWorks (NBW) program, which will undergo financial review to assess debt management capacity. Funds can be used for equipment purchases (refrigeration, shelving, etc.), renovation and build-out, facility upgrades, capital costs for inventory expansion, working capital tied to expansion or construction, and infrastructure and technology for SNAP/EBT. A $250 processing fee is required for all applications and may be paid directly from awarded grant funds. No application fee. Recipients may also be eligible for co-awards through the Maryland Market Money (MMM) program administered by the Maryland Department of Agriculture.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: February 20, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit or nonprofit food retailers serving communities with high fresh food gaps and committed to expanding access to healthy foods. Eligible food retailers include grocery stores, corner stores, farm stands, farmers' markets, food co-ops, delivery retailers, and small retail stores where the majority of inventory or sales are food-related.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of furniture, fixtures, and/or equipment (e.g., refrigeration, shelving); renovation and build-out; facility upgrades; capital needs related to inventory expansion (non-prepared foods); working capital involved with expansion or renovations/construction; and infrastructure/technology for SNAP/EBT setup. Funds must be used solely for improving or providing healthy food access.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Eligible retailers must serve a community with a Maryland Community Business Compass (MCBC) Fresh Food Gap Score of 60% or higher. Exceptions may be granted on an individual basis. Note: Your business does not need to be listed on the Maryland Community Business Compass to be eligible for the NourishMD grant program. However, if you don't see your business on the Maryland Community Business Compass and would like to add it, please email compass@maryland.gov.
requirements_list: Must be a for-profit or nonprofit food retailer
Must serve a community with a Maryland Community Business Compass (MCBC) Fresh Food Gap Score of 60% or higher
Must operate at least 5 days per week, year round (farmer's markets and on-farm markets exempt from 5-day requirement but must operate year round)
Must employ a maximum of 500 workers
Must be registered and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Must currently offer or plan to offer fresh, frozen, or minimally processed healthy foods including fresh/frozen/preserved produce, whole grains, dairy products, and fresh meats/proteins
Must dedicate at least 20% of inventory or food-sales space to healthy food items, documented through square footage of food display space or dollar value of inventory
Must submit detailed written plan describing use of grant funds (not to exceed 2 pages)
Must provide information demonstrating how business meets healthy and fresh food criteria
Must provide one year of business tax returns, audited financial statements, or alternative documentation sufficient to demonstrate financial viability if operating less than one year
If relocation or expansion is involved, must provide supporting documentation such as lease agreement, letter of intent, or proof of site control
A $250 processing fee is required and may be sourced from the award amount
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can schedule an initial consultation and submit complete applications through the online portal. The application portal opens January 20, 2026 at 12:00 p.m. EST and closes February 20, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. EST. All applications must include required documentation (use of funds plan, healthy food criteria information, financial documentation, and relocation/expansion documentation if applicable) to be eligible for review. DHCD staff evaluate eligible applications for completeness, impact, and alignment with program priorities from February-March 2026. The Review Committee (consisting of DHCD Division of Business Development leadership, Maryland Department of Agriculture, Maryland Department of Health, and DHCD Division of Neighborhood Revitalization representatives) makes funding determinations. Funding recommendations are finalized in April 2026. Award notifications and agreement processing occur in May 2026, followed by Board of Public Works approval and disbursements in June 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Operating Assistance Grants - Technical Assistance Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to nonprofit organizations and local governments to help cover operating costs associated with community revitalization and economic development efforts, including housing and community development activities. Projects should align with local Sustainable Community Action Plans or support activities related to capital projects receiving funds from other Department or State agencies.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants provide funding for operating costs related to administering community revitalization efforts, including salaries, professional services contracts, technology costs, and other related administrative expenses. The maximum grant amount is $50,000 per award. No matching funds are required. All projects or activities should be completed within one year. Capital project costs are not eligible, nor are alcohol, legal controlled substances, entertainment, personal souvenirs, excursions, toiletries, fines, parking tickets, or travel costs for companions not on the team. An initial advance of up to 25% of the total award amount is permitted for the first payment request with no supporting documentation required; evidence of how the advanced funds were spent must be submitted with the next request for payment. Subsequent payment requests must include paid invoices, contracts, receipts, ledgers, and other documentation substantiating reimbursement. A minimum request for reimbursement is $1,000. The grant term is one year from the date the award agreement is signed by DHCD.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, March 20, 2026 at 5:00 PM (EDT)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations and local governments in Maryland engaged in community and economic revitalization activities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating costs related to administering community revitalization efforts, including salaries, professional services contracts, technology costs, and other related administrative expenses. Eligible activities include staff and consultant services, general operating expenses, and other costs related to administering community revitalization programs. Capital project costs are not supported. Funds cannot be used for alcohol, legal controlled substances, entertainment, personal souvenirs, excursions, toiletries, fines, parking tickets, or travel costs for companions not on the team.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Priority Funding Areas (PFAs). Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper tool to verify if an organization or project/program is in a PFA. Additional consideration is given to projects in designated ENOUGH (Engaging Neighborhoods, Organizations, Unions, Governments and Households) areas, which represent rural, suburban and urban communities that have been historically impacted by barriers to economic mobility, and Just Communities, where all Marylanders, regardless of background, have access to fair housing and economic stability and opportunity.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit organization or local government
Project must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area (PFA)
Project should align with local Sustainable Community Action Plans or support activities related to capital projects receiving funds from other Department or State agencies
Maximum grant request is $50,000
All projects or activities should be completed within one year
Applicants must register in the Project Portal before submitting an application
Organization profile must include all required documents before submitting application

Nonprofit applicants must provide evidence of nonprofit status (Bylaws, Articles of Incorporation, IRS Determination Letter), evidence of good standing from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation, and evidence of charitable registration from Maryland Secretary of State

Current Operating Assistance Grant Program awardees must be in full compliance with all existing award agreements, including meeting all reporting deadlines and submitting all required final reports and payment requests from prior awards
Projects should be completed within one year from the grant agreement execution date
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, organizations must first register in the DHCD Project Portal by selecting 'New User?' and completing the registration request form. Registration approval may take up to 72 hours. Once approved, access the application through the Project Portal. The application portal opens February 20, 2026 at 8:00 AM and closes March 20, 2026 at 5:00 PM. Late applications will not be accepted. Applicants should request portal access and submit organizational documents at least two weeks before the application deadline to expedite processing. First-time applicants must contact a project manager for eligibility verification and system access. Make sure your organization profile includes all required documents (for nonprofits: evidence of nonprofit status, good standing, and charitable registration) before submitting, as applications missing documents may be disqualified. Virtual training sessions and a step-by-step application guide are available in the DHCD Project Portal. Applications will be evaluated using a 5-point scoring scale reflecting the overall strength and readiness of the application. Projects in ENOUGH areas may receive up to 10 bonus points, and projects in Just Communities areas will receive 10 bonus points. Review teams may conduct site visits and/or meetings with applicants.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that enables businesses to access additional capital and receive federal tax incentives when starting or expanding in designated Opportunity Zone areas.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal tax incentives for businesses starting or expanding in designated Opportunity Zone areas, with access to additional capital.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses starting or expanding in Maryland Opportunity Zones.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business startup or expansion activities in Opportunity Zone areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Designated Opportunity Zone areas in Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides financial assistance to help small businesses buy property they can operate in and use to build wealth. The program funds property acquisition and renovation for small business owners. Funding is provided through the federal State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) program.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $500,000 to $5 million with flexible terms designed to maximize community benefit. Borrowers must provide a minimum 1:1 private capital match. Loan terms include up to 30 years, senior or subordinate loan positions available, and interest rates determined by underwriting analysis. Borrowers must provide personal guarantees from all owners with more than 20% equity and adequate collateral. Total project costs cannot exceed $20 million.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses with fewer than 500 employees that want to purchase or renovate commercial real estate.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase, construct, or renovate commercial real estate. Eligible uses include buying the space where you currently operate, moving to a new location, buying property for the first time, or buying property as part of a company expansion. Renovation projects must be at least 51% owner-occupied upon completion. New construction must be at least 60% owner-occupied upon completion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide.
requirements_list: Business must have fewer than 500 employees
Project cannot be 100% residential (mixed-use projects may qualify)
Must provide minimum 1:1 private capital match
Loan amount must be between $500,000 and $5 million
Personal guarantees required from all owners with more than 20% equity
Must provide adequate collateral
Total project costs cannot exceed $20 million
Business cannot be an adult entertainment facility, check cashing facility, gambling facility, gun shop, liquor store, massage parlor, pawn shop, tanning salon, tattoo parlor, or cannabis business
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online using the application portal at https://apps.dhcd.state.md.us/nbwapplication. Schedule a consultation for more information by visiting dhcd.maryland.gov/Business/Pages/Own-Your-Future.aspx or emailing dhcd.businesslending@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides targeted financing for affordable rental housing development and preservation in partnership with various entities. The housing is for households that earn less than half of the statewide median income.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Targeted financing through direct loans for the development and preservation of partnership-based affordable rental housing projects.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted through competitions or throughout the year based on readiness to proceed
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and non-profit rental housing developers, county governments, municipalities, and sponsors of affordable rental housing developments.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development and preservation of affordable rental housing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in priority funding areas in Maryland.
requirements_list: Rental units must be occupied by households with incomes below 50% of the statewide median.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications accepted through competitions or throughout the year based on readiness to proceed. Applicants can find application documents in the agency's Multifamily Document Library. Contact the program representative for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Project C.O.R.E. (Creating Opportunities for Revitalization and Equity)
structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership between the Governor, Baltimore City, the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, and the Maryland Stadium Authority designed to demolish vacant buildings and catalyze redevelopment, reinvestment, and stabilization in Baltimore City neighborhoods. The initiative aims to improve economic opportunity and quality of life by creating safer neighborhoods, more jobs, more green space, and quality energy-efficient affordable housing. It provided funding to Baltimore City to demolish vacant properties, clearing the way for new green space and new affordable and mixed-use housing, creating safer, healthier and more attractive spaces for families.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Project C.O.R.E. provides funding and support for demolition, deconstruction, stabilization, and redevelopment activities in Baltimore City. The initiative supports workforce development training programs and partners with local trade organizations, non-profit organizations, and other state agencies to provide job-seeking residents with employment opportunities linked to demolition, deconstruction, stabilization, and redevelopment activities. The program results in creation of affordable single-family and multifamily housing, green space, and commercial development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents, small businesses, job-seeking residents, non-profit organizations, and other community stakeholders in Baltimore City neighborhoods eligible for demolition and redevelopment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support demolition of vacant buildings, deconstruction, stabilization of properties, redevelopment activities, construction of affordable housing, creation of green space, commercial development, workforce training, and job creation activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Project C.O.R.E. focuses exclusively on Baltimore City. The initiative specifically serves Baltimore City neighborhoods identified for demolition through community engagement processes.
requirements_list: Affected residents must comply with the federal Uniform Relocation Assistance and Real Property Acquisition Policies Act of 1970 if relocation is necessary
Community input required for site selection
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents and organizations can participate by checking information posted to the Project C.O.R.E. web pages on the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development website. Baltimore City engages affected communities regularly through its Vacants to Value (V2V) program. The schedule of demolitions is determined after substantial community input. Details on how to apply for specific opportunities under Project C.O.R.E. are posted on the project website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Project C.O.R.E. Phase I – Demolition Of Blighted Properties
structured_extraction.program_description: The state invests funding to demolish blighted properties and city blocks in Baltimore City. After demolition or stabilization, sites are graded, seeded, and fenced for future redevelopment. Phase I includes demolition projects and redevelopment initiatives across multiple neighborhoods in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The state invests $75 million over four years, with $18.5 million matching investment from Baltimore City, to demolish blighted properties and support redevelopment. FY17 Phase I awards totaled $15,860,000 distributed across 31 projects with individual award amounts ranging from $120,000 to $2,000,000. Baltimore City provides in-kind services valued at $0.25 for every $1 in state allocations. The Maryland Stadium Authority manages projects and handles site preparation including grading, seeding, and fencing. Eligible uses include demolition, stabilization, site preparation, and redevelopment of blighted residential and commercial properties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City agencies and nonprofit community development organizations working on property demolition and neighborhood revitalization
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Demolition of blighted properties, stabilization of historic structures, grading, seeding, and fencing of sites, and redevelopment projects including housing, retail, and community facilities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City, with recommended demolition locations identified in Phase I clusters based on blight density mapping
requirements_list: Property must be identified as blighted by Baltimore City Department of Housing
Property must be reviewed and approved by Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
Applicants must be Baltimore City agencies or nonprofit community development organizations
Projects must align with Phase I cluster priority areas
Applicants must demonstrate capacity to manage projects and secure matching funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Baltimore City Department of Housing identifies potential properties for demolition and redevelopment based on blight density analysis. These properties and project proposals are reviewed with the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development for final approval. The Maryland Stadium Authority serves as project manager. Awards are recommended through a competitive or prioritized selection process based on project readiness, alignment with Phase I priorities, and community impact.

structured_extraction.program_name: Project C.O.R.E. Phase II – Revitalization Through Redevelopment
structured_extraction.program_description: The state leverages funding through Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development programs to encourage new investment and redevelopment in blighted communities that have undergone demolition.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The state leverages an estimated $600 million through Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development programs to encourage new investment in communities that have completed Phase I demolition activities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public, private, and nonprofit development partners seeking to invest in Baltimore City redevelopment
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New investment and redevelopment in blighted communities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
requirements_list: Property must be located in an area that has completed Phase I demolition
Applicant must be a public, private, or nonprofit development partner
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants work with the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development to access various department programs for redevelopment funding and support.

structured_extraction.program_description: A financial assistance program that activates vacant buildings, supports small businesses, creates jobs, improves commercial corridors, and increases local economic activity by providing grants to place-based economic development organizations working to revitalize Maryland's commercial corridors.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants provided to place-based economic development organizations (nonprofits and local government entities) to activate vacant buildings, support small businesses, create jobs, and improve commercial corridors. For FY2024, $8.0 million is available to be awarded. Grant funds can be used for rent, interior/exterior renovation, furniture, fixtures, and equipment for small businesses occupying vacant commercial spaces. Place-based organizations can request up to 15% of the grant for operating costs (staff, professional services, marketing). Grants are disbursed when the Request for Payment/Progress Report is approved, which occurs before construction/purchasing begins. All grant funds must be expended and businesses must be operational by December 31, 2025. Operating funds are direct deposited if requested after the award agreement is executed. No match is required.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application currently closed; applications for FY2024 closed April 24, 2024 at 5pm EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: Place-based economic development organizations, including nonprofit organizations with missions focused on economic and community development in a district (such as Main Street Maryland programs or economic development associations) and local government entities (towns, cities, or counties). Small businesses are not eligible to apply directly but receive support as sub-grantees through awarded organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grants fund activation of vacant commercial buildings in designated Sustainable Communities. Eligible uses include: rent payments, interior and exterior renovation, furniture, fixtures, and equipment for small businesses occupying formerly vacant spaces. Up to 15% of grant funds can support operating costs for the place-based organization, including staff costs, professional services (e.g., architecture, legal), and marketing/promotion directly related to Project Restore 2.0. Funds cannot be used for: acquisition/building purchase, new construction, reimbursement for costs incurred prior to award, vehicles, or water/sewer infrastructure upgrades that are the responsibility of local government.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. All properties and applying organizations must be located in a DHCD-designated Sustainable Community at the time of application. Projects must activate vacant buildings in downtown and historic commercial corridors.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a place-based economic development organization with a mission focused on economic and community development in a specific district, OR a local government entity (town, city, or county)
Nonprofit applicants must have IRS-determined nonprofit status at time of application (501c3 status not required, but verified nonprofit status is required)
Organization must have at least 0.5 FTE paid staff at time of application
All properties for which funding is requested must be vacant at time of application (no executed lease with tenant at application date)
All properties must be located in a DHCD-designated Sustainable Community at time of application
Properties must be in downtown or historic commercial corridors with street-level retail that supports a walkable business district
Property must not be in indoor shopping malls, industrial parks, or office parks
Each entity can submit only one application
Eligible organization cannot apply for the same properties for which funding was previously awarded in FY22 or FY23
Property must remain vacant until the lease is executed; lease cannot be signed prior to application date
Sub-grantees (small businesses) must be legal businesses in good standing with the state
Sub-grantee businesses must be able to demonstrate ability to sustain operations beyond grant support
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are currently closed for FY2024 (deadline was April 24, 2024 at 5pm EST). When applications are open, interested parties submit via Maryland OneStop portal. Applications are reviewed after the deadline on a non-rolling basis. All applications are first reviewed for threshold eligibility. Applications meeting threshold requirements are then scored by DHCD staff (each application reviewed by two readers) on a 100-point scale based on: organizational readiness and capacity, creation of an equitable and inclusive process, project alignment with applicant's strategy, and advancement of Project Restore 2.0 goals. Highest-scoring applications are recommended for funding. Upon award, the grantee executes a grant agreement with DHCD. The grant term runs until December 31, 2025. Grantees must submit: (1) Request for Payment/Progress Report for each property before funds are disbursed; (2) Completion Report by property once the sub-grantee is operational (with U&O permit, photos, MHT determination, and paid invoices); (3) Final Report within 30 days of end of grant term (with operating cost documentation, sub-grantee operational status, and impact narrative). DHCD provides technical assistance through in-person training sessions held regionally across the state. Interested parties can sign up for DHCD news and alerts to be notified when future application rounds become available.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financing for the development and preservation of affordable rental housing in priority funding areas.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental housing financing program that accepts applications throughout the year and awards funding based on readiness to proceed. Provides loan financing for projects that develop or preserve affordable rental housing.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted throughout the year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers and sponsors of affordable rental housing, including for-profit, non-profit, and government organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development and preservation of affordable rental housing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Priority funding areas in Maryland.
requirements_list: Projects must be located in a Priority Funding Area.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications accepted throughout the year. Funding awarded based on readiness to proceed. Applicants can download application documents from the agency's Multifamily Document Library.

structured_extraction.program_description: Gap financing program that provides subordinate loans to create jobs and strengthen the Maryland economy by funding the creation and preservation of affordable rental housing. The program works in conjunction with the Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Subordinate loans funded from State general obligation bonds with a maximum of $2.5 million per project (waivable in certain circumstances). Loans feature a 40-year term, 2% simple interest, and payments limited to 75% of annual cash flow. Loans are due on sale, refinancing, transfer of property, or default. During the Construction Loan Period, no payments of principal or interest are required. During the Permanent Loan Period (commencing after construction completion plus 3 months for cost certification), borrowers must pay Surplus Cash annually in an amount equal to the Applicable Surplus Cash Percentage, applied to reduce the outstanding principal balance. After full repayment of principal, Contingent Interest payments become payable from Contingent Interest Surplus Cash. Late charges of 5% apply to payments not made within 10 days of the due date.
