structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers and organizations seeking to create or preserve affordable rental housing in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Gap financing for the creation and preservation of affordable rental housing projects financed through the Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; available throughout Maryland
requirements_list: Project must be financed using Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits
Must meet requirements for both the Multifamily Bond Program and Tax Credit Program as described in the Maryland Qualified Allocation Plan and Multifamily Rental Financing Program Guide

Required zoning for use and density must be in place at time of application with proper documentation (letter from local zoning office or approved PUD resolution satisfies this requirement; conditional use or special exception approval is not required at threshold)
Award of competitive public and private sources of funding necessary for financial feasibility must have been made
Project's Full Time Equivalent jobs must be documented using the Rental Housing Works Full Time Equivalent Job Calculator (where 1 FTE equals 2,080 hours per year)
Board of Public Works must approve all Rental Housing Works funding awards
Projects must meet scoring criteria for bond loans outlined in the Guide
Applicant must certify that competitive sources of public and private funding necessary for project feasibility have been awarded
Development or site plan approval is not required at application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis in conjunction with Multifamily Bond Program and Tax Credit applications. Applicants must submit a completed Application Submission Package with required threshold documentation including: completed CDA Form 202 clearly identifying RHW funds and conforming to RHW loan limitations; written documentation of required zoning for use and density; certification of award of competitive public and private funding; completed FTE Job Calculator; and certification form. A separate application for the Multifamily Bond Program (MBP), LIHTC, and any other DHCD funding must be completed using the Department's standard Application Submission Package and submitted in advance or simultaneously with the RHW application. Applications are tracked by date of receipt and reviewed with Multifamily Bond Program applications. If projects pass threshold, they are scored using evaluation criteria in the Guide. After scoring, kick-off meetings are scheduled with a timeline and critical path. Projects are funded on a first-ready, first-served basis. Maximum loan amount per project is $2.5 million (waivable in certain circumstances), and in no event shall RHW funding exceed an amount necessary to make a project financially feasible and viable as determined by the Department and in accordance with Section 42 of the Internal Revenue Code.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financing for the development and preservation of affordable rental housing in priority funding areas.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financing provided for developing and preserving affordable rental housing located in priority funding areas.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Multifamily property developers and owners focused on affordable rental housing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development and preservation of affordable multifamily rental housing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Priority funding areas in Maryland
requirements_list: Property must provide affordable rental housing
Property must be located in a priority funding area
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact DHCD for application procedures and financing terms.

structured_extraction.program_name: Request for Interest: Federal Funding Application Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to Local Jurisdictions or their Internet Service Provider (ISP) partners to cover costs associated with preparing Federal Funding Applications for broadband expansion to unserved rural areas. The grant can pay for engineering, financial, legal, marketing studies and other approved services from outside consultants needed to prepare a Federal Funding Application. The OSB will assist applicants in developing competitive applications and coordinating with other State Agencies on the use of State assets where they will feasibly benefit the project.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to cover costs of Federal Funding Application preparation. The OSB will reimburse for properly contracted services required for the application, such as engineering consultants, financial consultants, marketing studies, legal consultants, and other costs considered on a case-by-case basis. Maximum funding amount of $125,000 per applicant. Costs will only be reimbursed for projects that submit a completed application for the federal funding program and that meet the terms and conditions of the federal funding program.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis depending on federal funding opportunity and available state funding
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Jurisdictions or their ISP partners seeking to qualify for federal broadband financing opportunities to serve unserved rural residents and businesses
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Engineering consultants, financial consultants, marketing studies, legal consultants, and other approved costs necessary for Federal Funding Application preparation. Projects must provide minimum internet connectivity of 1000 Mbps down and 1000 Mbps up with maximum latency of 50 milliseconds unless federal program is more restrictive.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Projects must be located in unserved areas as defined by federal program requirements or areas without internet service at 25 Mbps down and 3 Mbps up. Federal broadband funding programs typically do not allow funding in areas with other federal investments.
requirements_list: Must be a Local Jurisdiction or ISP partner
Project must be for broadband expansion in unserved rural areas
Must submit completed application for federal funding program
Must meet all terms and conditions of the federal funding program
Network must meet minimum requirements of 1000 Mbps down and 1000 Mbps up with maximum latency of 50 milliseconds unless federal program is more restrictive
Proposed service area must meet all federal program requirements for unserved areas
Technology neutral - any technology capable of meeting speed and latency requirements is permissible
Applicant will be project owner and responsible for overall funding and implementation
Submit electronic copy of response to OSB.MD@maryland.gov with applicant name and 'Federal Funding Assistance RFP response' in subject line

Response must include cover letter with jurisdiction and partner contact information, completed application form signed by both local jurisdiction and ISP partner, business model summary, experience statement, network design and construction description, customer profile, and implementation schedule
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants should submit a Request for Proposals (RFP) response to the Office of Statewide Broadband at OSB.MD@maryland.gov. Response must include: (1) Cover letter with local jurisdiction name, authorized representative contact information; (2) Completed and signed application form; (3) Business model summary outlining network operations and customer operations; (4) Statement of experience of team participating in application preparation and service delivery; (5) Description of network to be constructed including speed, latency, backhaul method, pole vs. underground configuration; (6) Customer profile and competitive service description; (7) Implementation schedule with key milestones. The OSB will evaluate responses to guide partnership and funding allocation decisions. Evaluation is based on qualifications, submittals, and possible interviews. Response to RFP does not confer an obligation to establish a partnership. No reimbursement will be made for costs incurred in responding to the RFP.

structured_extraction.program_description: This federally funded program expands affordable housing for low-income adults with disabilities by providing project-based rental assistance tied to specific units in approved rental housing. The program is a partnership with the Maryland Department of Disabilities and the Maryland Department of Health, and helps eligible residents live in stable housing with access to supportive services.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Section 811 provides project-based rental assistance that subsidizes the contract rent of eligible participants in rental properties that receive DHCD financing. Funds are awarded to eligible housing projects, not directly to individuals. Eligible properties receive assistance to support unit subsidies for people with disabilities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on rolling basis; contact for additional information
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rental housing projects that receive federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits or State Rental Housing Funds can qualify for Section 811 funding. Eligible residents are non-elderly adults between ages 18 and 61 with a qualifying disability who receive Medicaid and have a household income at or below 30 percent of the Area Median Income. For-profit and non-profit sponsors of affordable rental housing developments may apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance to subsidize the contract rent for eligible non-elderly adults with disabilities in approved rental housing units.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in priority funding areas. Statewide program. Under the FY 2013 funding round, approximately 75 percent of units were expected to be in the Baltimore and Washington D.C. areas with the remaining 25 percent distributed on the Eastern Shore and Western Maryland. Under the FY 2012 funding round, units were anticipated to be evenly distributed between Baltimore and Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Areas.
requirements_list: Resident must be between ages 18 and 61 (non-elderly)
Resident must have a qualifying disability
Resident must receive Medicaid
Household income must be at or below 30 percent of the Area Median Income (AMI)
Resident must be referred by the Maryland Department of Disabilities (MDOD)
Housing must be a rental property
Housing must receive financing from DHCD
Project must receive federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits or State Rental Housing Funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: DHCD meets with an Interagency Committee that includes representatives from the Maryland Department of Disabilities (MDOD) and Maryland Department of Health (MDH) to review projects that align with program goals. Once a project is selected, DHCD issues a Reservation Award Letter to the developer confirming the property is eligible for funding to support unit subsidies for people with disabilities.

structured_extraction.program_name: Seed Community Development Anchor Institution Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: The Seed Community Development Anchor Institution Fund provides competitive grants and loans to anchor institutions for community development projects. The program generates jobs, strengthens partnerships between anchor institutions and the State of Maryland, and leads to safer, healthier, and more attractive communities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants and loans to anchor institutions for capital improvement projects. Anchor institutions must provide matching funds equal to the amount of financial assistance received from the Fund (1:1 match).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anchor institutions defined as institutions of higher education in Maryland or hospital institutions in Maryland that meet specific criteria.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital improvement projects in eligible project locations, including community development initiatives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Funds can only be used in Sustainable Communities or areas of the state that have not been previously invested in. Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to determine geographic eligibility.
requirements_list: Must be an anchor institution (institution of higher education or hospital in Maryland)
Must provide evidence of matching funds equal to the amount of financial assistance received (1:1 match)
Projects must be in Sustainable Communities or underinvested areas of the state
Successful projects should build an ongoing relationship between the anchor institution and the community
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For more information and how to apply, visit the State Revitalization Programs webpage.

structured_extraction.program_name: Shelter and Transitional Housing Facilities Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to improve or create transitional housing and emergency shelters that include supportive services, with the goal of reducing homelessness in Maryland. The program provides capital financing for emergency shelters and transitional housing facilities that provide housing and support services to households to prevent homelessness and assist households to be able to live independently.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants support new construction, acquisition, rehabilitation of housing, and purchase of capital equipment for transitional housing and emergency shelters. Grant funds may cover up to one-half of total project costs, or under certain conditions, as much as 75 percent of total project costs. Eligible project activities include: acquiring land and buildings; conducting necessary studies, surveys, plans, specifications, and appraisals; site preparation; labor and materials for construction and rehabilitation; acquisition of machinery, equipment, and furnishings (such as HVAC systems) with a life expectancy of at least 15 years; and fees associated with real estate development including bonds and insurance. Sponsors must maintain the project as transitional housing or emergency shelter for 15 years; if discontinued earlier, the grant becomes repayable. New construction projects must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA). Equipment and furnishings must have a 15-year life expectancy, be durable, not become technically obsolete within 15 years, and not be elaborate or extravagant. Ineligible uses include refinancing existing debt, operating assistance, salaries/wages, maintenance, and replacement of existing furnishings.
structured_extraction.program_audience: 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations and local governments seeking to provide transitional housing or emergency shelter for homeless or at-risk individuals and families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction, acquisition, rehabilitation of housing, and purchase of capital equipment for transitional housing and emergency shelters with supportive services. Eligible expenditures include real property acquisition, architectural/engineering services, construction work, site development and improvements, utilities, and equipment/furnishings meeting specific durability and life-expectancy requirements. Ineligible uses include refinancing debt, operating assistance, salaries, administrative costs, and maintenance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. All projects involving new construction must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA), which includes all incorporated municipalities (including Baltimore City with some exceptions), areas between Baltimore and Washington beltways, Sustainable Communities, Federal and State enterprise zones, areas designated by county governments as PFAs including rural villages, and certified heritage areas within locally designated growth areas. Local government letters of support are required for all projects, and new construction projects must include a letter from local government certifying location in a PFA.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization or local government
Residents served must be homeless (defined as households without permanent housing lacking resources to obtain it and in imminent danger of homelessness) or individuals
Project must be maintained as transitional housing or emergency shelter for 15 years
Local government letter of support required for all projects
New construction projects must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA) and include local government certification
Grant funds may cover up to 50 percent of total project costs, or up to 75 percent under certain conditions
Applicants must identify the homeless target population they expect to serve (families, women and children, single males, victims of domestic violence, etc.)
Applicants must provide complete description of supportive services to be offered to proposed target population
Applicants must submit commitment letters identifying funding sources for services and operating expenses
Supportive services must be specifically oriented to meeting needs of homeless target population and clearly defined with identified service providers
Eligible projects include apartments, condominiums, townhouses, single family detached homes, single room occupancy facilities, and group or shared housing

Equipment and furnishings must have life expectancy of at least 15 years, be unlikely to become technically obsolete for 15 years, be of durable construction, be heavy enough to prevent easy removal (except chairs), not replace adequate items already on hand, be necessary for intended functions, and not be elaborate or extravagant
All roofing projects must comply with State roofing policy (20-year minimum warranty; 60-year life cycle cost analysis for new construction)
Maryland Historical Trust must complete review and issue letter before funds are released
Comply with Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) participation requirements (State goal of 29%)
Projects must not use funds for sectarian religious instruction or sectarian religious buildings or programs
Forest Conservation Program applies to construction on land greater than 40,000 square feet
All prospective contractors must be checked against debarment list
Nonprofit organizations with Low-Income Housing Tax Credits must be sole managing general partner
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact the Housing Development Programs office or Multifamily Housing Programs (MHP) unit of the Community Development Administration (CDA). Applications must include local government support letters. Threshold requirements must be met for acceptance of applications. The Department conducts underwriting and construction review for projects involving new construction or substantial rehabilitation. Viability review and commitment review are conducted during processing. Maryland Historical Trust consultation must be completed before funds are disbursed. Standard processing time applies following submission of complete application materials.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program preserves and improves single-family properties by bringing them up to applicable building codes and standards or a minimum housing quality standard. Available in jurisdictions not served directly by DHCD's general rehabilitation program, this program helps Maryland homeowners address critical health and safety issues in their primary residence.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Zero percent interest fully deferred loans secured by a mortgage for applicants with household income at or below 50 percent of area median income. Loans with interest rates ranging from 0% to 6% based on ability to pay are available for applicants with income up to 80 percent of area median income. The maximum loan is generally $50,000. Loans in excess of $5,000 or with deferred payments are secured by a mortgage. Maximum loan term is 30 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of single-family homes with low to moderate income seeking to address critical health and safety repairs. Generally not available in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Harford County, Howard County, Prince Georges County, or Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation of owner-occupied single-family homes to address critical health and safety issues and bring properties up to applicable building codes and standards. Eligible repairs include mold remediation, gas leaks, roof repair and replacement, asbestos abatement, vermiculite removal, lead abatement, combustion appliance repair and replacement, chimney repair, foundation and sub-space waterproofing and drainage, radon mitigation, electrical hazards and upgrades, plumbing issues, water and well repairs, septic and sewer issues, window and door replacement for health and safety concerns, structural repairs, accessibility modifications, fall prevention improvements, ductwork upgrades, building shell stabilization, and pest treatments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Generally not available in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Harford County, Howard County, Prince Georges County, or Montgomery County. Available in all other Maryland jurisdictions.
requirements_list: Owner must occupy the single-family home as primary residence
Household income cannot exceed 80 percent of the statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income
Some loans available with 0% interest and fully deferred payments for households with income at or below 50 percent of area median income
Property must be a single-family home
Property must have documented critical repairs requiring licensed Maryland contractor or trade professional
Applicant must provide bid from licensed and insured Maryland contractor with photos documenting the issues
All bids must be current (not more than 60 days old)
Total repair costs should not exceed $50,000
Contractor must provide MHIC License or relevant trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance, Letter of Good Standing, and completed W-9 form
Applicant must provide proof of home ownership including deed and current mortgage statement
Applicant must provide photo ID for all applicants
Applicant must provide proof of homeowners insurance and flood insurance if applicable
Property tax bill and homeowners insurance declaration page required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: All loan requests are processed directly by local governments for properties within their jurisdiction. Applicants must submit a completed application with all required supporting documentation including income verification documents (recent paystubs or tax returns), proof of home ownership, property tax bill, homeowners insurance documentation, photo ID, and contractor bid with scope of work and contractor documentation (MHIC license, insurance certificate, letter of good standing, and W-9 form). Applications can be submitted by email to DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov or by mail to Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Strategic Demolition Fund helps accelerate economic development and job creation in existing Maryland communities. It supports greyfield development (reuse of previously developed land) projects that have barriers to completion. The fund focuses on projects with high economic and revitalization impact, investing in pre-development activities that accelerate economic development and job production. Funding program supports demolition projects for vacant and blighted structures across Maryland, helping communities eliminate dangerous buildings and clear land for revitalization.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Capital grants, loans, or recoverable grants for pre-development activities including demolition of derelict non-contributing structures, site acquisition and assembly, site development and infrastructure improvements, construction-level architectural and engineering designs, and stabilization of buildings. Available funding for FY26: $5.5 million capital (from budgeted $10 million). FAAP Fee of 4% of awarded funds applies beginning FY2026 and will be included in the award project budget. Potential recovery of future profits through Promissory Note and Deed of Trust for awards $500,000 or more. Projects outside Baltimore City must be located in Sustainable Communities or in Opportunity Zones in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, and Wicomico Counties.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: July 2, 2025 at 2:59 PM (FY26 application round closed); New user registration deadline June 11, 2025
structured_extraction.contact_name: Larry Brown, Jr., Assistant Director, State Revitalization Resources (Baltimore Region); Garland Thomas, Assistant Director, State Revitalization Resources (Statewide)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and nonprofit community development organizations seeking funding to remove vacant and blighted structures and prepare sites for economic development, working outside Baltimore City on redevelopment projects in Sustainable Communities or Opportunity Zones.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Predevelopment activities including demolition of derelict non-contributing structures, site acquisition and assembly to create redevelopment-sized parcels, site development and infrastructure improvements, construction-level architectural and engineering designs, and stabilization of buildings to prevent deterioration, remediate environmental hazards, and prepare properties for rehabilitation and reuse.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within Sustainable Communities in Maryland outside Baltimore City, or within Opportunity Zones in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, and Wicomico Counties. Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to verify eligibility. Projects should help achieve strategies outlined in the local government's Sustainable Communities plan.
requirements_list: Project must be located within a Sustainable Community boundary (outside Baltimore City) or Opportunity Zone in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, or Wicomico Counties
Addresses vacant or blighted structures or sites
Capital project with at least 15-year shelf life
Awardee must be a local government or nonprofit community development organization
Current awardees must be in compliance with existing award terms and conditions
Organizations with previous year funding required to be current on reporting and program requirements
New organizations must register as user in Project Portal by June 11, 2025 (72 hours approval time)
Applicant must provide evidence of site control or documentation of funding commitments
Sustainable Communities Action Plan alignment required
Maryland Historical Trust review required prior to work or disbursement of funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. New applicants must request a New User account in the DHCD Project Portal by June 11, 2025 (approval may take up to 72 hours). Contact your regional project manager to verify eligibility and authorize access. 2. Upload required organizational documents to profile (Disclosure Authorization and Certification, W-9 Form, operating budget, financial audit or Form 990, corporate resolution, articles of incorporation, bylaws, IRS tax exempt letter, board member list, SDAT certificate of good standing, Secretary of State charitable registration, and corporate diversity addendum). 3. Submit complete application through Project Portal including project information, photographs (interior/exterior), cost estimates, evidence of site control, funding commitments documentation, sustainable communities map reference, and construction drawings/specifications if applicable. 4. Applications must be submitted by July 2, 2025 at 2:59 PM. Review Period: Summer 2025. Award Recommendations: Fall 2025. Award Announcements: Fall/Winter 2025. Award Agreement Execution: Winter 2025. Active Award Term: 2 years with requirement to draw down 50% of awarded funds by first anniversary date. Applications evaluated on community need demonstration (20 points), project scope clarity (20 points), project readiness and timeline (15 points), project financing and leverage (25 points), and capacity of sponsors/partners (20 points).

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides a specific geographic designation for local areas to support community development, revitalization, and sustainability through coordinated strategies. It gives local governments resources to improve older communities and promote growth that is environmentally, economically, and socially responsible. The program combines resources for historic preservation and housing and economic development, focusing on infrastructure improvements, multimodal transportation, and development that strengthens existing communities. Designated Sustainable Communities receive access to an interagency revitalization toolbox of financing programs and tax credit incentives.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a geographic designation that qualifies local areas to access various state programs and resources for revitalization. Designated areas can apply for state programs including Community Legacy Program (capital funding for business retention/attraction, homeownership encouragement, commercial revitalization, mixed-use development, and streetscape improvements), Neighborhood BusinessWorks (gap financing for small businesses and nonprofits), Strategic Demolition Fund (grants for predevelopment, demolition, and land assembly), Operating Assistance Grants (support for operating and technical assistance costs), National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund (for grey field development), Seed Community Development Anchor Institution Program (grants and loans to anchor institutions), Main Street Maryland Program (technical assistance and training), Baltimore Regional Neighborhood Initiative (additional place-based revitalization investments for areas within and surrounding Baltimore City), and Maryland Façade Improvement Program (funds for commercial property exterior improvements). Tax incentives include enhanced Job Creation Tax Credits (up to $5,000 per job vs. $3,000 statewide, with lower job creation threshold of 25 vs. 60 jobs), Enhanced Local Tax Increment Financing Authority, and Low Income Housing Tax Credits with additional points. Financing programs include Water Quality Revolving Loan Fund, Bay Restoration Fund, Overflow and Stormwater Grants, State Highway Administration Transportation Alternatives Program, Safe Routes to School program, Sidewalk Retrofit Program, and Kim Lamphier Bikeways Network Program. The designation is valid for five years and provides access to coordinated state agency resources for community development and revitalization initiatives.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (municipal or county) seeking to designate areas for community revitalization and sustainable development.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The designation allows communities to access state funding and programs for historic preservation, housing and economic development, infrastructure improvements, multimodal transportation, development that strengthens existing communities, business retention and attraction, homeownership encouragement, commercial revitalization, mixed-use development, streetscape improvements, gap financing for small businesses and nonprofits, demolition and land assembly, commercial property exterior improvements, water quality improvements, and safe routes to school projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The entire proposed area must be within a Priority Funding Area. The proposed community should be within or near a town center or transportation center. State Designated Transit Oriented Development (TOD) Areas automatically constitute Sustainable Community Areas. Applicants can use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to verify if an address is within a Priority Funding Area or existing Sustainable Community area.
requirements_list: The entire area must be within a Priority Funding Area
The proposed community should be within or near a town center or transportation center
Must show a defined geographic area with an existing built environment
Must demonstrate need for revitalization or additional state investment to strengthen the local market
Must include a Sustainable Community Action Plan summarizing key initiatives and projects
Must include a local government resolution supporting the boundary designation and Action Plan
Plan must be consistent with other existing community or comprehensive plans

Must demonstrate financial need for local revitalization including support for nonprofit organizations, strengthening older commercial districts and residential communities, and improving public amenities
For State Designated TOD Areas approved prior to 2023, must have approved Sustainable Community Action Plan or update TOD Designation Applications to be eligible for State SRP funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Request an application template by sending an email to Tynan Stevenson at tynan.stevenson@maryland.gov with subject line including program type and community name. Note that for new designations, a meeting with program staff is required before applying. Step 2: Submit application including defined geographic area, Sustainable Community Action Plan, and local government resolution. Step 3: An interagency panel led by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development reviews the application. structured_extraction.program_name: UPLIFT (Utilizing Progressive Lending Investments to Finance Transformation)
structured_extraction.program_description: A public-private partnership program designed to increase homeownership opportunities and property values in underserved communities affected by redlining and disinvestment. The program provides funding to close the appraisal gap—the difference between the cost to build or renovate a property and what it can sell for on the market—to accelerate the development, construction, and sale of quality affordable housing in low-income census tracts and designated Sustainable Communities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The State provides funding through UPLIFT to cover the difference between the cost to build or renovate a property and its market sale price (the appraisal gap). Qualified development teams acquire, develop, build, and sell quality affordable housing in targeted neighborhoods using a combination of public and private financing. Homebuyers acquire fee simple title using down payments, down payment assistance, first mortgage loans (Maryland Mortgage Program or other sources), other acceptable subsidy support, and a 'soft' promissory note from the Department. Developer loans are provided for the construction phase with an origination fee of 1% of the loan amount. The program includes a non-refundable application fee of $1,000 per project.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a rolling basis as long as funding is available
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified nonprofit and for-profit development teams, local jurisdictions, and community-based organizations engaged in revitalization efforts seeking to develop affordable housing in historically redlined communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The assistance can be used to close the appraisal gap in historically redlined neighborhoods by funding the difference between the cost to build or renovate residential properties and the market price at which homes can be sold, enabling the development and sale of quality affordable housing. Funds support acquisition, development, construction, and sale of homes in low-income census tracts and Sustainable Communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in low-income census tracts (where 50% of households have incomes below 60% of Area Median Income or have a poverty rate of 25% or more) and designated Sustainable Communities. New construction projects are not permitted in FEMA Flood Zone areas, except on a waiver basis. The UPLIFT Qualified Areas Map (https://arcgis.com) identifies eligible locations.
requirements_list: Developers must submit a Pre-Application Meeting Request Form before applying
Projects must involve acquisition, development, construction, and sale of quality affordable housing
Projects must be located in both a low-income census tract and a designated Sustainable Community
Properties must be newly constructed or formerly vacant structures that will be substantially rehabilitated
Selected qualified development teams must meet all program standards and oversight requirements
Projects must comply with UPLIFT Design and Construction Standards
A non-refundable $1,000 application fee per project is required
Development teams must demonstrate acceptable credit history and current financial capacity
All development team members must submit appropriate financial statements (corporate entities submit audited, reviewed, or compiled statements; individuals submit personal financial statements)
Lead Developer must have a determinative or controlling position in the project entity

Each of the developer, builder/general contractor, architect, Neighborhood Engagement Facilitator, and marketing/sales entity must have experience as significant participants in comparably scaled projects
Projects must meet one of the following energy and environmental standards: EPA Energy Star, Enterprise Green Communities, USGBC LEED, or equivalent
Design must include accessibility features per latest USBC standards with 25% of units incorporating universal design features
New construction cost limits apply: $190 per square foot for cottages, single-family, semi-detached dwellings, and townhomes
Projects must address neighborhood conditions and strengthen community engagement
Site control documentation is required
Environmental assessments must be current (typically less than 12 months old)
All required exhibits must be included with application submission
Applications must include both electronic and hard copy versions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 0: Applicants must review the UPLIFT Program Guide and schedule a pre-application meeting with DHCD staff for preliminary feedback on project specifics. Step 1: After the pre-application meeting, submit an Electronic Application Submission Request Form at https://dhcd.maryland.gov/HousingDevelopment/Pages/UPLIFT/Submission-Request.aspx; DHCD will provide access to the Application Submission Package. Step 2: Download the complete Application Submission Package composed of seven parts: (1) Application Portfolio General Elements, (2) Development Team, (3) Project Economics, (4) Project Location, (5) Design and Construction, (6) Marketing and Sales, and (7) Neighborhood Engagement. Complete all required forms, narratives, certifications, development information, and financial documentation. Step 3: Pay the $1,000 non-refundable application fee via ACH or check to the Community Development Administration Central Cashier and include proof of payment with the application. Step 4: Prepare two complete copies of the application—one hard copy addressed to Brien O'Toole, 7800 Harkins Rd, Lanham, MD 20706, and one electronic copy in the specified format. Upload all files to the provided Dropbox link in correct subfolders and submit the hard copy to DHCD's Lanham office. Step 5: DHCD evaluates applications for compliance with Threshold Criteria and scores against Evaluative Criteria across five areas: (1) Development Team Experience, Capacity, and Composition (60 points), (2) Project Impact (50 points), (3) Leveraging Resources (30 points), (4) Readiness to Proceed (30 points), and (5) Development Quality (20 points). Step 6: Projects passing threshold review and scoring adequately enter the underwriting pipeline. A Project Kick-off Meeting is generally held 45-60 days after complete application submission to determine the underwriting schedule. Step 7: Processing includes submission of a Final Underwriting Submission (FUS) updating financing, design, construction, and marketing elements. Step 8: The UPLIFT Loan Committee makes a recommendation to the Secretary for authorization to commit and deploy resources. Step 9: Following Secretary's determination and underwriting approval, DHCD issues a Commitment Letter specifying terms and conditions for closing. Step 10: Initial Financing Closing occurs with satisfactory submission of closing checklist items, represented by the Office of the Attorney General. Step 11: Shortly after closing and issuance of Notice to Proceed to the builder, a Construction Kick-off Meeting is held to coordinate construction phase, marketing, and occupancy requirements. Applicants should notify DHCD when hard copy application materials are expected to arrive. Materially incomplete applications will not be considered. All documents submitted must be current, usually less than 12 months old; updated due diligence reports may be required depending on processing length. If an application is rejected, written notice will state reasons for rejection; applicants may request reconsideration in writing within 7 calendar days to the Director of Community Development Administration.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's largest residential energy conservation program that helps income-eligible homeowners and renters reduce heating and cooling costs through energy-conservation measures while addressing health and safety issues in their homes.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides energy conservation services at no cost to eligible participants. Services include a comprehensive home energy audit inspection followed by improvements such as blower door air infiltration reduction, insulation in attics, floors and walls, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofit, furnace clean and tune services, safety repairs, burner retrofit or replacement, and health and safety items. Additional services may include HVAC system replacement or repair, combustion safety repairs, carbon monoxide and smoke detector installation, window and door weatherization, ductwork sealing and insulation, water heater insulation, low-flow fixtures, roof and attic ventilation, and structural repairs. Homeowners and renters who meet the household income requirements are eligible to receive these services through local weatherization agencies in each territory. Emergency heating system repairs and replacements are available November 1 through March 31 (October 1 through March 31 in Garrett County). Emergency cooling system repairs and replacements are available June 1 through September 30. Water heater repairs and replacements are available April 1 through September 30. All work includes a one-year warranty on labor and materials from the date of installation.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Housing and Building Energy Programs / Kiahnna Burney
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible homeowners and renters in Maryland, with priority given to those over 60 years old, those with disabilities, those with children in the home, and households with high energy usage or energy burden.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy conservation measures including air infiltration reduction, insulation, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofit, furnace maintenance and replacement, health and safety repairs, HVAC system replacements, combustion safety repairs, and structural repairs in residential homes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland through local weatherization agencies in each territory. Local Weatherization Agencies (LWAs) serve the following counties and Baltimore City: Allegany County (Allegany County HRDC), Anne Arundel County, Baltimore County (Community Action Council of Howard County), Baltimore City (Baltimore City DHCD), Calvert County (Housing Authority of St. Mary's County), Caroline County (Maryland Rural Development Corporation and Shore Up!), Carroll County, Cecil County (Maryland Rural Development Corporation), Charles County (Housing Authority of St. Mary's County), Dorchester County (Shore Up!), Frederick County (Frederick Community Action Agency), Garrett County (Garrett County Community Action Committee), Harford County, Howard County (Community Action Council of Howard County), Kent County (Maryland Rural Development Corporation and Shore Up!), Montgomery County (Community Action Council of Howard County), Prince George's County (Housing Authority of St. Mary's County), Queen Anne's County (Shore Up! and Maryland Rural Development Corporation), Somerset County (Shore Up!), St. Mary's County (Housing Authority of St. Mary's County), Talbot County (Shore Up! and Maryland Rural Development Corporation), Washington County (Allegany County HRDC and Frederick Community Action Agency), Wicomico County (Shore Up!), and Worcester County (Shore Up!).
requirements_list: Limited income household status
Household income at or below 60% of State Median Income (SMI) or 200% of Federal Poverty Level (FPL), whichever is higher

Currently participating in Utility Bill Pay Assistance through the Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP), Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF), Supplemental Security Income (SSI), or HUD housing assistance programs qualifies as automatically income-eligible
Must submit an application to apply for services
Must be a homeowner or renter in Maryland
Home must be in a condition that permits weatherization work; homes with severe structural, mechanical, sanitary, or health and safety issues may be deferred until conditions are corrected
Energy Auditors must have BPI HEP Energy Auditor Certification
Weatherization installers must have BPI HEP Retrofit Installer Technician training or equivalent skills
Crew Leaders must have BPI HEP Crew Leader training or equivalent skills
Quality Control Inspectors must have HEP Quality Control Inspector certification from BPI
All weatherization workers must have EPA Lead Renovation, Repair and Painting (LRRP) certification

All weatherization workers must have Asbestos Awareness training
Licensed trades performing work must hold valid State of Maryland licenses or certifications
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your Local Weatherization Agency (LWA) serving your county to submit an application. The agency will review your application and determine whether additional information is needed. Income and eligibility will be verified and documented. Once eligibility is certified, the local weatherization agency will schedule an energy audit inspection within 30 days of application certification. The energy audit identifies energy-saving opportunities and a package of feasible improvements is modeled. If the home's condition permits and measures are cost-effective, a work order is prepared and weatherization work begins according to program guidelines. A certified quality control inspector verifies completion of all work. Occupant education is provided to maximize energy savings. For emergency heating repairs during the no-heat season, the agency must schedule an assessment within 8 hours of receiving the lead and resolve the crisis within 5 days (36 hours for life-threatening situations). DHCD will qualify applicants for all applicable funding sources.

structured_extraction.program_description: A COVID-19 pandemic relief grant program that provides financial assistance to child care providers to cover costs related to the coronavirus pandemic, including decreased enrollment, reduced capacity limits, temporary closures, fixed costs, increased operating expenses, cleaning and sanitation, personal protective equipment, and increased staff salaries or wages.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to child care providers to cover pandemic-related costs including decreased enrollment, reduced capacity limits, temporary closures, fixed costs, increased operating expenses, cleaning and sanitation, personal protective equipment, and increased staff salaries or wages. Grant amounts ranged from $2,400 to $60,000 depending on the licensed capacity of the child care facility. Grants are subject to 1099-G reporting requirements if amounts exceed $600. Grant funds must be spent by December 31, 2021. Recipients must keep financial documents for 5 years and may be subject to random audit. Payments can be received by direct deposit or mail. Federal regulations require documentation retention for audit purposes.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application closed on 3/3/21 at 3:00 p.m.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care providers in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Costs of decreased enrollment, reduced capacity limits due to state or local restrictions, temporary closures related to coronavirus, fixed costs (rent, mortgage, property taxes), increased operating expenses, cleaning and sanitation, personal protective equipment or PPE, and increased salaries or wages for staff. Grant funds must be spent by December 31, 2021.

Providers must submit W-9 form
Providers must complete eligibility checklist
Before and after school providers eligible if operating on March 3, 2021 and maintaining their license
Each location with a separate license number requires a separate application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Providers complete the online application through SurveyMonkey by the March 3, 2021 deadline at 3:00 p.m. They must submit required documentation including the W-9 form, completed eligibility checklist, and verification of reopening form if applicable. Providers can verify their application was received by searching for their Licensing Number in the list of Received Applications published on the relief grant webpage. Applications are processed individually after the deadline closes. Processing and changes begin after March 3rd with a 4-6 week timeline for grant distribution. Payments are distributed by direct deposit or mail. Providers can sign up for direct deposit using the ACH/Direct Deposit Authorization Form (GADX10Form), which requires submission of either a voided check (with matching address) or a bank letter signed by a bank representative confirming account name, account number, and ABA routing number. Starter checks, counter checks, sample checks, or deposit tickets are NOT acceptable. Online credit cards are NOT eligible for ACH transfer. For questions, providers can complete the Contact Us form at https://forms.gle/MCVNDpw13LGVFaMP9.

structured_extraction.program_description: This grant provides funding to stabilize existing child care programs affected by COVID-19. The program distributes approximately $128 million in American Rescue Plan Act funds to eligible child care providers, including family child care homes, large family child care homes, child care centers, and education programs. Providers receive a base award plus additional funding based on the ages of children served, participation in the Child Care Scholarship program, Maryland EXCELS rating, and location in areas with high social vulnerability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Awards are distributed as follows: a base award of $10,000 for all eligible providers, plus additional per-licensed child care slot funding of $126 for providers serving infants (6 weeks to 12 months), toddlers (13 months to 23 months), children in the Child Care Scholarship program, providers participating in Maryland EXCELS with a rating of 1-5, and providers located in census tracts with a Social Vulnerability Index greater than 0.6. The balance of any unutilized funds from providers not seeking grants is distributed evenly to all grant-awarded providers per licensed slot. All grants are taxable. Grants do not have to be repaid if recipients meet all required certifications. Funds can be used for: personnel costs including wages, benefits, premium pay, recruitment and retention; rent or mortgage payments, utilities, facilities maintenance and improvements, or insurance; personal protective equipment, cleaning and sanitation supplies and services, training and professional development related to health and safety; equipment and supplies to respond to COVID-19 including software, computers, health monitoring equipment; goods and services necessary to maintain or resume child care services including food, supplies, toys, cribs, bedding, books, craft materials, licensing fees; behavioral health supports for children and employees; and past expenses incurred during the grant period.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: January 23, 2022 by 6:00pm (EST) CLOSED
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care providers, family child care home providers, large family child care home providers, child care centers, and education programs under a Letter of Compliance that were operating on or before December 15, 2021 and meet licensing or compliance requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personnel costs (wages, benefits, premium pay, recruitment, retention, bonuses, vaccine-related costs); facilities (rent, mortgage, utilities, phone, internet, maintenance, COVID-related improvements like air filtration and plexiglass); personal protective equipment and cleaning supplies (masks, gloves, hand sanitizer, sanitizing wipes, bleach, cleaning services); training on cleaning and health/safety protocols; equipment and supplies (accounting software, payroll software, public health tracking software, thermometers, computers, smartphones, tablets); goods and services (food, snacks, diapers, wipes, toys, cribs, bedding, books, craft materials, licensing fees); behavioral health supports for children and employees; and past expenses incurred during the grant period.

requirements_list: Applicants must be a licensed family child care home, licensed large family child care home, licensed child care center, or education program operating under a Letter of Compliance

Applicants must provide relief from copayments and tuition payments for enrolled families to the extent possible, prioritizing relief for families struggling to make payments

Applicants must maintain records of all child care business activities, health and safety protocols, employee payments and benefits, hours worked, program operation hours, family payments, and any tuition forgiven
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications were submitted online only through a SurveyMonkey link. Providers could apply on a computer or mobile device. The application window opened January 3, 2022 and closed January 23, 2022 at 6:00pm EST. As of January 23, 2022 at 6:00pm, received applications were entered into the system as submitted and the information is listed as entered on applications. Receipt of an application does not mean the application has been accepted, approved, or completed in its entirety. If an application is incomplete or more information is required, an MSDE representative will contact the applicant.
