structured_extraction.assistance_description: The fund provides reimbursement for instructional materials and classroom learning materials required for pursuing Maryland Accreditation. Maximum reimbursement amounts are: $2,500 for child care centers or school-age only programs serving 100 or fewer children; $3,000 for programs serving more than 100 children. Funds cannot exceed the cost of materials as determined by the accreditation standards. Programs can be reimbursed for items purchased within 12 months before the date of the application for accreditation support. Consumable items (paint, crayons, markers, glue, paper, etc.) are not reimbursable.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers and school-age only programs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Instructional materials and classroom learning materials associated with pursuing Maryland Accreditation, including books, puppets, blocks, musical instruments, learning aids, technology equipment, and other non-consumable classroom materials for infants, toddlers, preschool, and school-age children.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide (all Maryland counties)
requirements_list: Must be a licensed child care center or school-age only program with an individual license number
Each site with individual license number can apply separately
Cannot use funds for facility improvements
Cannot use funds for accreditation fees
Cannot use funds for association membership fees
Cannot use funds for staff training
Cannot use funds for costs paid through another funding source
Cannot exceed the fees charged by the accreditation organization
Consumable items are not reimbursable
Purchases must have been made within 12 months before the application date
Maximum award of $2,500 for programs serving 100 or fewer children or $3,000 for programs serving more than 100 children
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Application for Maryland Accreditation Support through the Maryland One Stop portal. Refer to the Infant and Toddlers Classroom Learning Materials Checklist (for ages birth-36 months) or Preschool & School-Age Classroom Learning Materials Checklist (for ages 3-16 years) to identify eligible materials. Complete a separate reimbursement form for each vendor and attach receipts/invoices. Materials eligible for reimbursement include: language and literacy materials, discovery/science/nature materials, physical development materials, music materials, dramatic/imaginative play materials, mathematics materials (for preschool/school-age), outdoor learning materials (for preschool/school-age), technology equipment, and other approved instructional materials.

structured_extraction.program_description: This fund helps licensed child care centers, registered family child care providers, and school-age only programs pay for required application fees related to pursuing national accreditation through MSDE-recognized accrediting organizations, including initial applications, renewal applications, and annual updates.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The fund covers required application fees for national accreditation through MSDE-recognized accrediting organizations, including initial application fees, renewal application fees, and annual update fees. Awards are paid directly to the accrediting organization on behalf of the applicant. Funds cannot exceed the fees charged by the accreditation organization. Recognized accrediting organizations include: American Montessori Society (AMS), Association Montessori International/USA (AMI/USA), Association of Independent Maryland Schools (AIMS), Association of Waldorf Schools of North America (AWSNA), Cognia Early Learning Accreditation, Council on Accreditation – After-School Accreditation (COA/ASA), Lumen Accreditation, Maryland Accreditation (MSDE), Middle States Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Elementary and Secondary Schools (MSA-CESS), National Accreditation Commission (NAC), National Association for the Education of Young Children (NAEYC), National Association for Family Child Care (NAFCC), and National Early Childhood Program Accreditation (NECPA).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers, registered family child care providers, and school-age only programs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Required application fees for national accreditation through MSDE-recognized accrediting organizations, including initial applications, renewal applications, and annual updates
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide (all Maryland counties)
requirements_list: Must be a licensed child care center, registered family child care provider, or school-age only program
Must be pursuing accreditation through an MSDE-recognized accrediting organization
Must submit a completed application to the accrediting organization
Must submit a completed Accreditation Work Plan
Must submit a copy of the accrediting organization's fee page
Must submit a copy of current accreditation certificate if currently accredited
Cannot use funds for facility improvements
Cannot use funds for association membership fees
Cannot use funds for staff training
Cannot use funds for costs paid through another funding source
Cannot exceed the fees charged by the accreditation organization
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Application for National Accreditation Support through the Maryland One Stop portal. Required documents include: a copy of your completed application submitted to the accrediting organization, a completed Accreditation Work Plan outlining steps to achieve accreditation, a copy of the accrediting organization's fee page, and a copy of your current accreditation certificate if you are currently accredited. Once all required documents are submitted, your application will be approved within 30 days. The MSDE Accreditation Manager will notify you via email on the status of your application. Awards are paid directly to the accrediting organization on your behalf.

structured_extraction.program_description: Support funds are available to assist child care centers, school-age only programs, family child care providers, and public pre-K programs with the expense of pursuing Maryland Accreditation and other recognized national accreditations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two separate programs are available: (1) Maryland Accreditation Support Fund: Provides reimbursement for instructional materials purchased within 12 months before application date. Maximum awards: $2,500 for programs serving 100 or fewer children; $3,000 for programs serving more than 100 children. Materials must align with Infants and Toddlers Classroom Materials Checklist or Preschool and School-Age Classroom Learning Materials Checklist. (2) National Accreditation Support Fund: Provides assistance with required application fees for pursuing accreditation through recognized accrediting organizations (NAEYC, NAFCC, AMS, AMI/USA, AIMS, AWSNA, Cognia, COA/ASA, Lumen Accreditation, Maryland Accreditation, MSA-CESS, NAC, or NECPA). Awards are paid directly to the accrediting organization on behalf of the applicant.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers, school-age only programs, family child care providers, and public pre-K programs pursuing Maryland Accreditation or other recognized national accreditations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Maryland Accreditation Support Fund: Instructional materials for classroom learning (Infants and Toddlers or Preschool and School-Age classroom materials). National Accreditation Support Fund: Required application fees for pursuing national accreditation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide
requirements_list: Program must be a licensed child care center, school-age only program, family child care provider, or public pre-K program
For Maryland Accreditation Support Fund: Program must be pursuing or have received Maryland Accreditation and have individual license number(s)

For National Accreditation Support Fund: Program must be pursuing accreditation through a recognized accrediting organization (NAEYC, NAFCC, AMS, AMI/USA, AIMS, AWSNA, Cognia, COA/ASA, Lumen Accreditation, Maryland Accreditation, MSA-CESS, NAC, or NECPA)
Materials or expenses must not already be covered by another funding source
Purchases must be made within 12 months before the application date (Maryland Accreditation)

For National Accreditation Support Fund: Must submit copy of application to accrediting organization, completed Accreditation Work Plan, copy of accrediting organization's fee page, and copy of current accreditation certificate if currently accredited
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For Maryland Accreditation Support Fund: Programs should refer to the Maryland Accreditation Online System User Guide for guidance on requesting Accreditation Support Funds. For National Accreditation Support Fund: Submit required documents including application copy to accrediting organization, Accreditation Work Plan with action items and completion dates, accrediting organization's fee page, and current accreditation certificate if applicable. Applications are approved within 30 days of receiving all required documents. Applicants will receive email notification from the MSDE Accreditation Manager regarding application status. Awards for the National Accreditation Support Fund are paid directly to the accrediting organization on behalf of the applicant.

structured_extraction.program_name: Adjustment to Blindness for Life & Employment (ABLE)
structured_extraction.program_description: An eight-week program designed to help individuals with blindness or low vision develop basic adjustment to blindness skills, independent living skills, and work readiness skills in preparation for employment. Participants interact with others who have vision loss and develop strategies for managing their condition.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eight-week program operating four days per week (Monday through Thursday) from 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The program is conducted twice per year, in fall and spring. Participants receive instruction in adjustment to blindness skills, independent living skills, and work readiness skills.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who are blind or visually impaired
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in adjustment to blindness skills, independent living skills, and work readiness skills
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at the Workforce & Technology Center in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be blind or visually impaired
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Office of Blind and Vision Services at the Workforce & Technology Center to apply for the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial reimbursement to help school-based programs, non-profits, and organizations serve snacks or suppers to children in afterschool care programs that provide educational or enrichment activities in a supervised environment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial reimbursement provided to school districts, non-profit organizations, and school-based afterschool programs to help cover the cost of serving healthy snacks and suppers to children in afterschool care. Programs must be area eligible and provide educational or enrichment activities in a supervised environment. The NSLP Afterschool Snack Service is a federally-assisted snack service that provides cash reimbursement to encourage or assist schools in serving snacks to children after the regular school day. Children participating in an approved afterschool care program age 18 and under, and participating children who turn 19 during the school year, are eligible to receive reimbursable snacks through the NSLP.
structured_extraction.program_audience: School districts, non-profit organizations, and non-school-based organizations operating afterschool care programs for children.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for the cost of serving snacks and suppers to children in afterschool programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Programs must be area eligible according to USDA guidelines.
requirements_list: School district must participate in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) or be eligible for CACFP
Afterschool program must provide educational or enrichment activities in a supervised environment
Non-school-based organizations must meet CACFP area eligibility requirements
Afterschool care program must primarily provide care for children after school
Program must have organized, regularly scheduled activities in a structured and supervised environment
Program must include education or enrichment activities, distinct from extracurricular programs organized primarily for scholastic, cultural or athletic purposes
Children participating must be age 18 and under, or turn 19 during the school year
Eligible education or enrichment activities include: homework assistance, tutoring, supervised drop-in athletic programs, extended day programs, drama activities, and arts and crafts programs
Organized interscholastic programs or community-level competitive sports programs are not eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local school district or the Maryland Public Schools nutrition program office for participation requirements and application procedures. The NSLP Afterschool Snack Service is administered at the federal level by the Food and Nutrition Service (USDA) and at the state level by state agencies, which operate the snack service through agreements with local school food authorities (SFAs). SFAs are ultimately responsible for the administration of the snack service.

structured_extraction.program_name: American Rescue Plan (ARP) Act of 2021 Child Care Stabilization Fund Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Non-competitive grant program that provides funding to licensed child care providers and family child care programs in Maryland to help them keep their doors open and support early childhood educators affected by COVID-19. The federal Biden Administration released $39 billion in American Rescue Plan funds to states to address the child care crisis caused by the pandemic.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Non-competitive, non-repayable grant consisting of a $15,000 base award plus $500 per licensed slot. Grant period runs from September 6, 2021 through March 6, 2022. Funds do not need to be repaid as long as recipients meet all required certifications. Funds can be used for: personnel costs (payroll, salaries, benefits, premium pay, recruitment/retention, vaccine-related costs, bonuses, staff professional development); facility costs (rent, mortgage, late fees, utilities, phone/internet, maintenance, COVID-related facility improvements, insurance); PPE, cleaning, and sanitation supplies and services; health and safety training; equipment and supplies (computers, smartphones, tablets, thermometers, accounting/payroll software, health monitoring equipment); goods and services (food, snacks, beverages, diapers, wipes, toys, games, books, craft materials, cribs, sheets, blankets, licensing fees); behavioral health supports for children and employees; and past expenses incurred during the COVID-19 pandemic. Recipients must also provide relief from copayments and tuition payments for enrolled families to the extent possible, prioritizing families struggling to make payments.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: August 6, 2021 at 4:00 p.m.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care providers, family child care providers, and early childhood educators in Maryland that were licensed before March 11, 2021, are currently open and serving children, or reopening to serve children by September 7, 2021.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personnel costs including payroll, salaries, employee benefits, premium pay (hazard pay/hero pay), recruitment and retention costs, bonuses, vaccine-related costs (including paid time off for vaccine appointments and transportation), and staff professional development; rent or mortgage payments, late fees, utilities, phone and internet, facility maintenance and improvements, insurance; personal protective equipment, cleaning and sanitation supplies and services, health and safety training; equipment and supplies to respond to COVID-19 including accounting software, payroll software, computers, smartphones, tablets, health monitoring equipment, and thermometers; goods and services necessary to maintain or resume child care services including food, snacks, beverages, diapers, wipes, toys, games, books, craft materials, cribs, sheets, blankets, and licensing fees; behavioral health supports for children and employees; past expenses incurred during the COVID-19 pandemic; and relief from copayments and tuition payments for enrolled families to the extent possible, prioritizing families struggling to make payments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Programs must be licensed through the Maryland State Department of Education before March 11, 2021.
requirements_list: Program must be licensed through the Maryland State Department of Education with a license issue date on or before March 11, 2021
Program must have a valid License, Certificate of Registration, or Letter of Compliance issued by MSDE

Program must be currently open and serving children or, if temporarily closed, must have a Verification of Reopening Form on file with the Office of Child Care and be open and serving children by September 6, 2021
Must implement policies in line with Maryland guidance and CDC guidance when open and providing services

Must continue paying at least the same amount of weekly wages and maintain the same benefits for all employees (lead teachers, aides, and staff in transportation and food preparation) for the duration of the grant period
Must not furlough employees from the date of application submission through the duration of the grant period
Must provide relief from copayments and tuition payments for enrolled families to the extent possible, prioritizing families struggling to make payments

Must keep all documents and records related to child care business stabilization grant, including health and safety protocols, employee payments and benefits, hours worked, and tuition forgiveness amounts
For programs with multiple locations, a separate application must be completed for each location
Applicants must upload a digital copy of their license, registration, or letter of compliance with their application (accepted formats: PDF, JPG, JPEG, DOC, DOCX, PNG, GIF)
Must provide Form W-9 (Request for Taxpayer Identification Number) and Maryland ACH/Direct Deposit Authorization Form for payment processing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the grant eligibility checklist to confirm all requirements are met. 2. Review the expense tracking tool and category-specific guidance documents to understand allowable expenses. 3. Complete the grant worksheet. 4. Watch the demo video or technical assistance session recording. 5. Digitize and upload a copy of your license, registration, or letter of compliance. 6. Complete and submit the online application by August 6, 2021 at 4:00 p.m. 7. Submit required certifications and agree to all terms. 8. Provide Form W-9 and Maryland ACH/Direct Deposit Authorization Form for payment processing. 9. If assistance is needed, contact or visit your local Child Care Resource Center. 10. Each location must submit a separate and complete application. 11. After submission, verify receipt by searching for your license number or program name in the list of received applications. Incomplete applications that did not answer all questions or hit the submit button will not be processed.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free 90-minute annual training update required for all child care staff and family child care providers to maintain current knowledge of health and safety requirements. The training covers health, safety, and nutrition topics and qualifies for 1.5 hours of Core of Knowledge training credit in Health, Safety, and Nutrition. Participants receive a certificate of participation upon successful completion.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free 90-minute online training update accessible through the MSDE Canvas learning management system (https://msde.instructure.com). The training comprises multiple modules including Introduction to Basic Health and Safety plus additional topic modules. Participants must complete all topics and a Final Review Activity with a score of 80% or higher to unlock the Certificate of Completion. Upon successful completion, participants receive a certificate that qualifies for 1.5 Core of Knowledge hours in Health, Safety, and Nutrition. The training can be completed one section at a time, with the system remembering where you left off. The certificate can be downloaded, printed, or emailed to the licensing specialist. Also recommended for child care substitutes and volunteers.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Must be completed by December 31, 2025. Newly approved family child care providers and staff hired between October and December 2025 must complete by March 31, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: All child care staff and family child care providers in Maryland. Also recommended for child care substitutes and volunteers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Annual continuing education training on current health and safety practices and requirements for child care programs, covering health, safety, and nutrition best practices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all child care providers in Maryland through online access.
requirements_list: Must be a child care staff member or family child care provider
Must complete training by December 31, 2025
Newly hired staff or newly approved providers (October-December 2025) must complete by March 31, 2026
Must have internet access and basic computer skills to participate in online training
Must successfully complete all training modules
Must score 80% or higher on the Final Review Activity to receive certificate of completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Access the MSDE Canvas login page at https://msde.instructure.com/login/canvas. 2) Log in with your email address and password. 3) Click the Educator Resources button, then the Early Childhood Modules button, and select the Basic Health and Safety Annual Update 2025. 4) Begin with the Introduction to Basic Health and Safety module (other modules are initially locked). 5) Exit each module using the EXIT COURSE button in the upper right corner. 6) After completing the Introduction, all other topic modules become available and can be completed in any order. 7) As you complete each topic, a green check mark appears. 8) Once all topics are complete, the Final Review module becomes available. 9) Complete the Final Review Activity and achieve a score of 80% or higher to unlock the Certificate of Completion module. 10) Download and save the certificate to your device or print it, and email the certificate to your licensing specialist.

structured_extraction.program_description: DORS Rehabilitation Technology Services staff provides customized assessments, equipment, and training to help job seekers and students with disabilities find appropriate assistive technology to support their school and employment goals. Services include assessments, hardware, software, and training delivered at the Work Training Center in Baltimore or in the individual's community.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DORS Rehabilitation Technology Services provides customized assessments to identify appropriate assistive technology, including: desktop or portable video magnifiers, note-taking devices, specialized software (voice recognition software, screen reading software, and other products to assist with reading and writing), and mobile devices or apps to assist with organization and time management. The program provides training and technical support on hardware and software use through classes covering JAWS screen reading software, ZoomText magnification and screen reading software, and specialized classes based on individual needs. Assessments and training may be held at the WTC campus in Baltimore or in the individual's community.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers and students with disabilities who are DORS consumers with an employment or school goal.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assistive technology equipment, software, training, and technical support for job seekers and students with disabilities to support employment and school goals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services held at Work Training Center campus in Baltimore or in the individual's community.
requirements_list: Must be a DORS consumer
Must have an employment or school goal
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals who are DORS consumers contact their DORS Counselor or local office or request DORS services to access Rehabilitation Technology Services. Staff provides customized assessments to identify appropriate assistive technology, followed by equipment provision and training services as needed.

structured_extraction.program_description: A 16-week training course that prepares job seekers with disabilities to work in the automotive industry as entry-level General Service Technicians. Automotive general service technicians diagnose and repair motor vehicles, and perform other tasks such as vehicle inspection, tire and lubrication services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 16-week in-person training program provided at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center campus in Baltimore. Students receive hands-on instruction in automotive maintenance and repair, customer service, shop safety, and equipment operation using state-of-the-art equipment including tire balancing machines, 4-wheel alignment lifts, and hand tools. Training covers lubrication and fluid changes, tire changing and balancing, electrical system testing and charging, battery replacement, tune-ups, vehicle inspections, and brake repair.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with disabilities seeking entry-level positions in the automotive repair industry.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and skill development in automotive general service technician work, including lubrication and fluid changes, tire service, electrical systems, battery replacement, tune-ups, vehicle inspections, and brake repair. Training includes customer service, shop safety, automotive maintenance and repair, and equipment operation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is provided at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center campus in Baltimore.
requirements_list: Valid driver's license with no more than 2 points
Ability to lift 50 pounds
Ability to squat, stoop, and kneel
Third grade reading level and basic math skills
No disqualifying criminal background
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested individuals should contact their DORS Counselor or local office for more information. Individuals can also request DORS services via the QR code provided in program materials.

structured_extraction.program_description: Free online training course for all child care providers, staff, substitutes, and adults responsible for the care and safety of children in licensed child care programs. The training meets state and federal requirements of the Child Care and Development Block Grant (CCDBG) and reflects recommended best practices related to Office of Child Care Code of Maryland Regulations (COMAR). The course consists of four modules plus introduction and final review and takes approximately 3 hours to complete.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free online training course consisting of four modules plus introduction and final review that takes approximately 3 hours to complete. Accessed at https://msde.instructure.com. The course must be completed within a 21-day period after registration. Participants must score a minimum of 80% on all topic reviews and final review to receive a certificate of completion. Participants get up to two attempts to pass the final assessment. New employees have 90 days after hire to complete the course to be in compliance. Once completed, participants receive a certificate of completion that must be printed immediately; MSDE does not store or provide copies of certificates. Participants can complete the training at their own pace and stop/return without restarting, as long as they click EXIT COURSE when leaving. Accounts expire at the end of the course period. Face-to-face training is also available through approved trainers at a cost set by the trainer. A Spanish language version is available through Penn State Better Kid Care for a fee.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration opens monthly on a rolling basis; registration open one week per month on specified dates (e.g., April cohort closes March 23 at 12:00 pm, May cohort closes April 23 at 12:00 pm, June cohort closes May 23 at 12:00 pm). No late registrations accepted. New employees have 90 days after hire to complete the course.
structured_extraction.program_audience: All child care providers, staff, substitutes, and adults responsible for the care and safety of children in licensed child care programs in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training on health and safety basics for child care programs, including topics required by state and federal regulations, including breastfeeding awareness
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all child care providers in Maryland. For providers without computer access, public libraries provide computers available for use to complete the training. Face-to-face alternatives are available through approved trainers. Spanish language version available through Penn State Better Kid Care for a fee.
requirements_list: Must be a child care provider, staff member, substitute, or adult responsible for child care in a licensed program
Must have a valid email address to register
Must have basic technical skills including using a mouse, typing, using email, viewing videos, navigating the internet, and printing pages
Must complete all four modules, introduction, and final review
Must score a minimum of 80% on all topic reviews and final review
Must complete course before course end date/account expiration (21-day course period)
New employees must complete training within 90 days after hire to be in compliance
Each account is allowed only two attempts to pass the final assessment
Only one email address per registration; separate email addresses required for multiple registrants
Must print certificate immediately upon completion as MSDE does not retain or send copies
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Register during the designated one-week registration period each month through the online registration form at https://earlychildhood.marylandpublicschools.org/basic-health-safety-training. 2) Check spam/junk email folders for login information. Username is the email address used to register. 3) Log in to https://msde.instructure.com/login/canvas using your registered email address as username. Click the 'Request Password' button if you don't have your password. 4) Access the Introduction to Basic Health and Safety module first; other modules unlock after completion. 5) Complete all modules and final review at your own pace over the 21-day course period (you can stop and return without restarting by clicking EXIT COURSE). 6) Complete the final review and survey in one sitting; do not exit without completing it as the system will auto-submit. 7) Achieve at least 80% on all assessments to unlock the Certificate of Completion module. 8) Print your certificate immediately from the Certificate of Completion module as copies are not archived. 9) For face-to-face training, contact an approved trainer from the provided list. Contact healthandsafetyocc.msde@maryland.gov for any questions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Broadening Options and Opportunities for Students Today (BOOST) Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship program that provides award funding for eligible students from low-income families to attend participating nonpublic schools. Priority is given to students who qualified for free and reduced-price school meals and received a BOOST scholarship in the previous year, as well as their siblings.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship awards are provided directly to eligible students to help pay tuition at participating nonpublic schools. Award amounts depend on household income, academic level, and any financial assistance the school provides. The base scholarship amount and additional awards for special education students are determined by the BOOST Advisory Board. Scholarship checks are sent to the school, and the parent or guardian must sign the back of the check. The award may be reduced if it exceeds the tuition owed to the school. If tuition is $10,000 with a $4,000 school discount (making family responsibility $6,000), and the award is $7,750, it will be reduced to $6,000. If the student was not enrolled, did not attend school days, or withdraws/is expelled before April 30, 2027, the school must return the undeposited check or provide a prorated refund to MSDE.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Parent applications are due May 8, 2026, no later than 11:59 p.m. EDT. Nonpublic school applications are due March 6, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students entering kindergarten through 12th grade who qualify for free and reduced-price school meals and are enrolled or accepted at a participating nonpublic school. Siblings of current BOOST recipients receive priority consideration. Priority is also given to students who received a BOOST scholarship in the previous year.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and required fees for enrollment at participating nonpublic schools for grades kindergarten through 12. Funds may not be used for transportation or meals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Only nonpublic schools registered to operate in Maryland and approved to participate in the Nonpublic Textbook Program are eligible to participate. As of March 2026, 178 nonpublic schools across Maryland are participating.
requirements_list: Student must qualify for free and reduced-price meals (FARMs) based on household income compared to federal poverty level guidelines
Student must be enrolled or accepted at a participating nonpublic school for the 2026-2027 school year
Student must be entering grades kindergarten through 12th grade (pre-K students are not eligible)
Parents must upload their 2025 Federal 1040 tax returns to verify annual income and household size
Household income must meet FARMS income guidelines set by the U.S. Department of Agriculture
Nonpublic schools must hold a certificate of approval or be registered with the State Board of Education
Nonpublic schools must be approved to participate in the Nonpublic Textbook Program
Nonpublic schools must provide at least a 1st grade level program (not only pre-K and kindergarten)
Nonpublic schools must complete an online application to participate in the BOOST Scholarship Program

Nonpublic schools must comply with all reporting requirements by September 25, 2026, including: teacher certification data, student withdrawal/expulsion data, assessment results for English Language Arts, Mathematics, and Science in specified grade bands, and enrollment confirmation for BOOST students

Nonpublic schools must comply with Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and not discriminate in admissions, retention, or expulsion based on race, color, national origin, sexual orientation, or gender identity or expression

Awards are ranked by priority: (1st) Renewals and their siblings, (2nd) New applicants from public school qualifying for free meals, (3rd) New applicants from public school qualifying for reduced meals, (4th) Continuing nonpublic school students qualifying for free meals, (5th) Continuing nonpublic school students qualifying for reduced meals
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Parents complete an online BOOST Scholarship application through Submittable during the March 9 - May 8, 2026 application window and upload their 2025 Federal 1040 tax returns for income verification. Applications are reviewed for eligibility and completeness on a rolling basis. After May 30, 2026, all application data is compiled and ranked by household income as a percentage of the federal poverty index. The 7-member BOOST Advisory Board convenes in summer 2026 to determine base scholarship award amounts, additional awards for special education students, and other award criteria. Parents and guardians are notified by August 2026 via email of their award status and must accept or decline by the deadline provided. Participating nonpublic schools must confirm student enrollment for awarded applicants and provide copies of IEP, IFSP, or 504 plans for students receiving special education services. Once schools complete enrollment confirmation and required reporting, MSDE prepares scholarship checks at the Office of the Comptroller of Maryland. Scholarship checks are delivered to schools via FedEx between September and December 2026. No new awards are offered after December 11, 2026. MSDE offers customer service support sessions for parents on March 10, March 12 (with certified interpreter), and weekly Wednesdays from 12-1 pm (starting March 18, with interpreter available).

structured_extraction.program_description: USDA training grant that expands menu planning training for the Child and Adult Care Food Program to address meal pattern requirements, menu planning principles, creditable foods, standardized recipes, healthy food preparation, and culturally appropriate recipes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: USDA grant providing menu planning training covering meal pattern requirements, menu planning principles, creditable and non-creditable foods, standardized recipes, healthy food preparation methods, and culturally appropriate CACFP recipes. Also offers Feeding Infants in the CACFP training on infant feeding, breastfeeding, formula use, and safe food handling.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child and Adult Care Food Program participants
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Menu planning training, meal pattern training, infant feeding training, and technical assistance
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a CACFP participant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs for information about available training dates and participation

structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership with CVS Health and Community College of Baltimore County that prepares job seekers with disabilities to become Certified Pharmacy Technicians by taking the national Pharmacy Technician Certifying Board test. The program includes 14 weeks of classroom instruction, 6 weeks of clinical on-the-job training, and practice in a mock CVS pharmacy before externship in actual CVS locations. Pharmacy Technicians assist pharmacists in hospitals or retail pharmacies, serving customers, processing insurance claims, maintaining inventory and filling prescriptions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides 14 weeks of classroom instruction covering CVS programs and procedures, inventory management, and prescription medication measurements. Participants receive 6 weeks of clinical on-the-job training through an externship in CVS pharmacies throughout Maryland. Training is held at the DORS WTC location with externship placements in local community CVS pharmacies. Participants who complete the program and pass the national Pharmacy Technician Certifying Board (PTCB) test earn certification as a Certified Pharmacy Technician.
structured_extraction.contact_name: DORS Counselor or local DORS office
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with disabilities who meet age and educational requirements and are interested in becoming Certified Pharmacy Technicians.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training for pharmacy technician certification including 14 weeks of classroom instruction covering CVS programs and procedures, inventory management, and prescription medication measurements, mock pharmacy practice, and 6 weeks of on-the-job externship in CVS pharmacies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Externship placements occur in CVS pharmacies throughout Maryland in the job seeker's local community. Classroom training is held at DORS WTC locations.

Possess a High School Diploma or GED
Have desire to work in a retail environment and provide excellent customer service
Have 9th-grade reading comprehension level
Have 9th-grade math skills

structured_extraction.program_description: A job training program for people with disabilities interested in working in retail. Participants receive classroom instruction in a mock CVS store, hands-on learning activities at actual CVS locations, and a paid externship working in CVS stores throughout Maryland. The program includes customer service training and teaches skills like inventory management, cash register operation, and communication.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 10-week program consisting of classroom instruction in a mock CVS store, learning activities at CVS stores, and a paid externship in CVS stores throughout Maryland. Participants receive hands-on retail training at no cost. The program includes classroom instruction, learning activities at actual CVS locations, customer service training, and skill development in inventory tracking and stock rotation, phone and intercom etiquette, cash register skills, non-verbal communication, and other retail competencies. Upon completion, participants gain practical retail experience through paid externship opportunities at CVS stores throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with disabilities who are at least 16 years old and interested in working in retail.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and skill development in retail operations including inventory tracking and stock rotation, phone and intercom etiquette, customer service, cash register skills, non-verbal communication, and other competencies to prepare participants for employment in CVS stores and other retail positions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Offered at DORS WTC location and select locations throughout Maryland. Paid externship available in CVS stores throughout Maryland.

High school diploma preferred but not required
Desire to work in retail
6th-grade reading level minimum
Basic math skills and ability to use a calculator
Ability to follow simple written or oral instructions
Ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds and bend, stoop, and stand for long periods of time

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides financial support to child care providers for professional development, training, and career advancement activities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides financial assistance to child care providers for professional development and career advancement. Details available in the CCCPDF Brochure.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers in Maryland seeking to advance their careers through professional development and training.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional development, training, and career advancement activities for child care providers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a child care provider
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Division of Early Childhood. Refer to the CCCPDF Brochure for specific application instructions and requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tuition assistance program for child care providers to obtain a college education at participating colleges/universities in Maryland. Funding is available for child care providers to earn a college degree in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides tuition assistance payments made directly to participating colleges/universities. Awards can be used toward tuition, college fees, and textbooks for completion of a college degree in approved fields (Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education). Funds are awarded for one school year at a time with annual review. Upon graduation, participants must serve in a licensed Maryland child care facility for at least 20 hours per week for 2-4 years (depending on degree level) or repay the assistance.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: First-time Applications due by March 1st; Continuation Applications due by June 30th
structured_extraction.program_audience: Credentialed child care providers seeking to pursue a college degree while working in licensed child care facilities in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition, college fees, and textbooks for college degrees in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide availability across Maryland at participating colleges and universities

Work in a licensed child care center or be a registered family child care provider in Maryland and work at least 10 hours per week
Fulfill entrance requirements at the participating college of choice
Have at least one year of documented experience working with groups of children in an approved setting
Maintain employment in an approved child care facility in Maryland while participating in the program
Participate in professional development
Agree to complete service requirement of at least 20 hours per week in an approved child care facility in Maryland after completion of degree

Contact information for CCCPDF Coordinators at each college can be located at cccpdf.com.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides support to help child care providers achieve accreditation. The program is administered through regional offices across Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The fund provides financial support and technical assistance to help child care providers obtain and maintain accreditation. Support is available through regional offices located in Anne Arundel County, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, and Prince George's County.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for obtaining and maintaining child care accreditation

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A tuition assistance program for child care providers to earn a college degree from accredited colleges and universities in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education. The program supports child care professionals' career development and professional advancement while increasing the quality of care in Maryland child care programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding to support tuition, fees, and required textbooks for approved child care providers pursuing college degrees. A part-time CCCPDF Coordinator position (up to 25 hours per week for institutions with 20+ students) is also funded to administer the program. Indirect costs are capped at 10% of total funding. Funding amounts vary based on degree level and service commitment requirements: Associate degree requires 2 years of service, Bachelor's degree requires 4 years of service, and Master's degree requires 2.5 years of service (no more than 10% of total funding available for graduate degrees). Private colleges/universities funded at the tuition rate of the nearest public college/university.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 09, 2025, no later than 5:00 p.m. EDT
structured_extraction.program_audience: Accredited colleges and universities with early childhood programs or related fields serving Maryland early child care educators who participate in the Maryland Child Care Credential Program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition, fees, and required textbooks for approved child care provider participants pursuing degrees in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education. Partial funding for a CCCPDF Coordinator position at participating institutions to administer the program and manage student services. Indirect costs up to 10% of total funding.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through 24 participating Institutes of Higher Education (IHEs).

Participate in the Maryland Child Care Credential Program at Level 2 or higher
Currently work as a child care provider in a licensed child care center or be a registered family child care provider in Maryland working at least 10 hours per week

Have at least one year of documented experience working with groups of children in an approved setting
Maintain employment as a child care provider in a licensed childcare facility in Maryland while enrolled in college courses funded through this program

Maintain at least a 2.50 cumulative GPA from the point of first entering the program
Schedule a meeting with a college coordinator before completing an application

Completed proposals must be submitted by 5:00 p.m. EDT on June 09, 2025 via email to cccpdf.msde@maryland.gov. structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund (CCCPDF)

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Fund provides financial assistance to cover college tuition, fees, and required textbooks for degree completion. Funds are distributed directly to the participating college/university on an annual basis. Funding may continue if available and recipients continue to meet requirements. Recipients must commit to employment in child care for at least 20 hours per week during studies, and upon degree completion must work in the child care field full-time or part-time (minimum 20 hours per week) for 2 years (associate's degree), 4 years (bachelor's degree), or 2.5 years (master's degree). If the service commitment is not completed without good cause, recipients must repay all tuition, fees, and textbooks provided.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 1st for new applications; June 30th for continuation applications

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: College tuition, fees, and required textbooks for degree completion in early childhood education or related fields.

At least one year of child care experience
Current employment in an approved child care facility (child care center or family child care) for at least 20 hours per week

Professional development plan including courses and timeline to complete degree

structured_extraction.program_description: The Child Care Scholarship Program provides financial assistance to help eligible families afford child care services. As of May 1, 2025, the program has temporarily stopped issuing scholarships to new families due to reaching maximum budget capacity. The program has grown from serving approximately 21,000 children in January 2023 to over 45,000 children. Existing enrollees continue to receive support and new applications are still accepted and placed on a waitlist (frozen status list). Families receiving TANF, TCA, or SSI are exempt from the enrollment freeze and can receive scholarships immediately upon qualifying.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides scholarships to help families pay for child care services through approved providers. Scholarships are awarded based on eligibility criteria. As of May 1, 2025, new families who are eligible but not receiving TANF, TCA, or SSI are added to a frozen status list. Scholarships are awarded from this list as funding becomes available when children naturally leave the program (age out or no longer need care). Families receiving TANF, TCA, or SSI receive scholarships immediately upon qualifying and are not subject to the enrollment freeze. Payments are made directly to child care providers on behalf of enrolled families in advance of services rendered. Providers receive half the payment twice per month on the 15th and last day of each month. Scholarships are issued for a two-year period upon approval. Families currently enrolled continue to receive benefits without interruption provided they meet eligibility requirements and complete recertification on time. Scholarships cannot be backdated to cover care provided before official scholarship issuance.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a rolling basis; Fast-Track determinations within 3 business days; Full applications determined within 30 calendar days or 5 business days of receipt of all required documentation
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with low to moderate incomes who need financial assistance to pay for child care services. Priority given to families receiving TANF, TCA, or SSI benefits. Families must be Maryland residents who are working or employed, participating in an approved training program, or attending school.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The scholarships help families pay for child care services provided by licensed or approved informal child care providers. Child care must be for children younger than 13 who are not disabled, or individuals younger than 19 years old who are disabled.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Applicants must be Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Must meet income eligibility requirements per Child Care Scholarship Income Guidelines
Must be a Maryland resident
Must be working or employed, participating in an approved training program, or attending school
Must apply and be approved
If not receiving TANF, TCA, or SSI, applicant will be placed on frozen status list as of May 1, 2025
Families receiving TANF, TCA, or SSI are exempt from the enrollment freeze
