Must provide proof of identity for all household members
Parent and/or caregiver of a child younger than 13 who is not disabled, or an individual younger than 19 years old who is disabled
For Fast-Track applications: must provide Maryland residency, income, and activity documentation only

For Full applications: must provide comprehensive documentation including proof of address, proof of wages/salary, proof of other income, proof of activity, proof of citizenship or qualified alien status for children, and other supporting documents as applicable
Currently enrolled families must renew applications on time to continue receiving scholarships
Existing families can add children to current scholarships during freeze by completing Change of Circumstance form
Parents must not move outside of Maryland, gain income above continuing income scale, or gain $1,000,000 in assets to remain eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families can submit applications online at https://family.childcareportals.org at any time. Applications are available in English and Spanish. New customers can submit a Fast-Track application (requires Maryland residency, income, and activity documentation only) with eligibility determination within 3 business days. Fast-Track applicants are then prompted to submit a Full Application within 15 days. Full Applications are determined within 30 calendar days from submission or within 5 business days of receipt of all required documentation. If eligible and receiving TANF, TCA, or SSI, a scholarship is awarded immediately. If eligible but not receiving these benefits, the family is added to the frozen status list pending funding availability. Returning customers who have previously applied for Fast-Track can submit a New Scholarship Application. Families with current scholarships must complete a Redetermination Application 45 days before their scholarship end date to continue receiving benefits. Families receive notification through the Child Care Scholarship Portal or by email. Scholarships cannot be backdated; families must wait until officially issued to begin care and receive payment. Providers have 5 business days to approve or deny pending scholarship requests.

structured_extraction.program_description: The state provides payments in advance to child care providers based on enrollment rather than paying retroactively. The advance payment is calculated using the number of children listed on a provider's invoice by the last Saturday of each month, and is divided into two payments per month—one on the 15th and one on the 30th (or last day of the month). Payment includes allowances for absences up to 60 days per calendar year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Child care providers enrolled in the Child Care Scholarship program receive monthly advance payments split into two installments—one on the 15th and one on the last day of each month. The advance payment amount is based on enrollment of children with active scholarships as of the last Saturday of the previous month (Advance Payment Snapshot). The monthly amount is calculated by taking the weekly scholarship amount, dividing by five to determine the daily rate, then multiplying by the number of payable days for that month (ranging from 20–23 days per month). Providers receive payment for enrolled children even if they are absent, provided absences do not exceed 60 days in a calendar year (medical waivers may apply). For informal providers, absences and holidays are not paid. Payment continues for the full month regardless of attendance days. Adjustments (called True-Up) occur in the reconciliation month (fourth month onwards) to account for children enrolled after the advance payment calculation, scholarships that ended early, mid-month voucher assignments, EXCELS participation changes, or provider ineligibility. True-Up reconciliation dates vary by month and the process now accounts for changes during the prior three months. Providers must submit signed invoices with attendance documentation within 60 days of the end of the service period; failure to submit invoices results in required repayment of funds and potential overpayment establishment. Payment is processed by MSDE on the 15th and last day of each month, with providers typically receiving funds via direct deposit around the 6th and 21st of each month. Maryland EXCELS Tier Payments are added to advance payments based on provider quality rating. Registered Family Home Providers who are SEIU members continue to have union dues and COPE deducted from advance payments. Invoice Detail Reports are provided showing any adjustments broken down by month.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Child Care Scholarship Central 2 (Justin Dayhoff, Assistant State Superintendent)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care providers, regulated family child care home providers, large family child care home providers, and regulated informal child care providers enrolled in Maryland's Child Care Scholarship program who have children with active scholarships on their invoices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Advance payments are subsidies provided directly to child care providers to support their ongoing operations and cover the cost of child care services provided to children with active scholarships. Providers must submit invoices to document services provided and must comply with program integrity audits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Providers must be licensed, regulated, or informal child care providers approved by MSDE to operate as a child care provider
Providers must have an active Child Care Scholarship enrollment

Children must appear on the provider's invoice and have active receipted CCS program scholarship vouchers assigned to the provider as of the last Saturday of each month to be included in that month's advance payment
Providers must submit signed invoices for each monthly service period
Invoices must be submitted within 60 days of the end of the service period
Failure to submit an invoice or late submission results in failing the Program Integrity Audit and requiring repayment of all funds for that service period
For children with absences to be paid, absence days must not exceed 60 days in a calendar year (medical waivers may apply)
Informal providers are not paid for absences and holidays; overpayments are established when absences are reported

EXCELS participation is a requirement for CCS program participation; if EXCELS participation ends mid-month, payment will not be included for dates after EXCELS expiration unless renewed before payment calculation
Providers must register and maintain an account in the Child Care Provider Portal at https://provider.childcareportals.org
Providers must comply with program integrity audits and attendance verification audits
Customers must validate attendance within 15 calendar days of receiving validation alerts
Providers must upload relevant Sign-In/Sign-Out sheets within 10 business days of receiving an attendance dispute notification
Registration fees, union dues, and recoupments are reconciled and adjusted in subsequent months
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Child care providers register through the Child Care Provider Portal at https://provider.childcareportals.org by completing the User Registration Form with required information including first name, last name, date of birth, gender, email, phone number, and preferred language. Providers must verify their email and create a password meeting security requirements (12 characters with uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character). Once registered, providers submit invoices and attendance records after each monthly service period through the Attendance & Invoicing tab. Enrollment-based advance payment calculations are made using the Advance Payment Snapshot (last Saturday of each month). Two equal monthly payments are issued on the 15th and last day of each month; providers typically receive direct deposit funds around the 6th and 21st of each month. MSDE sends individual notification emails at the start of each month showing the enrollment calculation, unadjusted monthly amount, additional amounts from late-receipted vouchers, offsets for scholarships that ended, and the final total monthly amount. Detailed Invoice Detail Reports are provided the next business day after the State Comptroller's Office processes each payment. True-Up reconciliations occur starting in the fourth month (April for January enrollments) and onward each month, with reconciliation dates varying by month as specified in the 2025 CCS Advance Payment Schedule. Providers can submit customer service requests through the Provider Inquiry Link on the MSDE website or contact CCS Central 2; issues are addressed within 3 business days. Disputes regarding advance payments or true-up calculations may be submitted within 90 days of payment receipt. For repayment disputes or Program Integrity Audit results, providers may submit an informal appeal through the Provider Portal within 90 days. Families apply for child care scholarships online at https://family.childcareportals.org.

structured_extraction.program_description: The program helps eligible Maryland families pay for high-quality child care and early education programs. Families can receive a temporary 60-day scholarship while their full application is processed, or a full 52-week scholarship to cover part of their child care costs. The scholarship can be used at Maryland registered family homes, licensed child care centers, or informal care providers. The program serves approximately 37,000 children, 25,000 parents, and 3,500 early care and educational programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides scholarships that cover part of child care costs at participating Maryland EXCELS program providers. The scholarship amount represents the portion the State pays toward child care expenses. Families are responsible for paying a State-assigned co-payment (ranging from $0 to $3 per week) and any costs not covered by the scholarship. Families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) have a $0 co-payment. The temporary scholarship covers 60 days of child care while the full application is processed. The full scholarship covers 52 weeks of child care services. Advance payments are calculated on the last Friday of each month for the upcoming advance payment if the provider has submitted all required forms at least 5 days before the last Friday of the month. The Child Care Scholarship Program completes payment processing for advance payment by the 1st and 15th of each month. Providers receiving payment by direct deposit can anticipate payment from the Comptroller's Office within 7 days after the completion of payment processing.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: As of May 1, 2025, the program is temporarily not issuing scholarships to new families
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible Maryland families with children younger than 13 years old, or individuals 13-19 years old with a qualifying disability, who are working, in an approved training program, or attending school. Maryland residents including emancipated minors and migrant workers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Child care and early education program expenses, including before and after school child care at Maryland registered family homes, licensed child care centers, or informal care providers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residents
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident who is working, in an approved training program, or attending school
For families where both parents live in the same household, both parents must meet all eligibility requirements

Must be a recipient of Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI), or have family income below the Child Care Scholarship income guidelines (varies by family size; for new applications ranges from $76,117 for family of 2 to $167,904 for family of 12)
Must be willing to have child immunized to Maryland state standards or provide documentation supporting exemption from immunization
Must provide proof that each child needing child care is a citizen of the United States or a qualified alien, or proof of Head Start enrollment
Must provide proof of identity for all household members
Must provide a photo ID (head of household only)
For full scholarship, must submit four weeks of consecutive pay stubs or employer letter describing work schedule and gross salary
For employment income, must provide most recent four weeks of consecutive pay stubs (4 weekly, 2 bi-weekly, or 1 monthly)
Must submit proof of training or school attendance with days and hours of activity on employer or school letterhead
Must submit proof of address such as utility bill, lease, rental agreement, or mortgage statement
Must provide proof of home address that matches the Child Care Scholarship application

If receiving other income (alimony, armed services pay, Social Security, SSI, self-employment, TCA, tips/commission, unemployment benefits, veterans assistance, workers compensation), must provide documentation
If receiving SNAP, WIC, TCA, WAG, GBI, or housing assistance, must provide eligibility statement and/or housing voucher receipt

For proof of identity, must provide government-issued document for all adult household members; applicant and co-applicant must provide photo ID; other household members not requesting child care must provide birth certificate to document proof of relationship
For children, birth certificate or immigration status documentation can serve as proof of identity
For migrant workers, must provide documentation from employer verifying employment status
For those experiencing homelessness, must provide letter on agency letterhead or documents confirming level of homelessness
For emancipated minors, must provide documentation verifying financial responsibility for self and decision-making as adult
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Register for an account at the Child Care Scholarship Family Portal at https://family.childcareportals.org or https://family.childcareportals.org/s/?language=es (Spanish version). Step 2: Complete the fast-track online scholarship application and submit documentation including proof of employment or enrollment in training/school, proof of residency, and proof of income. Step 3: The fast-track application is processed within three business days by CCS Central 2. Step 4: If eligible, a temporary 60-day scholarship is issued while your full application is processed. Provide additional information and documentation within 15 days to be considered for a 52-week scholarship. All eligibility and income documentation must be received and verified to make a determination for benefits; the full application process may take up to 30 days. Step 5: Once approved for the full scholarship, take the signed scholarship agreement to a participating Maryland EXCELS program provider and begin receiving services. For questions or assistance during the process, contact CCS Central 2 through the Provider Inquiry Link on Money4ChildCare.com or submit questions online through the portal. Open office hours with Child Care Scholarship team representatives are held monthly from 12:00 to 1:00 PM.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Child Care Scholarship (CCS) program helps eligible families in Maryland pay for high-quality child care and early education programs. The program provides financial assistance to cover part of child care costs through scholarships issued by CCS Central 2. The program serves approximately 37,000 children, 25,000 parents, and 3,500 early care and educational programs across Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible families receive payment scholarships from CCS Central 2 to cover part of their child care costs. The scholarship shows the state-paid portion (scholarship rate) and the family co-payment amount. Three types of scholarships are available: a temporary 60-day scholarship, a full formal 52-week scholarship, and an informal scholarship for relative care. Families eligible for Temporary Cash Assistance or Supplemental Security Income have a $0 co-payment. Co-payments range from $0 to $3 per week and decrease for families receiving scholarships for multiple children. Parents are responsible for any remaining tuition beyond the scholarship amount and co-payment. Advance payments are made twice monthly (15th and last day of month) to providers by direct deposit or check. Scholarships can be used for Maryland registered family homes, Maryland licensed child care centers, relatives providing care in the relative's or child's home, and non-relatives providing care in the child's home. Scholarships also cover before and after school child care.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No specific deadline; ongoing enrollment (temporarily halted as of May 1, 2025 for new families)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible families in Maryland with children younger than 13 or individuals ages 13-19 with qualifying disabilities who need child care assistance. Parents must be working/employed, in an approved training program, or attending school.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Scholarships can be used to pay for child care provided by Maryland registered family homes, Maryland licensed child care centers, relatives in the relative's home or child's home (informal providers), and non-relatives in the child's home (informal providers). Scholarships can also be used for before and after school child care. For non-school-age children in informal care, proof of immunization to Maryland state standards or exemption documentation is required.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is available statewide in Maryland. Families must be Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident who is working/employed, in an approved training program, or attending school
For families where both parents live in the same household, both parents must meet all eligibility requirements
Must be a recipient of Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) or have income within CCS income guidelines
Must be willing to have child immunized to Maryland state standards or provide documentation of exemption
Must provide proof that each child needing child care is a citizen of the United States or qualified alien
Must provide proof of identity for all household members
Must provide photo ID from head of household
Child must be younger than 13 years old or ages 13-19 with a qualifying disability
Parents are not required to be US citizens
Must provide proof of residency (utility bill, lease, mortgage statement, or Maryland driver's license)
For employed household members, must provide most recent four weeks of consecutive pay stubs
For household members in school or training, must provide current school/training schedule on school letterhead
Must provide documentation of all other income sources (alimony, Social Security, SSI, self-employment, TCA, unemployment, veterans benefits, workers compensation)

For self-employed applicants, must provide previous year's tax return (if after April 15) or profit and loss statements for past three months (if before April 15 or business is new) plus completed Self-Employment Attestation Statement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Register for an account at the Child Care Scholarship Family Portal (https://family.childcareportals.org). Step 2: Complete a Fast-Track Scholarship application online and submit required documents: proof of employment or training/school enrollment, proof of residency, and proof of income. Step 3: Your Fast-Track application is processed within 3 business days by CCS Central 2. Step 4: If eligible, you receive a temporary 60-day scholarship to cover child care costs while your full application is processed. Step 5: Submit additional information and documentation within 15 days to determine eligibility for a full 52-week scholarship. Full applications are processed within 30 calendar days from submission or within 5 business days of receipt of all required documentation. If approved, a two-year scholarship is issued. Step 6: 45 days before your current eligibility period ends, you must complete a Redetermination application to continue receiving benefits. Upon approval, a new two-year scholarship is issued. Families can contact CCS Central 2 at 1-877-227-0125 or use the online portal's Message Center for assistance. Open office hours are held monthly from 12:00-1:00 PM on dates listed in the CCS Open Office Hours schedule.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program funded through the American Rescue Plan Act to provide financial stabilization support to child care providers. Grants were distributed to licensed child care providers in Maryland to help stabilize operations during the COVID-19 pandemic.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants calculated at $15,000 base amount plus $300 per licensed slot. Funds could be used for: staffing costs; rent/mortgage, utilities, facilities, maintenance, and insurance; personal protective equipment and cleaning; equipment and supplies; goods and services; mental health services; and payment of past expenses. Child care providers were required to provide relief on co-payments and tuition to families to the maximum extent possible, prioritizing relief for families struggling to pay. All grants were subject to taxation and reported on Form 1099-G for amounts over $600.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 4:00 PM Eastern Time on August 6, 2021
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care providers in Maryland who were licensed by March 11, 2021
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Staffing costs and employee benefits (wages, health insurance, retirement); rent/mortgage, utilities, facilities maintenance and insurance; personal protective equipment and cleaning supplies; equipment and supplies; goods and services necessary for operations; mental health services; payment of past expenses; and other operational costs to maintain and stabilize child care services during the pandemic.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Available to all counties in Maryland. Eligible providers were those licensed by the Maryland State Department of Education as of March 11, 2021.
requirements_list: Licensed by Maryland State Department of Education by March 11, 2021

Either open and providing child care services on date of application submission, OR temporarily closed due to public health, financial hardship, or other COVID-19 related reasons but committed to reopening by September 1, 2021
Must maintain a W-9 form on file
Must follow state and local health and safety guidance and CDC guidelines for child care to the maximum extent possible
Must pay employees at least the same weekly wage with same benefits throughout the grant period; no mandatory furloughs allowed

Must provide relief on co-payments and tuition to enrolled families to the maximum extent possible, with priority for families struggling to pay and targeting families at or below 85% of state median income
Must submit data and documentation demonstrating use of grant funds by March 1, 2022
Must comply with all audit requests
Maintain financial records for 5 years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible child care providers submitted applications online through the Maryland State Department of Education's system. Applications required: name and contact information of facility director/family child care provider; official program name as listed on license; license number; license issuance date; copy of license or registration certificate or letter of substantial compliance; provider ID; type of program; demographic information on director/owner; facility address and mailing address; number of licensed slots; current operating capacity; estimated monthly operational costs by category; intended use of funds; and certification statements regarding operations status and compliance with program requirements. Providers could submit a change form to modify applications until August 1, 2021. Applications received were verified and processed after the August 6, 2021 deadline. Grants were distributed beginning after August 6, 2021, with completion expected by September 30, 2021. Providers enrolling in direct deposit received funds faster than those receiving checks by mail. All grant funds were required to be distributed to providers by January 31, 2022.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides reimbursement rates for child care providers serving eligible families.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program establishes reimbursement rates for child care providers based on market rate survey results. Reimbursement rates vary by region, provider type (family child care or center-based), and age group served (infant, 2-4 years, five plus years). Rates are calculated at various percentiles (24th, 30th, 45th, 60th, 75th, and median) of the market rate survey data. Regional rate schedules detail specific reimbursement amounts for each percentile level and provider category.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers and families eligible for child care subsidy assistance
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Child care services and reimbursement for providers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide, with regional variations. Report includes rates for: Region U (Cecil, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Talbot, Washington Counties), Region V (Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Somerset, Wicomico Counties), and Region W (Anne Arundel, Calvert, Carroll, Charles, Prince George's Counties)

structured_extraction.program_description: A program designed to ensure quality of professional development offered to child care professionals in Maryland. The program approves individuals and organizations to provide training in accordance with Maryland regulations. It ensures child care professionals have access to quality training opportunities by conducting statewide review, approval, renewal, and monitoring of trainers and training proposals for birth through age 8.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides statewide review, approval, renewal, and monitoring of trainers and training proposals for Core of Knowledge, Pre-Service, and Continued training. Technical assistance is provided to applicants and approved trainers, and quarterly trainer meetings are facilitated.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and organizations providing professional development training to child care professionals in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional development training for child care professionals
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Applicants must meet requirements identified in COMAR 13A.14.08
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals and organizations apply for approval as trainers. Applications are reviewed, and applicants receive technical assistance throughout the process.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Child Care and Development Fund helps low-income families pay for child care so they can work or attend training and education programs. The program also improves the quality of child care and coordinates services among early childhood development and afterschool programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides subsidies to help low-income families afford child care services. The Child Care and Development Fund made available $5.2 billion to states, territories, and tribes in Fiscal Year 2012.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income families who need child care to work or attend training or education programs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment for child care services to allow parents to work or attend training and education programs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Low-income family status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested parties can review the Child Care and Development Fund plan and provide comments through public hearings or written submissions.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Child Care and Development Fund helps low-income families pay for child care so they can work or attend training and education programs. The program also improves the quality of child care services and encourages coordination among early childhood development and afterschool programs.

In Fiscal Year 2012, CCDF made available $5.2 billion to states, territories, and tribes.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child and Adult Care Food Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides child care food subsidies for low-income families. Child care centers that participate in the program can receive reimbursement for food costs to help address childhood hunger and support child development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Child care centers receive reimbursement for food costs. The program provides subsidies to support nutrition for low-income families using child care services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care centers serving low-income families
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Food costs and nutrition reimbursement for child care programs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must operate as a licensed or compliant child care center
Must participate in the program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland State Department of Education's School and Community Nutrition Programs Branch for application information and enrollment procedures.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal nutrition program that provides meals and snacks to children in child care settings and helps child care providers offer nutritious food to the children in their care.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides reimbursement to child care providers for nutritious meals and snacks served to eligible children in their care.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers and children in licensed child care settings
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Nutritious meals and snacks for children in child care
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide availability across Maryland

structured_extraction.program_name: Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) Training
structured_extraction.program_description: Training programs for child care centers, adult day care centers, family child care sponsors, and at-risk afterschool programs covering CACFP administration, meal patterns, and compliance with USDA regulations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly orientation training for new CACFP operators and staff; required annual administrative training for established CACFP programs covering USDA regulations, guidance, professional development, meal planning, and food safety.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and technical assistance in CACFP administration, meal patterns, food safety, menu planning, and compliance
requirements_list: Must participate in CACFP
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Enroll in required monthly orientation training for new program operators or staff, or required annual administrative training for established programs

structured_extraction.program_description: A meal service option that allows schools and school districts in low-income areas to serve breakfast and lunch at no cost to enrolled students without collecting household income applications. The program promotes equity and access to nutritious meals during the school day, ensuring all students have access to balanced meals regardless of family income.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Schools and school districts with an Identified Student Percentage (ISP) of 25% or higher are eligible to elect CEP. Identified students are those directly certified for free meals based on participation in programs such as the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) and Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF). Eligible schools receive federal reimbursement to serve breakfast and lunch at no cost to all enrolled students without requiring household income documentation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students in low-income schools and school districts, families, and schools and school districts eligible under the CEP criteria in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Meal service provision (breakfast and lunch) for enrolled students at no cost
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Schools and school districts in low-income areas of Maryland with an Identified Student Percentage of 25% or higher
requirements_list: School or school district must have an Identified Student Percentage (ISP) of 25% or higher
Identified students are those directly certified for free meals based on participation in SNAP, TANF, or similar programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools and school districts with an ISP of 25% or higher are eligible to elect CEP. Schools can apply through the Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs. Specific application procedures are not fully detailed on this page.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that requires local education agencies identified as having disproportionate identification of students by race or ethnicity in special education, placement, or discipline to reserve 15 percent of IDEA Part B funds to implement proactive and responsive actions addressing root causes of over-identification. The program funds educational and behavioral evaluations, services, support including evidence-based literacy instruction, professional development, and systemic change efforts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Local education agencies identified by the state as having significant disproportionality in identification, placement, or discipline of students by race or ethnicity must reserve 15 percent of their IDEA Part B Section 611 and Section 619 funds to implement comprehensive coordinated early intervening services. Funds support educational and behavioral evaluations, services and support including evidence-based literacy instruction, professional development, coaching, consultation, data systems development, and implementation of systemic changes to address root causes of over-identification. Allowable expenditures include salaries for coaches, mentors, general education teachers, guidance counselors, psychologists, RTI/MTSS coordinators, social workers, substitute teachers, and extended contracts for staff; professional development services; instructional materials and software for academic or behavioral interventions; computers and devices for intervention delivery; travel for professional development; tutoring services; and other implementation costs. Unallowable costs include special education evaluations for eligibility determination, universal screening, student transportation, furniture, office equipment, occupancy costs, and alternative programming that replaces core curriculum.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Gary W. Richardson, MBA (Branch Chief); Demetria White (Interagency Specialist)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local education agencies identified as having significant racial or ethnic disproportionality in special education identification, placement, or discipline
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational and behavioral evaluations, services and support, evidence-based literacy instruction, professional development and coaching, consultation, staff performance evaluation, data systems supporting decision making, implementation drivers including staffing and training, systemic organizational change efforts to address root causes of over-identification, academic and behavioral interventions for struggling students in Tier 2 and Tier 3 supports, review and adjustment of policies and procedures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland local education agencies identified by the state as having significant disproportionality in special education identification, placement, or discipline based on a risk ratio greater than 2.0 for two or more consecutive years in one or more of the noted categories
requirements_list: Must be identified by the state as having significant disproportionality over-identification based on race or ethnicity

Must have a risk ratio greater than 2.0 for two or more consecutive years in identification of children with disabilities, placement in educational settings, or incidence/duration/type of disciplinary actions
Must establish a local implementation team and diverse stakeholder group
Must engage in self-assessment and data review to determine root cause factors
Must develop plans addressing factors contributing to significant disproportionality
Must address and review policies, practices, or procedures identified as contributing to over-identification
Must implement results-based and job-embedded professional learning experiences
Must develop a comprehensive evaluation system emphasizing implementation fidelity and measurable student outcomes
Must align expenditures with specific actions to mitigate root cause factors

Must conduct self-assessment using one of the state-recommended tools (IDEA Data Center Equity Rubric, Root Causes of Disparities in School Discipline guide, or Assessing and Improving Special Education Program Review Tool)
Must reserve 15% of combined Part B 611 and Part B 619 funds for CCEIS activities
Must submit required fiscal documents including MSDE Grant Budget C-1-25 and Budget Detail Forms
Must maintain non-supplant status of funds used
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local education agencies identified as having significant disproportionality submit a comprehensive coordinated early intervening services plan using the state template. The plan must include: identification of the local education agency implementation team; data on categories of analysis (identification, placement, disciplinary removals); a self-assessment process and root cause analysis using a state-recommended tool; planned response actions (PRAs) addressing each area of disproportionality including policy/procedure reviews, academic/behavioral interventions, and professional learning; measurable goals and interim benchmarks with data sources; and a detailed budget using fiscal forms. Required fiscal documents include the MSDE Grant Budget C-1-25, separate Budget Detail Form for each C-1-25, and documentation of allowable costs aligned to the CCEIS Allowable Costs guidance. For programmatic or fiscal changes, LEAs submit amendment requests using the CCEIS Plan Programmatic Amendment Template. Progress reports are submitted at interim periods (due January 31 for reports ending September 30 or December 31) and final reporting (due November 30), documenting intervening supports provided, number of students served, and progress monitoring data for each PRA. Grant amendment requests are due by August 15.

structured_extraction.program_description: Consultation and support services for people with disabilities interested in exploring, accessing, and participating in registered apprenticeship programs across Maryland. Services include assessments, exploration of apprenticeship opportunities, academic instruction, and ongoing support throughout the apprenticeship journey.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DORS provides multiple support services including Apprenticeship Consult (one-on-one coordination to identify opportunities), Apprenticeship Academic Assessment (testing to determine current academic levels and eligibility), Apprenticeship Exploration (in-depth review of various apprenticeship opportunities), Apprenticeship Academic Instruction (help raising academic levels or preparing for testing), Apprenticeship Pre-Apprenticeship Support (assistance for those pursuing pre-apprenticeship programs), Apprenticeship Registered Apprenticeship Support (ongoing support for those in registered apprenticeships), and Apprenticeship Youth Apprenticeship Support (tracking and support for youth apprentices with transition assistance to registered apprenticeships). All services are provided by an Apprenticeship Coordinator and Academic Instructor. Registered apprenticeships are paid jobs where apprentices earn while learning, receive training from skilled craftspeople, and participate in related classroom instruction with a progressive pay scale. Apprentices are sponsored by employers or associations and hired directly.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Marylanders with disabilities interested in pursuing apprenticeships
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services to support individuals in preparing for and participating in registered apprenticeship programs, including academic assessment, instruction, and ongoing coordination and support. Apprentices earn while working and receive classroom instruction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout the state of Maryland
requirements_list: Applicant must have a disability
Applicant must be a DORS consumer or eligible for DORS services
Applicant must be interested in pursuing or participating in an apprenticeship opportunity
Must be at least 18 years of age
Must have a high school diploma (by high school graduation, GED, or NEDP)
Must be physically able to perform required tasks
Must be drug free
Must have transportation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals should contact the Apprenticeship Coordinator to begin the process. The coordinator will work with the individual to identify apprenticeship opportunities and determine what assessment and support services are needed. Depending on needs, individuals may receive academic assessments, exploration services, or direct support for pre-apprenticeship or registered apprenticeship programs. For available apprenticeship occupations, visit occupations.mdapprenticeship.com or call (410) 767-2246 or email info@mdapprenticeship.com to connect with an apprenticeship navigator. Applicants then apply directly to the program sponsor or employer.

structured_extraction.program_description: Specialized services tailored for individuals who are deaf-blind that provide supports to help them integrate into society and find competitive employment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Program provides specialized supports and services designed specifically for individuals who are deaf-blind to help them integrate into society and achieve competitive employment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who are deaf-blind.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Specialized supports and services for integration into society and career placement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through DORS offices.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides funding to expand prekindergarten services and increase access to quality early childhood education programs. The program supports the expansion of full-day prekindergarten slots (at least 6.5 hours of instruction, 180 school days per year) for three-year-old and four-year-old children, with funding of $14,473 per full-day prekindergarten slot.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded to eligible organizations at a rate of $14,473 per full-day prekindergarten slot to expand prekindergarten programs and services. Applicants request funding based on the number of full-day slots they plan to provide. New applicants must complete the full application in its entirety. Current grantees expanding existing programs with a track record of success may submit a modified short form application. The modified short form requires a minimum score of 35 (compared to full application minimum of 70), and MSDE will return an award determination within 30 days of submission for short form applications. A 15% advancement of the grant award amount may be issued upon request with supporting receipts required. Tuition may not be charged for the 6.5-hour day; tuition may only be charged for additional wrap-around services when applicable.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations seeking to expand prekindergarten services in Maryland, including local education agencies (LEAs), child care centers, family child care providers, and Head Start programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Expanding prekindergarten programs and increasing access to quality early childhood education. Funds may be used for salaries and wages, contracted services, supplies and materials, equipment, indirect costs, and other necessary program expenses. The grant budget may not be directed to tuition only.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. All counties are eligible.
requirements_list: Programs must provide a full day of instruction (at least 6.5 hours), 180 school days per year

Lead teachers must meet one of the following: bachelor's degree in early childhood education, child development, or related field; bachelor's degree from another country verified as equivalent to U.S. degree; bachelor's degree in an unrelated field with experience or qualifications in early childhood education; or 10 years of experience as of July 1, 2024 (with CLASS assessment and requirement to earn associate degree by July 1, 2030)

Assistant teachers must have a high school diploma or at least 5 years of documented experience as a teaching assistant in publicly funded prekindergarten for at least 20 hours per week and 180 days per year
Programs must have a published Maryland EXCELS rating of Level 3 or higher at time of application
Classrooms with more than 10 children must be staffed with both a lead teacher and an assistant teacher
Programs must implement an evidence-based curriculum aligned with Maryland Early Learning Standards in early language and literacy, science of reading, early mathematics, and social foundations
Professional learning activities must consist of 15 total hours supporting school readiness and high quality instruction
Programs must provide screening and referral services covering vision, hearing, speech and language, health, and physical development
Programs must offer or coordinate additional support services for families including parenting support, physical and mental health services, and early intervention for children with disabilities
Programs must maintain a comprehensive family engagement plan in accordance with Maryland Early Childhood Family Engagement Framework

Local Education Agencies receiving Blueprint funding and Prekindergarten Expansion Grants in FY26 must increase the number of three-year-old and four-year-old children served over September 30, 2024 enrollment
85% of approved slots must be filled by December 31st or award amount may decrease

Documentation of family income eligibility according to Federal Poverty Guidelines (students with disabilities, students experiencing homelessness, and multilingual learners are eligible regardless of income)
An instructional oversight person must be designated and dedicate a minimum of 8-10 hours per month to this task and cannot be a director teaching full-time
Montessori teachers may be certified by Association Montessori International (AMI), American Montessori Society (AMS), or Montessori Accreditation Council for Teacher Education
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations must complete and submit the FY2026 Prekindergarten Expansion Grant Application electronically using the Qualtrics online portal at https://msde.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_1MnGBHUOhXRWNKK. New applicants must complete the full application in its entirety. Current grantees with a track record of success expanding existing programs may submit a modified short form application (meeting criteria scores range from 4-7 for a minimum total of 35 points). The application autosaves automatically and applicants can use back and next buttons to edit pages (except the cover page). Prior to submission, applicants will be directed to review their entire application and can save it to return later. All required appendices must be uploaded with the application. Questions should be directed to prekexpansiongrant.msde@maryland.gov with subject "Pre-K Expansion Application". Applicants must include: Applicant Information, Maryland EXCELS and Accreditation Status, Extent of Need, Evidence of Impact, Goals and Outcomes, Plan of Operation, Evaluation and Dissemination, Staffing/Management/Key Personnel, Project Timeline, Collaboration and Sustainability, and Budget with Budget Narrative. Required appendices include: Works Cited, Documentation of family income eligibility policy, resumes of key personnel (excluding teachers), evidence of lead teacher qualifications, evidence of assistant teacher credentials, evidence of published Maryland EXCELS rating, valid child care license (if applicable), accreditation certificate (if applicable), signed C-1-25 MSDE budget form, and signed recipient assurances page. Head Start applicants must also submit a letter of support from the Head Start Program-funded grantee if the applicant is not the funded grantee.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides funding to support the expansion of high-quality prekindergarten programs in Maryland. The program broadsens availability and expands access to high-quality prekindergarten educational programming and school readiness services for three-year-old and four-year-old students from families with household incomes up to 300% of Federal Poverty Level (FPL).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding up to $19,950 per full-day prekindergarten slot for three-year-old and four-year-old children. Total funding available: $26,644,000 with an estimated average grant amount of $400,000 and an estimated 50 grants. Grant period: July 1, 2026-June 30, 2027. Minimum instructional year of 180 days required. Funds may be used for salaries and wages for teaching staff, equipment and materials, supplies, reasonable rental/mortgage and utility costs, technology costs (not exceeding 10% of total request), accreditation costs, screening and intervention services, evaluation and monitoring (not exceeding 5%), indirect costs (not exceeding 15% for nonprofits and 10% for others), meals meeting CACFP requirements, academic field trips, and professional learning activities. Funds may not be used for supplanting existing program funds, capital improvements, costs prior to grant approval, or transportation (except field trips).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 11, 2026, No later than 5:00 p.m. EDT (Amended on March 6, 2026)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Education Agencies (LEAs), qualified vendors, private providers (including Head Start, center-based, and family child care programs), and school districts seeking to expand or renew prekindergarten programs for income-eligible families
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Expansion and support of high-quality prekindergarten programs including instructional staff salaries, materials and curriculum resources aligned to Maryland Early Learning Standards, classroom equipment and furnishings, professional learning for instructional staff, health screenings and referrals, family engagement supports, quality improvement initiatives, and comprehensive services for children and families.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties are eligible. Programs must operate in Maryland and participate in the Maryland EXCELS program.
requirements_list: Must hold a valid license or registration issued by the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) if applicable
Must meet Maryland EXCELS rating requirement (Level 3 or higher for private providers; Level 4 or higher for public providers)
Must be a Local Education Agency (LEA), qualified vendor, or private provider including Head Start programs
Must comply with grant recipient assurances
Must follow professional salary schedules aligned with local education agencies
Must provide a full-day program with a minimum instructional day of at least 6.5 hours for 180 school days per year

Must employ qualified lead teachers: holding a State P-3 certification, bachelor's degree in early childhood education/related field, or meeting alternative pathway requirements including CLASS assessment minimums
For classrooms with more than 10 students, must employ an Assistant Teacher with high school diploma
Must use evidence-based curriculum aligned with Maryland Early Learning Standards and Maryland College and Career Ready Standards
Must implement valid and reliable child assessment tools to monitor progress
Must provide health screenings and referrals for vision, hearing, speech and language, general health, and physical development
Must maintain a child-to-instructional staff ratio of no more than 10 to 1
Must conduct CLASS assessments to monitor instructional quality
Must provide or coordinate family engagement, support services, and referrals
Must complete income verification for families using Federal Poverty Guidelines (300% FPL)
Must identify and serve students with disabilities, students experiencing homelessness, and multilingual learners
Must develop measurable SMART goals addressing standards alignment, instructional practice, quality improvement, and child outcomes
Must provide minimum 20 hours of annual professional learning for instructional staff aligned with Blueprint priorities
Must demonstrate a plan for long-term sustainability and community/business partnerships
Must submit required appendices including works cited, income eligibility documentation, and resumes of key personnel
Must have qualified individual responsible for instructional oversight with bachelor's degree or higher in early childhood education and early childhood experience
Must hire lead teachers by July 1, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit applications electronically through Qualtrics by March 11, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. EDT. Applications begin with eligibility questions confirming basic requirements. Based on responses, applicants are directed to either a full application (for new applicants and existing grantees without a track record of success) or a modified short form application (for existing grantees with documented track record of success including maintained lead teachers meeting grant requirements, maintained Maryland EXCELS Level 3 or higher, remained in compliance, not under corrective action, and filled majority of seats 85% by December 31, 2025). The full application consists of 10 sections: (1) Program Eligibility - Maryland EXCELS and Accreditation, (2) Evidence of Need/Market Analysis, (3) Measurable Goals, (4) Program Quality and Curriculum, (5) Plan of Operation, (6) Staffing, Key Personnel, and Management Plan, (7) Project Timeline/Implementation Plan, (8) Collaboration and Sustainability, (9) Fiscal Systems and Controls, and (10) Budget and Budget Narrative. The modified short form includes only required sections marked in the application. Applicants complete the electronic application, ensuring all required appendices are uploaded. Before submitting, applicants have opportunity to review answers and download responses. Full applications require minimum 80 points; modified short form applications require minimum 45 points. Questions should be directed to prekexpansiongrant.msde@maryland.gov with subject line 'Pre-K Expansion Application.' Refer to Grant Information Guide for technical assistance sessions and office hours information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Family Child Care Provider Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that helps registered family child care providers offset some of the costs of opening their child care programs. Provides a one-time direct grant award of up to $1,000 for eligible family child care providers, reimbursing approved items and expenses related to child care operations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grant award of up to $1,000 to eligible registered family child care providers. Funds are provided as reimbursement for approved items and expenses related to child care operations. Applicants submit receipts for items to be considered for reimbursement. Receipts must include vendor name, date of purchase, item description, and amount paid.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered family child care providers in Maryland planning to open or operating child care programs. Providers with combined annual family income at or below 60% of State Median Income (SMI) are eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for items and expenses related to family child care operations, including equipment, supplies, safety supplies, provider medical examination fees, criminal background check fees, small household repairs in approved child care areas, approved child care training course fees, program materials, and other approved child care-related expenses up to $1,000 per provider.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a registered family child care provider in Maryland with current registration
Must have combined annual family income at or below 60% of State Median Income (SMI) for applicant's family size
Must provide proof of combined annual family income (most recent tax form)
Must not have previously received funds from the Family Child Care Provider Grant Fund
If awarded, must provide family child care for at least one child for at least one to two years after grant award date
Applicants caring for priority groups (special needs, purchase of care, infants, or toddlers) may have enhanced eligibility
Must submit receipts for all items with vendor name, date of purchase, item description, and amount paid
Must submit copy of current IRS Form W-9
Must submit copy of one child care attendance sheet
Incomplete applications will be returned
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must complete the Family Child Care Provider Grant Application form in its entirety and include all required documentation: copy of current Family Child Care Registration, most recent tax form for income verification, receipts for all items requesting reimbursement, copy of IRS Form W-9, and attendance sheet. Completed applications must be mailed to the Office of Child Care at Maryland State Department of Education, Division of Early Childhood - Office of Child Care, 200 West Baltimore Street, 10th Floor, Baltimore, Maryland 21201. Incomplete applications will be returned.

structured_extraction.program_description: A training program that prepares job seekers with disabilities for jobs in the food service industry, including cafeterias, restaurants, and food stores. The program provides seven weeks of classroom instruction combined with hands-on experience in a cafeteria, followed by a seven-week internship at a local business. The program teaches food handling, preparation, kitchen safety, customer service, and point of sale skills.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides fourteen weeks of combined classroom and practical training offered in partnership with the Community College of Baltimore County at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center (WTC) campus in northeast Baltimore. The first seven weeks include classroom instruction at WTC and hands-on experience in the WTC cafeteria. The second seven weeks consist of an internship at a local business. Training covers food handling and preparation skills, kitchen safety and equipment operation, reading and following recipes, food portions and nutrition, weighing and measuring foods, customer service skills, point of sale skills and register operation, and ServSafe® principles.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with disabilities who are able to work independently, stoop, bend and stretch, work well with others, communicate effectively, follow two-step instructions, lift and carry 30 lb. food containers and trays, and stand for long periods of time.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in food service skills including food handling and preparation, kitchen safety, customer service, point of sale operations, and ServSafe® principles. The program prepares individuals for jobs in cafeterias, restaurants, and food stores.

The goal is to encourage children to eat more fresh fruits and vegetables.
