The program is a federal initiative administered by the USDA Food and Nutrition Service that provides schools with a variety of fresh produce to serve as snacks, introducing students to healthy eating habits and a wide variety of produce. Federal funding is provided to purchase and distribute the fresh fruits and vegetables.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Elementary school students and educators at eligible Maryland schools, including eligible schools and residential child care institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and distribution of fresh fruits and vegetables for student consumption during the school day
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Elementary schools in Maryland, with 196 schools participating in School Year 2022-2023
requirements_list: School must be an elementary school in Maryland
School must be selected as eligible for program participation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible elementary schools can apply through the Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs. Schools must be selected and designated as eligible participants in the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grant program to provide financial assistance to child care providers to help stabilize operations and support workforce development in the child care sector during the COVID-19 pandemic.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grant funding provided to eligible licensed child care providers. Grant amounts are determined by a formula based on the number of licensed slots and seven priority areas defined in HB89/SB480: (1) Base stabilization award of $75 per licensed slot; (2) Additional $150 for providers who did not receive federal stabilization grants in previous rounds; (3) Additional $25 for providers participating in the Child Care Scholarship Program; (4) Additional $75 for providers in counties with child care gaps; (5) Additional $100 for providers facing financial hardship or serving low-income communities in high-poverty areas (using Social Vulnerability Index); (6) Additional $50 for providers serving children with IEPs or IFSPs; (7) Additional $30 for providers serving children ages 2 and under. Unused funds from providers not requesting grants are redistributed equally among all grant-award providers per licensed slot.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: August 29, 2022 at 11:59 PM EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care providers including family child care homes, large family child care homes, child care centers, and programs with letters of compliance operating in Maryland. Programs must have been licensed or registered by May 1, 2022 and be open and providing child care services on the application date.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personnel costs including wages, benefits, health insurance, paid leave, retirement contributions, professional development, and COVID-19 vaccination support; rent, mortgage, utilities, facility maintenance and repairs, improvements for accessibility and social distancing; personal protective equipment, cleaning supplies, and health/safety measures; equipment and supplies; business materials and services; mental health services for children and staff; and any materials or services necessary for child care program operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties. However, certain priority areas receive additional funding consideration: providers in counties designated as having child care gaps (Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Carroll, Cecil, Dorchester, Garrett, Harford, Howard, and Wicomico) receive an additional $75 per slot. Providers in areas with high social vulnerability (SVI score greater than 6.0) receive an additional $100 per slot.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a licensed or registered child care provider in Maryland
Program must have been licensed or registered by May 1, 2022 or earlier
Program must be open and providing child care services as of the application date
Applicant must not be a startup program that has not yet begun operations
Program can be a family child care home, large family child care home, child care center, or educational program with letter of compliance
Providers operating multiple facilities must submit separate applications for each location
Accurate and complete accounting records must be maintained for audit purposes
Funds must be used only for eligible expenses or they may need to be refunded
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Providers must submit an application through the online Child Care Stabilization Grant application portal by 11:59 PM EST on August 29, 2022. MSDE processes applications on a rolling basis and reviews each application to verify eligibility and determine the provider's award amount using the established formula. Applicants with incomplete applications or eligibility issues are notified and given 7 calendar days to correct deficiencies. Upon approval, providers are notified of their award amount and payment method. All award processing is expected to be completed by October 28, 2022, with payments issued via direct deposit (ACH) within 3-4 business days or by check via USPS within 30 days. MSDE offers multiple customer service support sessions to assist interested applicants with the application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program designed to provide financial assistance to child care providers to help stabilize their operations during and after the COVID-19 pandemic.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grant payments to licensed child care providers. Grant amounts are determined by formula based on prioritization criteria including: (1) $75 per licensed slot base award; (2) $150 for providers not receiving federal stabilization grants in prior rounds; (3) $25 for providers participating in child care scholarship program; (4) $75 for providers in child care gap areas; (5) $100 for providers with financial hardship or serving low-income communities (SVI score greater than 6.0); (6) $50 for providers serving children with special needs (IEP/IFSP); (7) $30 for providers serving children age 2 and under. Unused funds from providers not seeking awards are redistributed equally among all grant-awarded providers per licensed slot. Funds available: $50 million. Estimated number of grants: 7,099. Payments issued in one lump sum via ACH direct deposit or check by mail.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: August 29, 2022 at 11:59 PM EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers operating family child care homes, large family child care homes, child care centers, and educational programs under letter of compliance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds may be used for: (1) Personnel costs including wages, benefits, health/dental/vision insurance, paid leave, retirement contributions, professional development, staff bonuses, employee transportation, and support for COVID-19 vaccination access; (2) Rent, mortgage, utilities, facility maintenance, and insurance, including facility improvements and minor renovations; (3) Personal protective equipment, cleaning supplies, and health and safety measures in response to COVID-19; (4) Equipment and supplies for COVID-19 response; (5) Goods and services necessary to operate child care programs including food, materials, business automation services, and licensing fees; (6) Mental health services for children and staff including infant and early childhood mental health consultation (IECMHC).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide (Maryland). Special consideration for providers in designated child care gap areas and communities with high social vulnerability index scores.
requirements_list: Program must be licensed or registered with Maryland State Department of Education by May 1, 2022 or earlier
Program must be open and operational on the date of application
Program must be providing child care services on the application date
Providers with multiple child care locations must submit separate applications for each site
Previously-funded applicants are eligible to reapply
Program must not be a start-up or newly operating program (not yet operational)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit applications through the online Governor's Child Care Stabilization Grant application portal. MSDE processes applications on a rolling basis. Upon submission, MSDE reviews applications to verify eligibility and match providers to corresponding award amounts based on prioritization criteria. If an application is complete and the provider is eligible, MSDE notifies the provider of the award amount. If an application is incomplete or the provider is deemed ineligible, MSDE provides notification and allows 7 calendar days to correct identified issues. MSDE expected to complete grant processing by early October 2022, with all awards submitted to the Comptroller by October 28, 2022. Funds distributed via ACH direct deposit (3-4 business days after processing) or check by mail (approximately 30 days). Customer service support sessions were offered on August 9, 11, 13, 15, and 16, 2022.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides co-payment waiver assistance for eligible families participating in the Child Care Scholarship Program, particularly for parenting youth in out-of-home care.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Waives co-payment requirements for qualifying families in the Child Care Scholarship Program. Once approved, eligible families receive a co-payment waiver letter confirming their HB 1121 Program participation and waived co-payment status. Parents must provide this letter to their selected child care program. The parent remains responsible for any amounts not covered by the child care scholarship. Families submit verification and complete DHS Out-of-Home Care Referral forms to request waiver consideration. DHS Case Managers complete and submit the referral, which can take up to 60 days or longer for processing.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families participating in the Child Care Scholarship Program who meet HB 1121 eligibility criteria, particularly parenting youth in out-of-home care.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Waiver of co-payment costs for child care services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be participating in the Child Care Scholarship Program
Must meet specific eligibility criteria outlined in HB 1121
For out-of-home care referrals: parenting youth must be in out-of-home care status at time of referral
Must complete Fast-Track and Full Application prior to referral submission
At redetermination: if parent is above age 22 and no longer in out-of-home care or was not in out-of-home care on their 18th birthday, must meet all CCS Program eligibility requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families work with their DHS Case Manager to complete the HB 1121 Out-of-Home Care Referral Form, providing head of household information, child information, care type selection (formal or informal), and hours/days of child care needed. The DHS Case Manager submits the signed and dated referral to ccscentral2dhsreferral.msde@maryland.gov. The referral must be signed and dated by DHS staff (electronic signatures not acceptable). CCS Central 2 processes the referral, which can take up to 60 days or longer. Once approved, families receive a co-payment waiver letter confirming waived co-payment status. The child care scholarship begin date and out-of-home activity start date must be within 10 days of referral submission.

structured_extraction.program_description: Coordinates early learning and comprehensive services between local Head Start programs and local, state, and federal government agencies, informed by the current Head Start Assessment Report and Strategic Plan.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Coordinates and facilitates collaboration between Head Start programs and government agencies to deliver early learning and comprehensive services, informed by the current Head Start Assessment Report and Strategic Plan.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Head Start programs and government agencies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Coordination of early learning and comprehensive services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide.

structured_extraction.program_name: Health Insurance for Child Care Providers
structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership between Maryland State Department of Education and Maryland Health Connection to help child care providers access health insurance coverage. Providers can shop for plans that cover doctor visits, mental health services, prescription drugs, and more for themselves and their families through the state's official health insurance marketplace.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible child care providers can access health insurance plans through Maryland Health Connection's marketplace. Qualifying individuals may be eligible for financial assistance to help pay for coverage, including tax credits that can lower monthly premiums and cost-sharing reductions that lower out-of-pocket costs including deductibles when enrolled in Silver-level plans. Open enrollment runs from November 1st through January 15th annually. Medicaid enrollment is available year-round. Income eligibility for Medicaid varies by household size (for example, single individual up to approximately $22,025 annual income, household of 4 up to approximately $45,540). Financial assistance eligibility and amounts depend on household income and size. Plans cover doctor visits, mental health services, prescription drugs, hospital and emergency services, maternity and newborn care, pediatric care, and preventive services at no cost.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Open enrollment runs from November 1st through January 15th. Medicaid enrollment is open all year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers in Maryland seeking health insurance coverage for themselves and their families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health insurance coverage including doctor visits, mental health services, prescription drugs, hospital and emergency services, maternity and newborn care, pediatric care, dental care, vision care, behavioral health treatment, preventive care and screenings, and other medical care for the provider and their family members.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Free local help available through authorized navigators in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel, Frederick, Carroll, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, Harford, Cecil, Kent, Queen Anne's, Talbot, Caroline, Dorchester, Calvert, Charles, St. Mary's, Garrett, Allegany, Washington, Wicomico, Somerset, and Worcester counties.
requirements_list: Must be a child care provider in Maryland
Income must qualify for eligibility (varies by plan, household size, and type of assistance)
Must include required household members on application
Qualifying individuals may be eligible for Medicaid or Qualified Health Plans through Maryland Health Connection
Pre-existing conditions cannot be grounds for denial of coverage or higher rates
For Medicaid: immigration status requirements apply (generally must be lawfully present for 5 years, with exceptions for children under 21 and pregnant individuals)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Visit MarylandHealthConnection.gov and use the Get an Estimate tool to compare plans and check eligibility for financial assistance and Medicaid. 2. Determine household size and calculate household income using online tools. 3. Apply online at MarylandHealthConnection.gov, via the free mobile app (Enroll MHC - Apple or Android), by phone at 1-855-642-8572, or request an enrollment kit by mail. 4. Get free, in-person help from authorized health insurance navigators or brokers available statewide (call 1-855-642-8572 or visit MarylandHealthConnection.gov/help to find a navigator in your area). 5. If eligible for Medicaid, complete application and choose a Managed Care Organization (MCO) from available options (Aetna Better Health of Maryland, Wellpoint Maryland, Jai Medical Systems, Kaiser Permanente, Maryland Physicians Care, MedStar Family Choice, Priority Partners, UnitedHealthcare, or CareFirst BlueCross BlueShield Community Health Plan of Maryland). If for Qualified Health Plans, select your plan from available options. 6. For Medicaid: red and white Medical Assistance card will arrive within 14 days of enrollment; coverage begins first day of month applied. For QHP: pay first monthly premium by the first of the month coverage starts to activate coverage; member ID card arrives after payment. 7. Make ongoing premium payments directly to insurance company or MCO.

structured_extraction.program_name: Infant & Early Childhood Mental Health Support Services Program Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant supports positive mental and behavioral health practices for young children who have developmental, social, emotional or behavioral issues. It provides referrals and services for children, families, teachers, and caregivers to build the capacity of early care and education providers and family members to promote healthy social-emotional development. The program prevents, identifies, treats, and reduces the impact of social, emotional, and other mental health problems among children birth through 5 years old.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are provided to non-profit and public agencies licensed to do business in Maryland to support infant and early childhood mental health services and consultation programs. Applicants must operate 12 months per year except for federal holidays.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Wednesday, August 9, 2023 at 5:00 p.m.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit and public agencies licensed to do business in Maryland that provide infant and early childhood mental health services for children birth through 5 years old.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting positive mental and behavioral health practices for young children through providing referrals and services for children, families, teachers, and caregivers. Funds build capacity of early care and education providers and family members to promote healthy social-emotional development, including consultation, training, and technical assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be licensed to do business within the State of Maryland. Available statewide.
requirements_list: Must be a non-profit or public agency
Must be licensed to do business in Maryland
Must have proven capacity to provide Infant and Early Childhood Mental Health Services
Must operate 12 months per year except for federal holidays
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants can attend virtual customer service support sessions provided by MSDE to learn about the program, requirements, and proposal process. Applications are submitted directly through the application form provided. Visit the grant opportunity page for application instructions and requirements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Infant and Early Childhood Mental Health Support Services (IECMHSS) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The IECMHSS improves the ability of staff, programs, and families to prevent, identify, treat, and reduce the impact of social, emotional, and other mental health problems among children birth through 5 years old. The program uses a hybrid model that focuses on both individual child behaviors and overall classroom environment quality, providing consultation, training, coaching, and mentoring to early childhood programs. It also refers children and families needing more intensive mental health services to appropriate support and clinical programs. The program began as a pilot in Baltimore City and on the Eastern Shore in 2002, then expanded statewide in 2006.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides on-site consultation, training, coaching, and mentoring to child care staff, teachers, and programs. IECMH consultants work with teachers to improve overall classroom environment quality while also addressing specific child behavioral challenges. The program builds teacher confidence and competence in managing challenging behaviors, improves classroom quality, and refers children and families needing more intensive mental health services to appropriate support and clinical programs including Judy Centers, Head Start Centers, health departments, Child Find, Maryland Infants & Toddlers Program, and preschool special education.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers, early childhood education programs, teachers, families, and children from birth through 5 years old across Maryland's 12 child care licensing regions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: On-site consultation and technical assistance to improve classroom environment quality, support children with emotional and behavioral challenges, train and coach teachers, and connect children and families to appropriate mental health services and community resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in all 12 statewide child care licensing regions across Maryland. Started in Baltimore City and on the Eastern Shore in 2002, then expanded statewide in 2006.
requirements_list: Serve children birth through 5 years old
Be a child care program or provider in Maryland
Programs must be licensed child care facilities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Infant and Early Childhood Mental Health Support Services program through the Maryland State Department of Education Division of Early Childhood to request on-site consultation and support services. Consultants work directly with child care programs and families through referrals and partnerships with local community resources including Judy Centers, Head Start Centers, health departments, Child Find, Maryland Infants & Toddlers Program, and preschool special education.

structured_extraction.program_name: Judith P. Hoyer Early Child Care and Education Enhancement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Judy Center Early Learning Hubs prepare children for success in school and life by connecting families with high-quality, comprehensive, full-day, full-year early education services. The program promotes school readiness for children ages birth through five using a multigenerational approach for families and children, and provides professional development for early childhood educators. Judy Centers help support all the adults in a child's early years by providing physical health, academic, and other types of support needed to thrive.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program operates Judy Center Early Learning Hub sites throughout the state serving children and families in every local school system. Services include full-day, full-year early education, family support, physical health services, academic support, early identification and intervention, family literacy, and professional development for early childhood educators. As of the most recent data, sites operate in all 24 Maryland counties plus Baltimore City through school-based centers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children ages birth through five and their families, particularly low-income families. Early childhood educators and school systems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: High-quality, comprehensive, full-day, full-year early education services. Physical health services, academic support, early identification and intervention services, family literacy programs, and professional development for early childhood educators.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in all Maryland counties through every local school system. Judy Center sites are located in all 24 counties and Baltimore City. Contact the specific county Judy Center coordinator listed in the program's contact list for access to services in your area.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Judy Centers operate through Maryland public school systems. Families seeking services should contact their local school system's Judy Center site. Each site has a Judy Center Coordinator who can provide information about enrollment and available services. Contact information for all county coordinators and school locations is maintained and updated by the Maryland State Department of Education.

structured_extraction.program_description: Judy Centers provide a central location for early childhood education and support services for children from birth through Kindergarten and their families. Services and programs are typically available 10 to 12 hours a day, year round, to help achieve school readiness.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Early childhood education and support services for young children and families, available 10 to 12 hours daily, year round.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children birth through Kindergarten who reside in Title I school districts across Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Early childhood education and support services for children and families
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Specific Title I school districts across the State of Maryland
requirements_list: Children must be birth through Kindergarten age
Families must reside in Title I school districts
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Judy Center in your Title I school district to inquire about enrollment and services.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a central location for early childhood education programs and comprehensive support services for children from birth through kindergarten and their families who reside in specific Title I school districts across the state.

structured_extraction.contact_name: Kaymi Plank, Judy Center Program Manager; Para asistencia en Español - Nancy Garcia, Judy Center Specialist
structured_extraction.program_audience: Schools and school systems seeking to establish new Judy Center Early Learning Hubs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Expansion of Judy Center Early Learning Hub services and infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide for eligible applicants in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the application process for Fiscal Year 2026. Contact the Judy Center Program Manager for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Comprehensive early learning hubs located in elementary schools where families can engage in learning experiences with children from prenatal through age 5 and access support services. Using a multigenerational approach, Judy Centers focus on preparing children for school success by empowering families through various initiatives and community partnerships. The program is officially named the Judith P. Hoyer Early Care and Education Enhancement Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Judy Center Early Learning Hubs are grant-funded programs that provide or connect families with local community partners for comprehensive family support and early care and education services. Services include: full-day, full-year early care and education services (7-12 hours per day); meals for children and families during school day, breaks, weekends and after-school hours; developmental screenings; family learning activities and engagement with evidence-based family and child playgroups (minimum two per week); parenting classes and training workshops; adult education and workforce development connections for family members; early intervention identification; evidence-based home visiting; referrals for services and supports; case management; health-related services including referrals for dental, vision, and hearing screenings; mental health assessments; connections to health care insurance; professional learning opportunities for early childhood providers; and service coordination with community partners. All programs operate year-round and are integrated with partner agencies including Early Head Start, Head Start, licensed child care centers, family child care providers, Patty Centers, early intervention programs, family literacy programs, preschool special education, workforce development programs, and home visiting organizations.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Contact local Judy Center for enrollment information
structured_extraction.contact_name: Kaymi Plank, Judy Center Program Manager; Para asistencia en Español - Nancy Garcia, Judy Center Specialist
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children from prenatal through age 5 who live within the school zone where the Judy Center is located. Program emphasizes support for historically underserved families in high-needs Title I schools. Children who live in the school zone will attend Pre-K and Kindergarten at the school where the Judy Center is located.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Full-day, full-year early care and education services; developmental screenings; family learning activities; parenting training and workshops; adult education and workforce development connections; evidence-based playgroups; meals; service referrals; early intervention identification; home visiting; case management; health-related services including dental, vision, hearing screenings and mental health referrals; professional learning for staff and partners.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Judy Center Early Learning Hubs are located in elementary schools across the state of Maryland at 86 sites as of FY2024. Eligible families and children must live within the school zone where the Judy Center is located. Judy Centers are located in all 24 Maryland jurisdictions with expansion planned: nine new sites annually through 2025, then 18 sites annually from 2026-2030.
requirements_list: Families and children must reside within the school zone where the Judy Center is located
Children from prenatal through age 5 are eligible
Families from all backgrounds are welcome; program emphasizes historically underserved families in high-needs Title I schools
Children with disabilities and their families are fully included in all services as part of Individualized Education Program (IEP) or Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested families should contact their closest Judy Center Early Learning Hub directly for enrollment information and to learn about available services. A comprehensive map and contact information for each Judy Center location can be found at marylandfamiliesengage.org/judy-center-hubs-map/. Families are considered engaged with the Judy Center if they participate in at least 12 meaningful interactions during the fiscal year or are enrolled in formal partner programs such as Kindergarten, Prekindergarten, Early Head Start, Head Start, Patty Centers, family child care providers, or accredited child care centers.

structured_extraction.program_name: Licensing Compliance Grant for Family Child Care Providers (LCGFCCP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that helps registered family child care providers offset the costs of opening and maintaining their child care programs by reimbursing expenses needed to achieve or maintain compliance with family child care regulations. The program reimburses up to $1,000 in eligible expenses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reimburses up to $1,000 in eligible expenses incurred by registered family child care providers to achieve or maintain compliance with family child care regulations. Reimbursement is provided as a grant award. Eligible expenses include safety supplies, provider medical examination fees, criminal background check fees, small household repairs in approved child care areas, approved child care training course fees, expenses related to local water, sewer, fire, and health requirements, program materials and equipment, and other costs necessary for completion of the registration process.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered family child care providers whose annual household income does not exceed 60% of Maryland's current State Median Income (SMI) for their family size.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Safety supplies, provider medical examination fees, criminal background check fees, small household repairs in approved child care areas, approved child care training course fees, expenses related to local water, sewer, fire, and health requirements, program materials and equipment, and other costs identified as necessary for completion of the registration process.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a registered family child care provider
Annual household income must not exceed 60% of Maryland's current State Median Income (SMI) for the applicant's family size
Expenses must be necessary to achieve or maintain compliance with family child care regulations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are processed in accordance with regulations set forth at COMAR 13A.14.07, which specify eligibility requirements, application procedures, and the method by which awards are made. More information about the application process will be available on the program webpage.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Quality improvements, start-up costs, and sustainability for family child care and center-based programs.

structured_extraction.program_name: Local Early Childhood Advisory Council System Improvement Grant FY26
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that supports Local Early Childhood Advisory Councils (LECACs) in establishing school readiness benchmarks, conducting needs assessments, developing action plans to increase participation in early childhood programs, coordinating local early childhood initiatives, and reporting progress to the State Advisory Council on Early Childhood Education and Care.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding to support the operations and activities of Local Early Childhood Advisory Councils in fiscal year 2026. Applicants must apply through the MSDE Grants website. Funds may be used for LECAC operations, establishing school readiness benchmarks, conducting needs assessments, developing action plans to increase participation in early childhood programs, and coordinating early childhood initiatives and reforms locally.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Established Local Early Childhood Advisory Councils in Maryland counties
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting LECAC operations, establishing school readiness benchmarks, conducting needs assessments, developing action plans to increase participation in early childhood programs, coordinating early childhood initiatives and reforms locally, professional development for early childhood educators, family engagement practices, and reporting progress to the State Advisory Council.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties with established Local Early Childhood Advisory Councils. Note: Baltimore County LECAC was disbanded as of 2/24/25.
requirements_list: Must be an established Local Early Childhood Advisory Council with a formal Memorandum of Agreement with MSDE
Must apply through the MSDE Grants website
Must meet at least four times per calendar year
Must establish annual benchmarks of school readiness skills of children entering kindergarten
Must conduct periodic local needs assessments concerning the quality and availability of early childhood education and development programs
Must develop action plans for increasing overall participation of children in existing programs
Must develop recommendations regarding local professional development and career advancement plans for early childhood educators
Must coordinate locally the projects in Maryland's Race to the Top Early Learning Challenge and other early childhood initiatives and reforms
Must submit quarterly attendance rosters, meeting minutes, and an annual report on action plans to the State Advisory Council on Early Childhood Education and Care
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the MSDE Grants website to apply for the Local Early Childhood Advisory Council System Improvement Grant FY26. Applicants must be established LECACs with an approved Memorandum of Agreement with MSDE. Contact the MSDE Division of Early Childhood Development for specific application materials and instructions.

structured_extraction.program_description: Financial assistance for child care providers pursuing Maryland accreditation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement support for eligible expenses related to pursuing Maryland Program Accreditation. Funds may be used to cover instructional materials and classroom learning materials for infant/toddler, preschool, and school-age classrooms. Reimbursement is provided for documented purchases made after the accreditation timeline has been established.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers (licensed child care centers) seeking Maryland Program Accreditation
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Instructional materials and classroom learning materials for infant/toddler, preschool, and school-age classrooms in pursuit of Maryland Program Accreditation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Must be a licensed child care facility
Must be pursuing Maryland Program Accreditation through MSDE
Must have completed a Program Improvement Visit prior to application submission
Must have completed an Accreditation Program Improvement Plan identifying accreditation indicators rated Not Met or Partially Met
Must provide proof of purchase with receipts/invoices/packing slips indicating vendor name, date of purchase, item description, and cost
Items cannot be purchased prior to accreditation timeline
Cannot have received or applied for program accreditation funds from any other source
Applicant must sign application in blue ink
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Application for Accreditation Support form (OCC 279) with all required facility information. Submit with required documentation including: completed Instructional Materials Checklist with proof of payment for each vendor, completed Program Improvement Visit documentation, and Accreditation Program Improvement Plan with task timeline. Mail completed application and all documentation to Maryland State Department of Education, Office of Child Care, 200 West Baltimore Street, 10th Floor, Baltimore, Maryland 21201. Incomplete applications will be returned.

structured_extraction.program_description: Support funds available to assist child care programs with the expense of obtaining Maryland Accreditation. The fund offers reimbursement for non-consumable learning materials purchased in pursuit of accreditation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement for non-consumable learning materials purchased during the accreditation process or during accredited status. Maximum reimbursement is $2,500 for programs with capacity 1-100 or $3,000 for programs with capacity 101+, per accreditation cycle. Eligible purchases include curricula, classroom technology, outdoor play equipment, science and sensory materials, books, and literacy activities. Receipts dating as far back as twelve months before the application date are acceptable.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care centers and school-age only programs pursuing or maintaining Maryland Accreditation
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Non-consumable learning materials including curricula, classroom technology, outdoor play equipment, science and sensory materials, books, and literacy activities purchased during the accreditation process or during accredited status.
requirements_list: Program must be currently Maryland Accredited or have completed the Initial Self-Appraisal as part of the Maryland Accreditation process
Receipts for learning materials must be gathered, dating back up to twelve months before the date of application
Infants and Toddlers Learning Materials Checklist and/or Preschool and School-Age Learning Materials Checklist must be completed, with information matching the purchases on receipts
Application must be completed through Maryland OneStop portal
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Gather receipts for learning materials purchased during the accreditation process or during accredited status (up to 12 months before application date). 2. Complete the Infants and Toddlers Learning Materials Checklist and/or Preschool and School-Age Learning Materials Checklist, matching information to receipts. 3. Complete the MSDE Application for Maryland Accreditation Support through Maryland OneStop portal and upload documentation. Applications are reviewed within 30 business days, with approvals and requests for further information sent through the Maryland OneStop portal.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Blueprint for Maryland's Future - Full-Day Pre-K Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides free full-day Pre-K services to all three- and four-year-old children from families earning incomes at or below 300% of the Federal Poverty Level. The program emphasizes high-quality early education to prepare children for kindergarten and lifelong success. A subsidized sliding scale is also available for Tier II families (301-600% FPL) and full-cost enrollment for Tier III families (above 600% FPL).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free full-day Pre-K services provided at no cost to Tier I eligible families (income at or below 300% FPL or experiencing homelessness). Tier II families (301-600% FPL, four-year-olds only; partially implemented in FY 26 for 301-360% FPL) pay a subsidized cost on a sliding scale ranging from 10-40% of the per-pupil cost, capped at no more than 7% of gross annual family income. Tier III families (above 600% FPL, four-year-olds only) pay the full per-pupil cost. The per-pupil cost is $13,003 (FY 25), $14,473 (FY 26), and $19,950 (FY 27-28), adjusted annually for inflation thereafter. For FY 26, Tier II families in the 301-360% FPL range pay $1,447.30 annually (10% of cost). For FY 27, sliding scale ranges from $1,995-$7,980 annually depending on income tier. Maryland State Department of Education provides state share through grants to LEAs and private providers; counties may cover family share with local funds at their discretion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: All three- and four-year-old children from families earning incomes at or below 300% of the Federal Poverty Level, children experiencing homelessness, children with disabilities, and multilingual learners. Four-year-olds from families earning 301-600% FPL also eligible under sliding scale (partially implemented FY 26). Four-year-olds from families earning above 600% FPL eligible at full cost if space available.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: High-quality early childhood education and learning experiences through full-day Pre-K programming, supporting brain development and kindergarten readiness.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - available to families across all Maryland counties through both public school LEAs and private community-based providers.
requirements_list: Child must be three or four years old (Tier I); four-year-olds only for Tier II and Tier III

Family income at or below 300% of Federal Poverty Level (Tier I) OR experiencing homelessness (Tier I) OR income 301-600% FPL (Tier II, four-year-olds only) OR income above 600% FPL (Tier III, four-year-olds only)
Children with disabilities and multilingual learners within 300-600% FPL placed in Tier I through FY 26
Children with disabilities requiring group services in Pre-K with Extended IFSP or IEP placed in Tier I regardless of income
All children except those experiencing homelessness must provide proof of income at enrollment
Valid full-day Pre-K enrollment required (part-time enrollment does not qualify)

Family income verification required at time of enrollment through W-2, 1099, pay stubs, unemployment verification, or tax return; LEAs may also use FARM eligibility or Direct Certification (SNAP, TANF, Foster Care); Private providers may use Child Care Scholarships, SNAP eligibility, Head Start forms, or program-developed income forms

Children experiencing homelessness need only provide documentation of homelessness status (completed eligibility questionnaire, McKinney-Vento liaison note, or similar record) rather than income proof
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Families enroll child in an eligible full-day Pre-K program at a public school LEA or private community-based provider. 2. At time of enrollment, families provide income verification documentation. 3. LEAs and private providers use MSDE Pre-K Cost Calculator to determine family tier status based on gross annual income and household size. 4. For Tier II families, provider and family sign standardized agreement acknowledging sliding scale reimbursement level and agreed payment schedule (weekly, monthly, or yearly). 5. Tier I families receive free services; Tier II families make sliding scale payments; Tier III families pay full cost if enrolled. 6. MSDE provides state share to LEAs through state aid grants (bimonthly) and to private providers through Pre-K formula grants (monthly per invoicing). 7. Enrollment determination made at time of initial enrollment; family income level remains the same through end of academic year even if income changes. 8. Information on all available Pre-K options and enrollment process available through MSDE website and Pre-K Grantee List resources.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Business Enterprise Program for the Blind (BEP)
structured_extraction.program_description: BEP prepares individuals whose primary disability is vision loss to operate successful retail concession, food service, and vending operations in federal, military, DOD, and State of Maryland facilities. The program is authorized by the Federally mandated Randolph-Sheppard Act and provides training, licensing, and oversight to help people who are blind run successful retail and food service businesses in public facilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a three-phase training program: (1) An eight-week New Manager Training course conducted by BEP staff at DORS' Workforce & Technology Center in Northeast Baltimore; (2) Formal food service training with certified instructors and chefs, with certification by the National Restaurant Association in food service sanitation; (3) On-the-job training consisting of three to six months of extended internship at various BEP facilities under an experienced manager. BEP-licensed business operators manage approximately 50 long-term, successful businesses in Maryland State, county, and federal agencies. Many BEP managers use assistive technologies including laptop computers with adaptive software, digital talking cash registers, talking bill identifiers, scales, thermometers, and Braille note takers to perform daily job duties.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maryland Business Enterprise Program for the Blind
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals whose primary disability is vision loss and who are legally blind, US citizens, and certified as eligible by DORS. OBVS can also assist legally blind individuals over age 55 who have independent living, but not employment, goals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and preparation to manage and operate retail concession, food service, and vending operations in public facilities managed by federal, military, DOD, and state agencies, including technology support such as adaptive software, digital talking cash registers, talking bill identifiers, scales, thermometers, and Braille note takers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide for operations in federal, military, DOD, and State of Maryland facilities. Operations may be established at state office buildings in Annapolis and Baltimore, National Institutes of Health, Internal Revenue Service, U.S. Food & Drug Administration, Motor Vehicle Administration, Social Security Administration, US Coast Guard, and Fort George G. Meade.
requirements_list: Individual must be legally blind (primary disability is vision loss)
Individual must be a US citizen
Individual must have at minimum a high school diploma or GED equivalent
Candidate must have an aptitude for business management
Candidate must have practical skills and meet the legal criteria for operating a business supported by federal law
Candidate must be referred by a DORS OBVS counselor
Candidate must receive an evaluation from a local DORS counselor
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: If you already have a DORS counselor, ask your counselor about BEP. If not already working with DORS, go to dors.maryland.gov and select Request DORS Services. Complete the form, which can be submitted by you, a family member, a medical provider, or a social worker. You will be contacted to set up an intake meeting where a DORS counselor will gather information and provide details regarding your eligibility for DORS services and the BEP program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary professional development program that improves the quality and stability of the child care workforce by recognizing and supporting child care providers who go beyond state licensing and registration requirements. Participants advance through seven credential levels for staff and four credential levels for administrators by completing approved training, gaining work experience, and participating in professional activities. The program helps develop a professional workforce, improve compensation, recognize professional learning, and provide structure for career growth.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants earn achievement bonuses upon completion of credential levels. Staff bonuses: $200 one-time at Level 2, $300 one-time at Level 3, $500 one-time at Level 4, $600 annually at Level 4+ (Options 1-3), $750 annually at Level 5 (Options 1-3), and $1,000 annually at Level 6 (Options 1-3). Administrator bonuses: $600 one-time at Level 1, $750 annually at Level 2, $1,000 annually at Level 3, and $1,500 annually at Level 4. Participants with Credential Level 2 or higher receive $400 in training vouchers and reimbursements annually as funds are available, covering pre-service training, conferences, and college coursework. All participants are eligible for tuition assistance through the Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund (CCCPDF) to earn Associate's, Bachelor's, or Master's degrees at approved colleges or universities. The program also provides recognition and structure for career advancement for child care providers who exceed state licensing requirements.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Coming soon; applications open for renewals
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered family child care providers and operators, directors, infant/toddler/preschool/school-age teachers, and assistants or aides working part-time or full-time in licensed child care centers or Letter of Compliance programs in Maryland. Individuals must work directly with children on a daily basis and must not have been sanctioned by the Office of Child Care. Substitutes, volunteers, and employees who do not work directly with children (e.g., regional/district managers, administrative, maintenance, food service, transportation staff) are ineligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Achievement bonuses upon credential level completion; training vouchers and reimbursements for approved training (pre-service training, conferences, college coursework); tuition assistance for college or university programs in early childhood education or related fields leading to Associate's, Bachelor's, or Master's degrees; Core of Knowledge training in six key areas: Child Development, Curriculum, Health/Safety/Nutrition, Special Needs, Professionalism, and Community; and professional activities that contribute to professional growth and the child care community.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Participants must be employed in a registered family child care home, Letter of Compliance program, or licensed child care center in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a registered family child care provider, operator, director, or staff member (teacher, assistant teacher, or aide) in a licensed child care center or Letter of Compliance program in Maryland
Must work directly with children on a daily basis in an approved setting
Cannot have been sanctioned by the Office of Child Care
Cannot be a substitute or volunteer in a child care program
Cannot be a child care center employee who does not work directly with children on a daily basis (e.g., regional/district manager, administrative, maintenance, food service, transportation staff)
Must continue working in a child care setting for at least one year after acceptance
Must complete approved Core of Knowledge (COK) training in six key areas: Child Development, Curriculum, Health/Safety/Nutrition, Special Needs, Professionalism, and Community
Must gain work experience in a child care setting (duration and hours vary by credential level)
Must participate in Professional Activity Units (PAUs) related to the child care profession

Credentials are issued for a 12-month period and must be renewed annually by continuing to work in a registered or licensed child care program, completing continued training for the applicable credential level, and participating in professional activities
For renewal: Training, Professional Activity Units (PAUs), and proof of employment must be submitted every year to maintain participation
Requirements vary by credential level regarding number of training hours, years of experience, college credits, and PAUs needed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participants review credential level requirements based on their current qualifications and experience. They must complete approved Core of Knowledge (COK) training (ranging from 45 to 240 clock hours depending on level) from approved trainers, training organizations, or accredited colleges/universities. Training options include Core of Knowledge courses, pre-service training (45-90 hour programs), college coursework, and continued training. Participants gain work experience by continuing employment in registered or licensed child care settings working directly with children. Participants earn Professional Activity Units (PAUs) through eligible professional activities such as joining child care associations, presenting trainings, mentoring providers, participating in accreditation cohorts, attending Maryland EXCELS or state conferences, serving on boards or task forces, and other activities that contribute to professional growth and community benefit. Custom activities not listed on the PAU matrix may be submitted on the PAU Approval Form for review within 60 days, with assignments of 1-3 units based on professional growth and community benefit impact. Upon meeting all requirements, providers submit documentation of completed training, PAU participation, and employment verification. Applications are open for providers seeking renewals; contact the Credentialing Branch at workforceadvancementocc.msde@maryland.gov or (410) 767-7852 for application information. More information at tinyurl.com/md-credential.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Child Care Resource Network Technical Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Child Care Resource Network provides technical assistance services to help child care providers start, expand, and operate child care centers or become family child care providers. Services cover licensing and compliance, behavioral issues, children with special needs, and support for credential and program accreditation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical assistance services including guidance on licensing and compliance, behavioral issues, children with special needs, credential attainment, and program accreditation. Services are available to center-based and family child care providers, Head Start programs, nursery schools, cooperatives, drop-in centers, playgroups, community and non-profit organizations, employers, and public agencies. There is no cost for technical assistance services.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing
structured_extraction.program_audience: Existing and potential center-based and family child care providers, Head Start programs, nursery schools, cooperatives, drop-in centers, playgroups, community and non-profit organizations, community groups, employers, and public agencies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical assistance for starting, expanding, and operating child care services, including licensing compliance, behavioral support, special needs accommodation, and credential and accreditation support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals and organizations can contact the Maryland Child Care Resource Network directly to request technical assistance. Services are provided on an ongoing basis without formal application requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Child Care Scholarship Program provides assistance to help families pay for child care services. This is a subsidy program designed to make child care more affordable and accessible to families in need.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides financial assistance to eligible families to help cover the cost of child care services from licensed providers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Parents and families seeking child care assistance; child care providers serving eligible families
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Child care services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Information and instructions are available on the program webpage for both parents and child care providers.

structured_extraction.program_description: A quality rating and improvement system that recognizes and supports child care providers who meet high quality standards through tiered ratings and incentives.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maryland EXCELS rates child care providers on quality standards and provides technical assistance and recognition to help providers improve their services and advance through quality rating levels.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers and family home care providers in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Quality improvement initiatives and technical assistance for child care providers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland for licensed child care providers.
requirements_list: Provider must be licensed in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Child care providers participate in Maryland EXCELS through the Division of Early Childhood. Providers are rated on quality standards and receive support to improve.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland State Department of Education distributes bonuses to child care programs participating in Maryland EXCELS to support quality improvement. Programs receive bonuses ranging from $1,000 to $13,500 based on the type of program, quality rating, and capacity. Bonuses are awarded when programs publish a quality rating for the first time or re-publish a quality rating of 4 or 5.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Bonuses are distributed as flat payments based on program type and quality rating level. Child care centers with capacity 1-50 receive $1,000-$4,500; centers with capacity 51-100 receive $1,000-$9,000; centers with capacity 101 or more receive $1,000-$13,500; family child care homes receive $1,000-$4,300; large family homes receive $1,000-$4,500. Bonuses are paid each time a program meets eligibility criteria (publishes a quality rating for the first time or re-publishes a rating of 4 or 5). Bonuses are typically processed within 60 days of the quality rating publication date. Payments are made by check or direct deposit. Programs can use bonuses for any purpose, including purchasing learning materials, equipment, furniture, and supporting staff salary increases.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Bonuses available between July 1, 2025 and June 30, 2026

structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care programs participating in Maryland EXCELS including child care centers, family child care homes, and large family homes
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bonuses can be used at the discretion of the program, including purchasing high-quality learning materials, equipment, furniture, supporting staff salary increases, and improving program quality.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - all Maryland counties
requirements_list: Program must be participating in Maryland EXCELS
Program must be in compliance with all Maryland EXCELS regulations
Program must participate in scheduled Continuous Quality Improvement visits
Program must publish a quality rating for the first time or re-publish a quality rating of 4 or 5
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No application or forms are required. Eligible programs automatically receive bonus payments by check or direct deposit within 60 days of their quality rating publication date. Program administrators can check payment status on the General Accounting Division (GAD) website after registering. Contact a Quality Assurance Specialist for assistance with increasing your quality rating and to learn more about available training, work groups, and resources.

structured_extraction.program_description: A reimbursement program that rewards early childhood and school-age care programs for providing high-quality services to families using the Child Care Scholarship program. Programs receive increased reimbursement amounts ranging from 10% to 44% based on the age of the child, type of care, and the program's quality rating level.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Programs at Maryland EXCELS Quality Ratings 3, 4, and 5 receive increased reimbursement amounts. Family child care homes receive 10% to 29% increases depending on quality rating and child age. Child care centers receive 10% to 44% increases depending on quality rating and child age. Payments are shown as EXCELS payments on the Invoice Detail Report for each child.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed early childhood and school-age care programs participating in Maryland EXCELS and accepting Child Care Scholarship families
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Increased reimbursement payments for providing high-quality child care services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Program must be participating in Maryland EXCELS
Program must accept families using Child Care Scholarship
Program must achieve and maintain Maryland EXCELS Quality Rating of Level 3, 4, or 5
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Programs that are already participating in Maryland EXCELS and the Child Care Scholarship program automatically receive these enhanced reimbursement payments based on their quality rating level. No separate application is required.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Economic Development Assistance Authority and Fund (MEDAAF) - Child Care Facility Loans
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides special purpose loans to construct, expand, or improve child care facilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Special purpose loans available to help child care facility operators construct new facilities, expand existing facilities, or improve current facilities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care facility operators, providers, and developers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction, expansion, or improvement of child care facilities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Applicant must be operating or planning to operate a child care facility
Project must involve construction, expansion, or improvement of a facility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Department of Business and Economic Development to inquire about loan availability and application procedures.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Hearing Aid and Language & Communication Video Loan Bank
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide resource that allows families of children who are deaf or hard of hearing to borrow hearing aids for up to one year at no cost. The program also provides videos and resources to help families learn communication methods to use with their children.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Families may borrow hearing aids for up to one year. The program also offers DVDs, videos, and links to resources about language and communication methods including American Sign Language, Cued Speech, and spoken language development. All resources are provided to eligible families at no cost.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Zella Shabasson, Au.D. and Dr. Paige Bradford
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families of children who are deaf or hard of hearing from birth through age 21 who have not yet graduated from high school
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hearing aids and educational materials about language and communication development options
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residents only
requirements_list: Child must be diagnosed by an audiologist or other medical professional as deaf or hard of hearing
Child must be from birth to age 21 and not yet graduated from high school
Family must be Maryland residents

For hearing aids: family must not have insurance coverage for hearing aids, be experiencing delays or difficulties acquiring or replacing hearing aids, and/or need a hearing aid trial before purchasing personal aids or receiving a cochlear implant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families can request hearing aids or materials by using the provided links to request materials from the Loan Bank.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Infants & Toddlers Program (MITP) Consolidated Local Implementation Grant (CLIG)
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant mechanism through which local jurisdictions receive federal and state funds to implement local early intervention programs for infants and toddlers with disabilities in compliance with federal and state regulations, policies, and procedures.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Local Lead Agencies designated by each local jurisdiction receive federal and state funds through this consolidated grant. The grant covers various early intervention program costs and services for infants and toddlers with disabilities, including personnel, services, equipment, and administration. Funds are delivered via grant awards and may also include Intergovernmental Transfer state general funds from the Maryland Department of Health. Grantees must submit all required grant applications, reports, and amendment requests through the MSDE MOVEit Secure File Transfer Website (MMSFTW) at https://msde.sftp.md.gov/. All documents must be submitted in PDF format with proper file naming conventions and accompanied by email notification to the designated fiscal grants liaison.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing - specific annual submission deadlines established for FFY 2025/SFY 2026
structured_extraction.contact_name: Daniele Redivo, Management Associate; Glenn Graymen, Lead Fiscal Grants Liaison; Nancy Vorobey, Fiscal Liaison
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Lead Agencies (LLAs) and Local Infants & Toddlers Programs (LITPs) in Maryland jurisdictions that administer early intervention services for infants and toddlers with disabilities and their families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementation of local early intervention programs including early intervention services, personnel costs, program administration, and related expenses required to comply with federal Part C and state regulations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All local jurisdictions in Maryland that have designated Local Lead Agencies administering Local Infants & Toddlers Programs.
requirements_list: Designated Local Lead Agency status
Aggregation of information from LITP partner agencies
Compliance with federal and state regulations, policies, and procedures
Submission of grant applications and required forms by established deadlines
Use of current forms downloaded immediately before completion
Upload of all submissions to MSDE MOVEit Secure File Transfer Website at https://msde.sftp.md.gov/ using proper file naming conventions
Single submission per file with correct FileCode_EntityID_SFY_GrantNameCode format
Email notification to designated fiscal grants liaison upon document upload with names of uploaded documents
All submissions must be in PDF format

Submission of required reports including semi-annual program reports, annual program reports, annual LICC reports, interim cumulative variance reports, final cumulative variance reports, Form 400, and Form 500 on established timelines
Grants Submission Coordinator (GSC) designation and credential management
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Each Local Lead Agency completes the grant application by aggregating information from partner agencies. The Grants Submission Coordinator (GSC) designated by each program director/project manager receives Entity Code and log-on credentials to access the grant program files on the MSDE MOVEit Secure File Transfer Website at https://msde.sftp.md.gov/. The application process includes submission of the CLIG Application, budget forms from the Excel Budget Submissions Workbook, recipient assurances, federal certifications, GEPA Section 427 compliance documentation, and State Systemic Improvement Plan. All submissions must follow strict file naming conventions (FileCode_EntityID_SFY_GrantNameCode_APP.pdf for applications) and be uploaded to the designated program's shared folder ToMSDE subfolder. Grantees must email notification to the fiscal grants liaison specifying the uploaded document names and are advised to save a screenshot as proof of submission. Files remain in the inbound FromMSDE folder for 30 days before deletion. Post-application reporting includes semi-annual program reports, annual program reports, interim and final cumulative variance reports, Form 400 and Form 500 submissions, annual LICC reports, and financial reports on established timelines throughout the grant period.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program providing free, family-centered early intervention services and support for infants and toddlers from birth to age three in Maryland, including those with developmental delays, disabilities, or medical conditions that can impact their development. The program also provides grants to local governments to help them create and run these services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MITP provides free, family-centered support for children from birth to age three. Services include developmental screenings and evaluations (provided free of charge), individualized support that builds on the child's and family's strengths, and addresses family goals and concerns. Teachers, therapists, and other providers offer coaching and support in the home, child care, library, or other community locations where families spend time. Services help children participate in everyday activities and develop new skills, and connect families with community resources. Additionally, the program provides formula and project grants to local jurisdictions to support the creation and operation of local early intervention services for infants and toddlers with disabilities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Infants and toddlers from birth to age three, particularly those with developmental delays, disabilities, or medical conditions that can impact their development, and their families. Also local governments and non-profit organizations that provide services to infants and toddlers with disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Early intervention services and support for infants and toddlers, including developmental screenings, evaluations, therapy services, coaching, and family support to help children participate in everyday activities and develop new skills. Funds also support the creation and operation of local early intervention services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - available to all children living in Maryland who have not turned three years old.
requirements_list: Child must be from birth to age three
Child must live in Maryland

Child must have developmental delays, a disability, a medical diagnosis that can impact development, or not be moving, communicating, learning, interacting with others, or participating in daily activities like others of the same age
Free developmental assessment is provided to determine eligibility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit a referral online at referral.mditp.org or call 1-800-535-0182 to get contact information for the local Infants and Toddlers Program. Referrals can be made over the phone if preferred. Anyone - a parent, child care provider, doctor, grandparent, nurse, friend, or other relative - can submit a referral. 2. After the referral, someone from the local Infants and Toddlers program will call to gather information about the child's development and any concerns. A developmental screening or evaluation appointment will be scheduled. 3. The evaluation takes place in the home or another location of the family's choice. The team will ask questions about the child and observe how they move, communicate, and play. 4. If the child is eligible for services, the family becomes part of the early intervention team. Together they will develop a plan. Families give permission for all assessments and services and can stop or change services at any time.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Meals for Achievement provides state funds to supplement federal meal reimbursements. This allows participating schools to offer free breakfast in the classroom. The program increases students' access to and participation in breakfast and has been credited with improving students' test scores, behavior, attendance, and well-being.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides state funds to supplement federal meal reimbursements, allowing participating schools to offer free breakfast in the classroom. Currently, 581 schools participate in MMFA.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students in participating Maryland schools that offer free breakfast in the classroom
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free breakfast meals served in the classroom to students
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Currently, 581 Maryland schools participate in MMFA
requirements_list: Schools must be participating in MMFA
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools can participate in MMFA to provide free breakfast in the classroom using state and federal funds

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Medicaid Home and Community-Based Services Waiver for Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (Autism Waiver)
structured_extraction.program_description: Community-based, long-term, person-centered therapeutic services and support for eligible children and youth with Autism Spectrum Disorder to enable home and community living as an alternative to institutional care.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The waiver provides funding for approved Medicaid provider agencies to deliver seven types of services: Intensive Individual Support Services (one-on-one assistance based on the child's need for interventions and support to acquire self-help, socialization, communication, daily living, functional living, behavior management, and adaptive skills); Therapeutic Integration-Regular or Intensive (structured programs outside school hours providing therapeutic activities and expressive therapies for children with socialization, isolation, hyperactivity, impulse control, and behavior problems); Respite Care (short-term supervision and assistance with activities of daily living); Environmental Accessibility Adaptations (funding for physical home adaptations to ensure health, welfare, and safety); Family Consultation (individualized consultation and training for the child's family); Adult Life Planning (family-centered support in accessing adult community services); and Residential Habilitation-Regular or Intensive (community-based residential placement for children who cannot live at home). Participants also receive Service Coordination and targeted case management through their local education agency. The waiver qualifies participants for full Medical Assistance benefits including health insurance, prescription coverage, dental care, physician and hospital care, home health, laboratory services, disposable medical supplies, durable medical equipment, and mental health services. Participants must maintain eligibility by using at least 5 hours of Autism Waiver services per month.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 45 days from the date of application letter from MDH
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children and youth ages 1 through the end of the school semester when the child turns 21 years old who have Autism Spectrum Disorder or an educational classification of Autism and reside in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community-based therapeutic services, home accessibility adaptations, family consultation, one-on-one support services, residential placement, respite care, after-school and weekend therapeutic programs, and full Medical Assistance benefits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Children and youth must be residents of Maryland.
requirements_list: Be a resident of Maryland
Be between the age of 1 and 21 years old
Have a current educational classification of Autism or a diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder
