Receive early intervention or special education services identified through one of the following: an Individual Family Service Plan (IFSP) for ages 1-5, an Individual Education Program (IEP) in an early childhood or Kindergarten setting for ages 3-5, or an IEP with 15 hours or more of special education and related services and/or 1:1 adult supports per week for first grade through high school exit
Meet an institutional Level of Care for Intermediate Care Facilities for individuals with Intellectual Disabilities (ICF-IID) and choose to receive Autism Waiver services as an alternative
Be able to be served and safely maintained in the home and community with Autism Waiver services
Meet financial eligibility for Medical Assistance with monthly income not exceeding 300% of Supplemental Security Income (SSI) benefits and countable assets not exceeding $2,000
Choose the Autism Waiver as the waiver that best meets the child's needs

Military Exception: Dependents of US Military Service members invited to apply to the Autism Waiver while the family is out of state for military services shall be offered an opportunity to apply upon request when they return to Maryland and meet all technical eligibility requirements
Register with the Autism Waiver Registry at 1-866-417-3480 to be eligible to apply when a vacancy occurs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Call the Autism Waiver Registry Helpline at 1-866-417-3480 to register as interested in Autism Waiver services and provide child information (name, date of birth, address, county of residence, contact information). Parents must confirm the child has an ASD diagnosis, an IFSP or IEP, and at least 15 hours of special education/related services per week on IEP (1st grade and above). 2. MDH vendor conducts initial screening during the intake call based on parent self-report to verify technical eligibility criteria. 3. If technical eligibility is met, the child's name is added to the Registry and MSDE is notified; a letter is sent to the family. 4. MSDE verifies technical eligibility (resident of MD, under age 21, Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis, IFSP or IEP with 15 hours of special education/health-related services). 5. If verified, the child is added to the Autism Waiver Waitlist; a letter is sent confirming the name is on the waitlist and includes the Autism Waiver Fact Sheet. 6. If additional information is needed, a letter is sent with a 30-day deadline to provide updated information. If not provided, a final notice is sent with a 15-day deadline. 7. When a vacancy occurs, MDH sends an invitation letter to apply and a 45-day deadline to accept the invitation, establish contact with the Autism Waiver Contact at the local education agency (LEA), complete the technical eligibility checklist, and submit the financial application. The invitation includes the Medical Assistance (MA) Financial Application, Parental Rights and Responsibilities, Autism Waiver Contact List, and Application Documentation Checklist. 8. The family works with the Autism Waiver Contact at the LEA to confirm technical, financial, and medical eligibility. 9. The child contributes to the Level of Care assessment process that determines medical eligibility. 10. LEA/MSDE track application progress. 11. Upon eligibility determination, the family receives notification from the State. If eligible, the letter includes a start date to begin Autism Waiver services. 12. The family attends a multidisciplinary team meeting to develop a Plan of Care. Application is based on chronological order from the time the child's name is placed on the Waitlist. Parents must ensure all demographic information stays up to date and contact the Helpline to report any changes.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Technology Assistance Program helps Maryland residents with disabilities and their families qualify for low-interest loans to buy assistive technology equipment, devices, adapted and non-adapted vehicles in order to live, work, and learn more independently and to support various employment goals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest loans are available from $500 to $60,000, depending on restrictions and qualifications. The loans can be used to purchase assistive technology equipment, devices, adapted and non-adapted vehicles.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents with disabilities and their families
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of assistive technology equipment, devices, adapted and non-adapted vehicles to support living, working, learning more independently, and employment goals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland resident with a disability or be a family member of a resident with a disability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a loan application through the online application portal.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland's Child Care Training Approval Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program designed to ensure quality of training offered to child care professionals in Maryland by approving trainers and training content.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program approves trainers and training courses for child care professionals. Approved trainers can develop and deliver training accepted for the Maryland Child Care Credential and continuing education. Approval numbers are valid for a 4-year period as long as the trainer or organization operates within regulations and maintains compliance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and organizations who work with child care professionals, except community colleges, universities, and approved national organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training development and delivery for child care professionals to earn the Maryland Child Care Credential and continuing education credits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Trainer orientation is required before submitting a Training Approval Application
Must comply with COMAR 13A.14.08 regulations
Must maintain operational compliance throughout the 4-year approval period
Approved core of knowledge trainers must follow established curriculum standards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants attend a trainer orientation session to receive required knowledge. After orientation, they submit a Training Approval Application with required documentation. The application and documents are reviewed and approved by Training Approval staff within the Division of Early Childhood's Workforce Development unit. Proposals are reviewed within 60 days of receipt. Upon approval, a unique training approval number is assigned by the automated tracking system. Letters are generated following the training approval decision.

structured_extraction.program_name: Medication Administration Training for Child Care Providers
structured_extraction.program_description: A required pre-service training course for individuals seeking to acquire a Child Care Center License or a Family Child Care Registration in Maryland. The training covers medication administration theory and practice, and is conducted by licensed Maryland Registered Nurses approved by the Office of Child Care.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A six-hour classroom-based training course conducted by licensed Maryland Registered Nurses (MBON-RN) approved by the MSDE Office of Child Care. The course covers both theory and practical components of medication administration for health, safety, and nutrition competency. Participants must pass content and skill tests and receive a certificate upon completion. Over 80 approved registered nurse trainers provide training in various county combinations across Maryland, with day and/or evening scheduling options available. Each approved trainer sets their own fee structure, payment methods, refund policy, cancellation policy, and no-show rescheduling policy. Some trainers offer special needs support services for individualized medical management and treatment plan procedures (such as Type 1 Diabetes management, seizure support, tube feeding, urinary catheter care, and oxygen administration). Some trainers also offer training in Spanish.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals seeking to acquire a Child Care Center License or a Family Child Care Registration in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in medication administration procedures and protocols for child care settings, covering health, safety, and nutrition competency
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland through approved trainers in different regions. Over 80 approved registered nurse trainers provide training in various county combinations across all Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Must be seeking a Child Care Center License or Family Child Care Registration
Must complete all six hours of classroom-based training
Must pass both content and skill tests to receive certificate
Training must be conducted by an MSDE Office of Child Care-approved Registered Nurse instructor
Must be a licensed Maryland Registered Nurse (RN) to become an approved trainer
Trainers must complete an orientation session with the Office of Child Care Nurse Consultant
Must abide by the Office of Child Care's Medication Administration Training Guidance and Standards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals seeking training should contact an approved Medication Administration Trainer in their county or surrounding area using the provided trainer list. Each trainer has their own application and registration process, scheduling, fees, and policies. Applicants should contact their chosen trainer directly using the contact information provided in the trainer list to inquire about class schedules, registration procedures, fees, and payment methods. Interested individuals seeking to become approved trainers must submit a completed Medication Administration Instructor Application and Training Plan to MSDE, DECD Office of Child Care, Licensing Branch, 200 W. Baltimore Street, Baltimore, MD 21201, ATTN: Nurse Consultant.

structured_extraction.program_description: A national program that recognizes and honors top educators with unrestricted cash awards to reward and inspire excellence in education.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each award recipient receives $25,000 in unrestricted funds that can be used at the educator's discretion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Outstanding educators working in Maryland public schools who demonstrate excellence in education.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The $25,000 award is unrestricted, allowing educators to use the funds as they determine.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to educators in Maryland public schools statewide.
requirements_list: Must be an educator in a Maryland public school
Must demonstrate excellence in education
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process details are not provided on this page. Interested educators should contact the Office of Communications for information on how to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: Financial assistance for child care providers pursuing national accreditation through recognized accrediting organizations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to support child care facilities pursuing national accreditation. Eligible organizations include NAEYC (National Association for the Education of Young Children), NECPA (National Early Childhood Program Accreditation), COA After School Accreditation, and NAFCC (National Association for Family Child Care). OCC may consider other accrediting organizations for support. Applicants specify the amount requested for accreditation costs. Association membership fees are the responsibility of the provider/program and are not covered.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Family child care providers and child care center directors seeking national accreditation
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: National accreditation costs for child care facilities, including accreditation fees and requirements for first accreditation, re-accreditation, or annual updates.
requirements_list: Facility must be a licensed Family Child Care provider or Child Care Center
Provider must be pursuing national accreditation through an eligible accrediting organization
All application information must be complete; incomplete applications will be returned
Statement of requirements and fees from the accrediting organization must be submitted
Accreditation Work Plan with steps and timeline must be submitted
Accrediting Organization Provider ID must be provided
For re-accreditation, copy of current accreditation certificate must be submitted
Applicant must certify that they have not received or applied for accreditation funds from any other source
Provider commits to pursue and complete program accreditation through selected organization
Provider must submit certificate of accreditation to the Office of Child Care upon completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the National Accreditation Support Application form (OCC 278) with all required facility information. Submit the completed application along with: (1) Statement of requirements and fees from the accrediting organization; (2) Accreditation Work Plan detailing steps and timeline for achieving accreditation; (3) Accrediting Organization Provider ID; (4) Copy of current accreditation certificate (for re-accreditation applications only). Mail completed application and documentation to Maryland State Department of Education, Office of Child Care, 200 West Baltimore Street, 10th Floor, Baltimore, Maryland 21201. Applicant signature in blue ink is required.

structured_extraction.program_description: Support funds available to family child care providers, child care centers, and school-age only programs as their first step toward accreditation with the National Association for Family Child Care (NAFCC) or other national accrediting organizations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial support paid directly to the accrediting organization on behalf of the program. Funds cover NAFCC application fees, Annual Update fees, renewal application fees, and initial application fees. Funds may not be applied to membership fees, program improvements, staff training, or other accreditation expenses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Family child care providers, child care centers, and school-age only programs seeking national accreditation (such as NAFCC)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Application fees and Annual Update fees for obtaining national accreditation (including NAFCC accreditation). Funds cannot be used for membership fees, program improvements, staff training, or other accreditation-related expenses.
requirements_list: Copy of the accrediting organization's application fee page
Completed Accreditation Work Plan detailing required tasks and due dates
Copy of completed accreditation, re-accreditation, or Annual Update application
Proof of membership in the national accrediting organization
If currently accredited, copy of accreditation certificate
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Gather required documents (accrediting organization fee page, Accreditation Work Plan, completed accreditation application, proof of membership, and current accreditation certificate if applicable). 2. Visit earlychildhood.marylandpublicschools.org and search for 'accreditation support fund.' 3. Select the Accreditation Support Fund link and choose 'Apply Online.' 4. Complete the application and upload all required documentation to the Maryland OneStop Portal. 5. MSDE will review the completed application within 30 days of submission. Applicants can check status anytime using OneStop and will receive updates via emails and OneStop messages. Contact accreditationsupport.fund@maryland.gov for questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: Financial assistance to support child care facilities in obtaining and maintaining national accreditation credentials.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants provided to support child care facilities in achieving and maintaining national accreditation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care facilities seeking national accreditation
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Accreditation application fees, accreditation maintenance costs, and related accreditation support expenses

structured_extraction.program_name: National School Lunch Program (NSLP) and School Breakfast Program (SBP) Training
structured_extraction.program_description: Twice-annual administrative meetings for public school systems that provide updates on USDA regulations and guidance along with professional development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Twice-annual administrative meetings required for local public school systems to receive updates on USDA regulations, guidance, and professional development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local public school systems participating in NSLP and SBP
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and professional development in USDA regulations and guidance for school nutrition programs
requirements_list: Must be a local public school system participating in NSLP and SBP
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participate in required twice-annual administrative meetings scheduled by the Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs

structured_extraction.program_description: State aid program that provides tuition reimbursement for students placed in nonpublic special education schools through the Individualized Education Program (IEP) process. The State covers a portion of the cost of nonpublic special education based on the formula in Maryland Education Article §8-415. The program supports both MSDE-approved day and residential programs as well as individual placements in non-approved or out-of-state special education programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The State reimburses a portion of tuition costs for eligible students placed in nonpublic special education schools through the NTAP program. Students are included in the September 30th enrollment count with code 09 to indicate nonpublic placement. The State's share is calculated according to Maryland Education Article §8-415. Reimbursement covers standard educational and related services, extended school year services, residential services (when applicable), and additional related services and supplemental aids specified in the student's IEP. The specific reimbursable services and costs are detailed on an accompanying cost sheet submitted with each application. Reimbursement applies to MSDE-approved day and residential programs, as well as individual placements in non-approved or out-of-state special education programs with appropriate justification and documentation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications must be submitted within specified timelines depending on entry date and program type
structured_extraction.program_audience: School districts and local education agencies placing students with special education needs in nonpublic schools, including MSDE-approved day and residential programs and individual placements in non-approved or out-of-state programs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition costs for students placed in nonpublic special education day and residential schools, including standard educational and related services, extended school year services, IEP residential services when applicable, and additional related services and supplemental aides as specified in the student's IEP
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide, available to all Maryland school districts and local education agencies
requirements_list: Student must be placed in a nonpublic special education school through the Individualized Education Program (IEP) process
School must be MSDE-approved for day and residential program placements, or justification must be provided for non-approved or out-of-state placements
Applications for ESY or entry dates occurring during July/August must be submitted by September 30
Applications for entry dates on or after September 1 to June 2 must be submitted within 30 calendar days of entry date
Applications for entry dates between June 3 and June 30 must be submitted by July 7
Discharge applications must be submitted within 30 calendar days of discharge date
Service revision applications must be submitted within 30 calendar days of service revision date
An approved cost sheet must accompany each application

For individual placements in non-approved or out-of-state programs, required documentation includes: approved cost sheet, IEP team minutes supporting placement, letter from service-providing school stating ability to implement FAPE in least restrictive environment, and copy of mediation or due process agreement if applicable
LEA Special Education Supervisor/Director or designee signature required to authorize submission and assure compliance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: School districts submit applications to MSDE for nonpublic special education placements. Applications must include completed NTAP application forms (separate forms for MSDE-approved day/residential programs versus individual non-approved or out-of-state placements), an accompanying approved cost sheet, and supporting documentation. For new or renewal individual placements in non-approved or out-of-state programs, districts must also submit IEP team minutes, a letter from the school confirming ability to provide FAPE, and documentation of any mediation or due process agreements. The LEA Special Education Supervisor/Director or designee must sign and date the application to authorize submission and verify accuracy of all information. Applications are reviewed and processed according to MSDE directions and guidelines. Specific submission timelines depend on the entry date and application type (new, renewal, re-entry, discharge, service revision, or correction). MSDE may audit and investigate application contents and supporting documentation. Discrepancies or noncompliance findings may result in requirement for refund of state funds.

structured_extraction.program_description: OBVS provides employment, vocational rehabilitation, transition, independent living, and specialized services for individuals whose primary disability is vision loss, including those who are blind, vision impaired, or deaf-blind.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: OBVS provides four main service areas: (1) Employment or vocational rehabilitation (VR) services to help people with disabilities obtain competitive employment; (2) Transition services for Students with Disabilities, which prepare students to move from school to post-school life; (3) Independent Living Older Blind (ILOB) programs for people age 55 and over to become independent in their homes and communities; and (4) Maryland Business Enterprise Program for the Blind (BEP), which prepares individuals with vision loss to operate retail concession, food service, and vending operations in federal and State facilities. Services include career guidance and exploration, assistive technology such as screen reading software and magnifiers, career training or academic education, independent living skills training including safe cooking and personal care management, orientation and mobility instruction, and job placement assistance. The Vocational Rehabilitation program receives 78.7% of its funding through a grant from the U.S. Department of Education (Federal fiscal year 2024: $60,204,299) with the remaining 21.3% ($14,999,444) funded by State appropriations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who are blind, vision impaired, or deaf-blind and residents of Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Career guidance, assistive technology, career training, academic education, independent living skills training, orientation and mobility instruction, and job placement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services available statewide through DORS offices located throughout Maryland. OBVS Regional Offices: Baltimore (410-554-9217) serving Baltimore City and Baltimore, Cecil, Howard & Harford Counties; Wheaton (301-949-3750) serving Allegany, Carroll, Frederick, Garrett, Montgomery & Washington Counties; Annapolis (410-974-7604) serving Anne Arundel, Calvert, Caroline, Charles, Dorchester, Kent, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico & Worcester Counties.
requirements_list: Primary disability must be vision loss (blindness or vision impairment)
Must be eligible for DORS services
Employment Services and Student Employment Services are subject to eligibility requirements
Note: There may be a waiting list for some DORS services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To request services, go to dors.maryland.gov and select 'Request DORS Services.' The Request DORS Services form can be completed by anyone – the job seeker or student themselves, a parent or family member, a medical provider, a teacher, or other advocate. Once the form is received, you will be contacted via text, email, or letter and assigned to the appropriate staff. You will receive a follow-up email or phone call to schedule your intake meeting where a DORS counselor will gather information and determine your eligibility. If eligible, you will be assigned a counselor or teacher in your community. You can also contact your local DORS office directly to request services. If you are on a waiting list, you will be given information about programs and services that may be able to help you while waiting.

structured_extraction.program_name: Outdoor, Nature-Based Child Care License Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A four-year pilot program that expands access to high-quality early childhood education through outdoor, nature-based programs offering full-day, year-round early learning experiences in outdoor settings. The program licenses outdoor, nature-based early learning and child care programs to investigate the benefits of outdoor, nature-based child care and learning environments. Between 5 and 10 outdoor nature-based early learning and child care programs will be selected to participate during the first year of the pilot program. The pilot operates under COMAR 13A.14.15 regulations with modifications to accommodate the unique nature of outdoor settings.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a license pathway to operate outdoor, nature-based child care, along with licensing support, training opportunities, and technical assistance for child care providers to establish and operate outdoor, nature-based early learning programs. Selected providers receive a pilot license (or provisional license) to operate outdoor child care programs with maximum capacity of 12 children. Training includes Nature-Based Teacher Certification (36-clock hours online course or program approved by the Department, June 23–July 31) and Wilderness First Aid & CPR courses (hybrid, August 17, through American Red Cross or equivalent program). Participating providers receive comprehensive policy and procedure guidance, resources, risk benefit assessment support, guidance documents and comprehensive policy templates, and ongoing technical assistance throughout the four-year pilot period. Support from MSDE Office of Child Care includes application review, site inspections, and ongoing compliance oversight. The program selects between 5 and 10 programs in the first year. Priority is given to: (1) existing outdoor, nature-based early learning and child care programs licensed as camps by Maryland Department of Health; (2) existing licensed child care centers or registered family child care homes participating in Maryland EXCELS Program seeking to expand into outdoor, nature-based early learning; (3) areas with few or limited licensed early child care programs; and (4) areas where licensed early child care programs are at or near full capacity.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers and early childhood educators who are passionate about outdoor education and serving Maryland children. Priority given to existing outdoor, nature-based programs licensed as camps by Maryland Department of Health, existing licensed child care centers or registered family child care homes in Maryland EXCELS Program, and programs in areas with few licensed early child care options or where programs are at or near full capacity. Providers serving diverse populations and geographic areas (rural, urban, and suburban) across Maryland are prioritized.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Providers use the pilot license and support to establish and operate outdoor, nature-based child care programs offering full-day, year-round early learning experiences serving children ages 3 and older in outdoor settings with a maximum capacity of 12 children at any one time. Funds support programming that demonstrates innovative, nature-centered practices including risky play, nature exploration, and outdoor skill development. Programs must comply with all health, safety, and environmental standards while maintaining comprehensive policies addressing outdoor-specific requirements such as weather protocols, emergency sheltering, campfire activities, water access, sanitation, and child supervision in outdoor environments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland. Priority given to programs serving a variety of geographic areas across the state, including a mix of rural, urban, and suburban programs. Programs may be permanently located or roaming programs where resources are brought to the site each day. Priority consideration given to areas where there are few or limited licensed early child care programs and areas where licensed programs are at or near full capacity with restricted access due to enrollment waitlists.
requirements_list: Must be a child care provider or early childhood education program (non-profit, for-profit, or government entity)
Must be willing to participate in the four-year pilot program
Must demonstrate commitment to outdoor, nature-centered educational practices
Must serve children ages 3 and older in outdoor, nature-based settings
Must have maximum capacity of 12 children at any one time
Must have at least 4,000 square feet of natural space with minimum 75 square feet per child for vigorous and active play
Must staff the program at all times with two child care teachers
At least one child care teacher must hold current wilderness first aid and CPR certification and complete 36-clock hours of outdoor, nature-based teacher certification training
Must comply with all applicable zoning, health, safety, and environmental standards of state and local jurisdiction
Must conduct and maintain daily visual inspections of program areas before children arrive
Must have method to remove or mitigate hazards including overhead branches, hazardous materials, wildlife, and other safety threats
Must have adequate communication system enabling staff to communicate with other staff, emergency services (911, poison control), Department, and parents/guardians
Must provide adequate bathroom facilities (portable chemical toilet, public facility toilet, or compliant backcountry toileting)
Must provide approved diapering area separate from food storage and play areas
Must provide safe potable water for drinking, food preparation, handwashing, and sanitizing
Must provide approved rest areas with waterproof tarps and age-appropriate mats
Must maintain safe food storage at approved temperatures
Must provide safe medication storage and documentation
Must provide families with list of required outdoor clothing and equipment
Must not operate when MSDE Child Care Weather Watch chart is in red zone for Heat Index or yellow/red zone for Wind-Chill Factor
Must have plans to relocate or seek shelter during inclement weather and emergencies
Must provide reasonable accommodations for children with disabilities or special health care needs
Must submit risk benefit assessment identifying site hazards and mitigation methods for risky play activities
Must have written landowner permission and necessary permits for campfire activities
Must have signed parent/guardian fire hazard waivers for each child before any campfire activities
Must train staff in safe fire practices provided by U.S. Forest Service
Must maintain first-aid kits near campfires with fire-specific supplies
Must provide parents/guardians with handbook containing written policies and procedures
Must require parents/guardians to sign risk waiver acknowledging potential hazards and risks
Must store all records in manner protecting from weather damage

Must submit annual evaluation data to Department by October 1st including number of children and families served, EXCELS participation, Child Care Scholarship Program participation, infant and early childhood mental health support services participation, and state funded public prekindergarten participation
Must comply with all COMAR 13A.16 Child Care Center requirements or request variance approval
Operator may not operate more than one pilot program
If operating educational program, must comply with educational program requirements of COMAR 13A.16.16
Must have land use agreement if program not on owned property
Must have sufficient workers' compensation insurance and liability insurance (strongly encouraged)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested providers should review application materials, COMAR 13A.14.15 regulations, and resources available on the program hub at earlychildhood.marylandpublicschools.org. Complete the Department-approved application form available at the program hub. Submit the following with application: (1) Completed application form; (2) Any requested variances to COMAR 13A.16 regulations using the variance request process; (3) Comprehensive policies and procedures for all program requirements listed in COMAR 13A.14.15.08; (4) Any additional documents required by Department to ensure child health, safety, and welfare including risk benefit assessment, proof of land use agreement if not on owned property, site plan, and documentation of operator qualifications. Email completed application to odalc@marylandpublicschools.org by 5:00 p.m. on June 30, 2025. MSDE Office of Child Care reviews applications and conducts site inspections. Within 60 days after completing evaluation and inspection procedures, MSDE issues pilot license, provisional license, or denial notice. All staff must pass federal and state criminal background checks and child/adult abuse and neglect record reviews before license issuance. Selected providers participate in the four-year pilot, receive training and technical assistance, and submit annual evaluation data.

structured_extraction.program_description: Pathways provides educational support services for job seekers with Autism through a collaboration between DORS and community colleges throughout Maryland. The program supports students in credit and certificate classes with adjustment to college life, career guidance, employment and communication skills development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Educational support services including adjustment to college life, assessment services, career guidance and counseling, employment and communication skills training through individual and group sessions at participating community colleges. Students enroll in credit/certificate classes and register with the Disability Support Services (DSS) office at their college. The DORS Pathways coordinator works with students, families, DORS counselors, DSS staff and faculty.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with documented Autism diagnosis seeking post-secondary education at participating community colleges
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational support and skill development for college success and employment
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at Anne Arundel Community College, Community College of Baltimore County, Howard Community College, Prince George's Community College, College of Southern Maryland, and Montgomery College
requirements_list: Have a documented diagnosis of Autism
Have a DORS Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) that supports college as part of the employment plan
Register with the Disability Support Services (DSS) program at their college
Attend weekly group sessions and schedule classes around this standing appointment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your DORS Counselor or local DORS office for more information or request DORS Services. Register with Disability Support Services at participating community college and work with the DORS Pathways coordinator.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide network of 24 Patty Centers (formerly named Family Support Centers) in 14 counties that provide free educational and health-related services to parents and their children ages birth through three. The centers promote optimal child development, help adults develop effective parenting skills, provide supportive parent networks, and connect families to community resources and agencies. Services include infant and toddler care assessment, parent education, adult education, family literacy, job readiness training, health education and referral, home visits, peer support, and service coordination. Funded by the Maryland State Department of Education, U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, private foundations, corporations, and individuals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free services including quality infant and toddler care and assessment while parents are on site, parent education classes, adult education and family literacy programs, job readiness training, health education and referrals to community resources, home visits for some services, peer support groups, and service coordination to connect families with community agencies and resources. Services are provided at no cost to eligible families.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Parents and their children ages birth through three residing in participating Maryland counties
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services support optimal child development, effective parenting skills, school and employment goals, family life goals, and connection to community resources and agencies. Includes parent education, adult education, family literacy training, job readiness programs, health education, infant and toddler care assessment, peer support, and service coordination.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in 24 Patty Centers located across 14 Maryland counties including Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Carroll, Cecil, Dorchester, Frederick, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, Talbot, Washington, Worcester, Calvert, Caroline, and St. Mary's counties.
requirements_list: Parents and children ages birth through three
Reside in one of the participating counties with an active Patty Center
Parents must participate in services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Patty Center directly or visit the Maryland Family Network website at marylandfamilynetwork.org to find your local center. Each center has its own director and contact information. Services may be offered on a walk-in or appointment basis depending on the specific center.

structured_extraction.program_name: Pre-Employment Autism Support (PEAS) and Counseling on Post-Secondary Education Opportunities (CPSEO)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Pre-Employment Autism Support (PEAS) program provides instruction in self-advocacy and social skills training to Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS) students with Autism through classroom and other activities that expose students to soft skills needed to obtain and maintain employment. Students also participate in the Counseling on Post-Secondary Education Opportunities (CPSEO) program, which introduces them to education, training, and employment options available after high school, including apprenticeships, career training, job placement, and college, with college tours included.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Classroom and activity-based instruction in self-advocacy and social skills development designed to help Pre-ETS students with Autism obtain and maintain employment. Services include participation in the Counseling on Post-Secondary Education Opportunities (CPSEO) program featuring college tours and exploration of apprenticeships, career training, job placement, and college options. Students participate in activities that help develop the soft skills needed to get and keep a job.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pre-Employment Transition Services students with Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis, ages 14-21, currently enrolled in high school, post-secondary education, or recognized educational programs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Self-advocacy and social skills training for employment readiness, post-secondary education counseling, career exploration activities, and soft skills development
requirements_list: Documented Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis
Currently enrolled in high school (including homeschool or alternative secondary education program), post-secondary education program, or recognized educational program such as a trade school
At least 14 years old but less than 22 years old
Has an Individualized Education Program (IEP), 504 plan, or medical records that document disability
Eligible for Pre-Employment Transition Services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your DORS Counselor or local office to enroll in Pre-Employment Transition Services and PEAS/CPSEO program activities, or request DORS Services via QR code provided by DORS.

structured_extraction.program_description: Five specific services designed to help students with disabilities identify their career interests and enhance their awareness of the world of work. Services include job exploration counseling, instruction in self-advocacy, counseling on post-secondary education opportunities, workplace readiness training, and work-based learning experiences.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Five specific short-term services provided at no cost to students: (1) Job Exploration Counseling to explore skills, interests, and career opportunities through interest inventories, labor market information, and sessions about specific in-demand occupations; (2) Instruction in Self-Advocacy to learn communication strategies, rights, and responsibilities, including sessions on self-awareness, problem-solving, and effective communication such as the Youth Leadership Forum; (3) Counseling on Post-Secondary Education Opportunities to gain awareness of training options and career pathways after high school, guidance on choosing the right type of training, and information on accessing disability supports; (4) Workplace Readiness Training to learn skills for workplace success including peer and supervisor interaction, strategies for timeliness, and professional behavior and dress; and (5) Work-Based Learning Experiences to participate in work opportunities with local employers outside of the traditional school setting. Services vary based on individual needs and local availability. Services are provided by DORS staff or approved community rehabilitation partners (CRPs).
structured_extraction.contact_name: Jessica Markum, Staff Specialist for Students and Transitioning Youth; Muttasim Fadl, Employment Services Specialist for Students with Blindness or Vision Impairments; MSDE Division of Rehabilitation Services Headquarters
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students with disabilities between 14 and 21 years old who are enrolled in secondary school (including homeschool or other alternative secondary education program), post-secondary education program, or other recognized educational program and have not graduated or withdrawn, and have a documented disability. Includes transition-age students who are blind or visually impaired.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Career exploration, self-advocacy training, education counseling, workplace readiness skills development, and work-based learning experiences to help students transition from school to post-school life and employment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local DORS offices throughout Maryland. Services are also available virtually. DORS is located in more than 20 offices around Maryland.
requirements_list: At least 14 years old and no more than 21 years old

Currently enrolled in secondary school (including homeschool or other alternative secondary education program), post-secondary education program, or other recognized educational program, and have not graduated or withdrawn
Have a documented disability (on an Individualized Education Program [IEP], a 504 plan, or medical records)
Students who are blind or visually impaired are also eligible as transition-age students
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Request services by completing the Request DORS Services form at dors.maryland.gov. The form can be completed by anyone: the student, parent, family member, school staff, medical provider, or teacher. You can also call your local DORS office for assistance with the form over the phone. Step 2: Within about 10 business days, DORS will contact you via text message and email through Sara, the client communication system. Texts come from 34459 and emails from sara@sara.digital. Select 'I accept' to consent to texts or emails. You can also text 95424 after receiving initial contact to connect directly with your DORS counselor. Step 3: Provide required documentation including Social Security Number, proof of disability, proof of school enrollment, and proof of age, then sign the Pre-ETS Consent to Participate form and submit via the secure SARA system. Step 4: DORS staff reviews the documentation and forwards qualifying students to the local DORS office. Step 5: A counselor from the local DORS office contacts the student and family to schedule a virtual or in-person intake meeting to discuss career interests, service needs, and plan their Pre-ETS services. Allow 10 business days for a DORS representative to respond.

structured_extraction.program_description: The state provides grants to support high-quality full-day Pre-K programs for three- and four-year-old children from families earning incomes at or below 300% of the Federal Poverty Level. The program ensures access to early education opportunities that prepare all children for kindergarten and promote school readiness and long-term academic success.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are provided to support the operation of high-quality full-day Pre-K programs. Funding supports both traditional Pre-K slots and Pre-Kindergarten Expansion Blueprint funding. The program provides no-cost access to Pre-K for eligible children from families earning at or below 300% of the Federal Poverty Level. Grantees include public school systems, Head Start programs, nonprofit organizations, and private child care providers across all 24 Maryland counties. Awards vary by provider and include slots designated for expansion and capacity building initiatives.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Three- and four-year-old children from families earning incomes at or below 300% of the Federal Poverty Level; Pre-K program providers and grantees including public school systems, Head Start programs, nonprofit organizations, and private child care providers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for high-quality full-day Pre-K program operations, ensuring children are ready to learn and successful when entering kindergarten. Funding includes Pre-Kindergarten Expansion Blueprint funding for program expansion and capacity building.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland through approved grantees in all 24 counties including Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Baltimore City, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Somerset, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester counties.
requirements_list: Child must be three or four years old
Family income must be at or below 300% of the Federal Poverty Level
Enrollment through approved Pre-K program grantees
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families can enroll in Pre-K programs through their chosen approved grantee provider. The Maryland State Department of Education maintains a list of funded Pre-K providers by county. Families should contact their chosen provider directly for enrollment information and procedures. Grantees are selected through a competitive grant process administered by the Maryland State Department of Education.

structured_extraction.program_description: High-quality full-day prekindergarten for three- and four-year-old children from families earning incomes at or below 300% of the Federal Poverty Level, available at no cost to eligible families. The program prepares children for kindergarten and promotes school readiness and academic success. A sliding scale is also available for Tier II families (301-600% of FPL) with subsidized costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Full-day prekindergarten services provided at no cost to eligible Tier I families (three- and four-year-old children whose families earn at or below 300% of the Federal Poverty Level, or children experiencing homelessness). Tier II families (four-year-old children from families earning 301-600% of FPL) receive subsidized full-day Pre-K on a sliding scale. In FY 2026, Tier II is partially implemented for families earning 301-360% of FPL. Family contributions for Tier II in FY 2026 are 10% of the $14,473 per-pupil cost (approximately $1,447.30 annually or $144.73 monthly). In FY 2027, sliding scale ranges from 10-40% of the $19,950 per-pupil cost, capped at no more than 7% of annual family income. Tier III families (income above 600% FPL) pay full program cost. Families have access to multiple Pre-K options through approved grantees across the state. Children with disabilities and multilingual learners within 300-600% FPL are designated as Tier I for FY 2024-2026. Children experiencing homelessness are Tier I by definition and do not require income verification.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling enrollment
structured_extraction.program_audience: Three- and four-year-old children whose family incomes are at or below 300% of the Federal Poverty Level (Tier I), four-year-old children from families earning 301-600% of FPL (Tier II), and children experiencing homelessness.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: High-quality full-day prekindergarten instruction and educational services (6.5 hours per school day) to prepare children for kindergarten entry. Programs may blend and braid funding with Head Start, Child Care Scholarship, Title I, and other federal, state, and local funding to support wraparound services (before- and after-care) and infant/toddler programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through Pre-K grantees in all Maryland counties. Families can enroll in private provider settings in the county in which they live. If capacity is not available in home LEA, families may seek enrollment with private providers in their jurisdiction.
requirements_list: Child must be three or four years old (Tier I); four years old (Tier II); or three or four years old (Tier III)
Family income must be at or below 300% of Federal Poverty Level (Tier I) or 301-600% of FPL (Tier II)
Children experiencing homelessness are automatically Tier I regardless of income
Children with disabilities with an Extended IFSP or IEP requiring group services are Tier I regardless of income
All children except those experiencing homelessness must provide proof of income at time of enrollment
For Tier II families, income verification documents required include W-2, 1099, pay stubs, unemployment verification, or tax return
Child must be enrolled in full-day (not part-time) Pre-K program to receive Blueprint funding
Family income is determined at time of enrollment and does not adjust during the program year even if income changes
For LEA providers: income verification may use FARM eligibility or Direct Certification (SNAP, TANF, or Foster Care documentation)

For private providers: income verification may use approved Child Care Scholarships, SNAP eligibility, Head Start income eligibility forms, or program-developed income form listing family size, parent/guardian income, and employment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families enroll directly in the Pre-K program option of their choice through approved grantees. At the time of enrollment, families must provide income verification documentation to determine tier status (Tier I, II, or III). LEAs and private providers use the MSDE Pre-K Cost Calculator to determine family tier and, for Tier II families, the family share based on a sliding scale tied to total family income and household size. For Tier II families who choose to pay a portion of costs, providers must have the family sign an agreement acknowledging the tier status and agreed-upon payment schedule (weekly, monthly, or yearly). Families receive a copy of the agreement. The Maryland State Department of Education ensures families are aware of all available Pre-K options and the enrollment process through approved grantees.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Prekindergarten Expansion program grants all three- and four-year-old children from families earning incomes at or below 300 percent of the Federal Poverty Level access to high-quality full-day Pre-K at no cost.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible children receive access to high-quality full-day Pre-K at no cost to their families.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Three- and four-year-old children from families earning at or below 300 percent of Federal Poverty Level
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pre-K education and services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide
requirements_list: Child must be three or four years old
Family income must be at or below 300 percent of Federal Poverty Level

structured_extraction.program_description: The Prekindergarten Expansion program, authorized by the Blueprint, provides free full-day pre-kindergarten services to all three- and four-year-old children from families earning incomes at or below 300 percent of the Federal Poverty Level.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free full-day pre-kindergarten services provided to eligible children. The program covers tuition and related costs for high-quality pre-K programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with three- and four-year-old children earning at or below 300 percent of the Federal Poverty Level
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Full-day pre-kindergarten programs and services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Child must be three or four years old
Family income must be at or below 300% Federal Poverty Level
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Details available through the program webpage

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program that provides funding to local education agencies and private providers to deliver high-quality full-day prekindergarten and school readiness services for three- and four-year-old children from families earning at or below 300% of the Federal Poverty Level.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding provided to local education agencies (LEAs) and qualified private providers (including Head Start, Center Based, and Family Child Care programs) to administer and deliver high-quality full-day prekindergarten programming and school readiness services. Grant awards average $400,000, with approximately $19,950 per full-day slot for three- and four-year-olds. Programs must deliver a minimum of 6.5 hours of instruction per day for 180 school days per year. Funded programs must serve children ages three and four from families earning at or below 300% Federal Poverty Level at no cost for the instructional day. Total funding available: $26,644,000 with an estimated 50 grants available. Grant period: July 1, 2026 - June 30, 2027.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Wednesday, March 11, 2026. No later than 5:00 pm EDT.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local education agencies, Head Start programs, and qualified private child care providers that hold a valid license or registration and will deliver prekindergarten services. Providers must participate in the Maryland EXCELS program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports the delivery of high-quality full-day prekindergarten educational programming and school readiness services. Approved uses include: salaries and fringe benefits for teaching staff at LEA-comparable rates; equipment, materials, and supplies; reasonable rental/mortgage and utility costs (prorated by square footage); technology costs (up to 10% of total); costs for maintaining Maryland or national accreditation or Maryland EXCELS ratings; contracts for screening and intervention services; evaluation and monitoring costs (up to 5%); indirect costs (up to 15% for nonprofits, 10% for other grantees); at least one meal per day meeting CACFP requirements; academic field trips; and approved professional learning activities for instructional staff. Funds may not be used for supplanting existing program funds, capital improvements, costs incurred prior to grant approval, or transportation (except field trips).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland to serve children from families with household incomes up to 300% of Federal Poverty Level. Priority consideration given to programs in areas of the state with unmet need for prekindergarten services.
requirements_list: Hold a valid license or registration (if applicable)
Be a Head Start program or qualified vendor as defined in COMAR 13a.06.02
Deliver high-quality prekindergarten services in alignment with The Blueprint for Maryland's Future
Meet Maryland EXCELS quality standards (Level 3 or higher for private providers; Level 4 or higher for public providers)
Serve children ages three and four from families earning at or below 300% Federal Poverty Level
Participate in Maryland EXCELS program
Provide full-day instruction (minimum 6.5 hours per day) for 180 school days per year

Employ lead teachers meeting Blueprint requirements: must hold bachelor's degree in early childhood education or related field, or have 10+ years documented ECE experience (with CLASS assessment requirements), or be P-3 certified
Employ assistant teachers (for classrooms with 10+ students) meeting Blueprint requirements: high school diploma plus CDA or associate degree in ECE or 5+ years documented experience
Charge no tuition for 6.5-hour instructional day (tuition may only apply to wrap-around services)
Use valid and reliable child assessment tools to monitor progress
Provide health screenings and referrals in vision, hearing, speech/language, general health, and physical development
Offer or coordinate family support services including parenting support, physical/mental health services, and early intervention
Include measurable SMART goals addressing standards alignment, instructional practice, quality improvement, and child outcomes
Develop and implement professional learning plan with minimum 20 hours of training for instructional staff
Maintain or achieve Maryland EXCELS Level 5 rating within timeframe specified in application
Provide evidence of community need through recent needs assessment or market analysis
Hire lead teachers by July 1, 2026 to avoid disruption in grant funds
Submit Memorandum of Understanding (by September 30, 2026) for LEAs and private providers specifying collaboration plan
Meet all grant requirements before start of grant year and before invoices can be paid
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants must review the Grant Information Guide released January 21, 2026 (amended March 6, 2026). The application is submitted electronically through Qualtrics at https://msde.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0qxUC1IT7xwk08C. Applications must be submitted by March 11, 2026 at 5:00 pm EDT. All applicants must complete initial eligibility questions confirming program has valid license/registration and meets Maryland EXCELS requirements. New applicants and existing grantees without a track record of success must complete the full application covering 10 sections: Program Eligibility, Evidence of Need, Measurable Goals, Program Quality and Curriculum, Plan of Operation, Staffing and Key Personnel, Project Timeline, Collaboration and Sustainability, Fiscal Systems and Controls, and Budget/Budget Narrative. Applicants seeking renewal or expansion of existing programs with demonstrated track record of success may submit modified short form application (minimum score: 45 points). Full applications require minimum score of 80 points. MSDE encourages timely submission to increase likelihood of award. Customer service support sessions and office hours available to provide guidance on program requirements and application completion. Applicants may save progress in browser and return to complete application later on same device and browser. Before submitting, applicants must review all answers and may download responses. Required appendices must be uploaded in Qualtrics system before submission. Final award is contingent on applicant meeting all grant requirements and having approved budget. Lead teachers must be hired by July 1, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Professional Learning in Early Literacy Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding to Local School Systems to support rigorous professional learning for Prekindergarten teachers, assistant teachers, coaches, specialists, special educators, Head Start teachers, and private childcare providers of 3-year-olds and 4-year-olds. Professional learning focuses on strategies based on the science of reading research to align with the Maryland Leads Science of Reading initiative.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $40,000 to $80,000 per award. A total of $1,000,000 is available with an estimated 12 to 24 grants awarded. Funds support professional learning, training, and materials for Prekindergarten educators on Science of Reading strategies. Funds must be obligated by December 30, 2022. Allowable budget categories include salaries and wages, contracted services with approved Science of Reading vendors, supplies and materials, other charges, equipment, and indirect costs. All proposed budget line items must align with program activities and be necessary, reasonable, and cost-effective. The MSDE reserves the right to consider geographic distribution when making awards.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 5:00 p.m. EST on October 11, 2022
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local School Systems seeking to provide professional development to Pre-K and early childhood educators, including prekindergarten teachers, assistant teachers, coaches, specialists, special educators, Head Start teachers, and private childcare teachers and supervisors/directors of 3-year-olds and 4-year-olds. School administrators and childcare directors are also encouraged to participate.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support professional learning, training, and materials for Prekindergarten teachers, assistant teachers, coaches, specialists, special educators, Head Start teachers, and private childcare providers on science of reading research strategies. Eligible budget categories include salaries and wages for key personnel, contracted services from approved Science of Reading vendors, supplies and materials for training, equipment, other necessary costs for professional learning implementation, and indirect costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland Local School Systems. The Maryland State Department of Education reserves the right to consider geographic distribution when making award decisions.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Local School System (LSS)

Professional learning must be targeted to meet the needs of Pre-K teachers, assistant teachers, coaches, specialists, special educators, Head Start teachers, and private childcare teachers of 3-year-olds and 4-year-olds
Training must be aligned to the Science of Reading research
Professional learning plan must clearly align to the LEA's Maryland Leads grant application science of reading plan
An approved Science of Reading vendor must be identified to deliver the training
Must include a robust plan to engage private childcare providers and Head Start staff
Facilitator must be clearly qualified to lead the training
Complete project timeline required for all grant activities including evaluation
Clear and robust evaluation plan required to measure program success
All grant tasks must be assigned to qualified personnel with defined roles and responsibilities
One-page resume required for all key personnel
Supporting documentation required for education support professionals data
Signed C-1-25 MSDE budget form must be submitted
Signed recipient assurances page must be submitted
Scope of work for approved Science of Reading vendor must be included
Funds must be obligated by December 30, 2022
Budget line items must align with program activities and rates must be reasonable and accurate
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants complete the Professional Learning in Early Literacy Grant application form with sections covering: (1) Proposal Cover Page with LEA information and contact details; (2) Extent of Need section identifying the problem and evidence of impact; (3) Goals and Outcomes aligned to science of reading research; (4) Implementation Plan describing professional learning opportunities, vendor selection, facilitator qualifications, format and schedule, and outreach to Head Start and private childcare providers; (5) Project Timeline for all proposed activities including evaluation; (6) Evaluation and Dissemination plan; (7) Management Plan assigning tasks to qualified personnel; and (8) detailed Budget and Budget Narrative by category (salaries/wages, contracted services, supplies/materials, other charges, equipment, indirect costs). Required appendices include scope of work for approved Science of Reading vendor, one-page resumes of key personnel, supporting documentation for education support professionals data, signed C-1-25 MSDE budget form, and signed recipient assurances page. MSDE holds optional customer service support sessions to provide an overview and answer questions about the application process. Completed applications must be submitted via email by 5:00 p.m. EST on October 11, 2022. Applications are scored on a 100-point rubric: Extent of Need (10 points), Goals (20 points), Implementation Plan (30 points), Evaluation and Dissemination (10 points), Management Plan (10 points), and Budget (20 points). Awards are made based on scoring and consideration of geographic distribution.

structured_extraction.program_description: USDA Team Nutrition training grant implemented from 2016 through 2019 targeting middle schools in five school systems. The grant provided training in culinary and food service operations, Smarter Lunchrooms strategies, food tasting events, and nutrition education to increase student selection and consumption of vegetables and fruits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: USDA Team Nutrition training grant providing training and technical assistance in culinary and food service operations, Smarter Lunchrooms strategies, food tasting events, and nutrition education. Grant partners included five targeted school systems, University of Maryland Food Supplement Nutrition Education, and University of Maryland Baltimore Division of Growth and Nutrition.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Middle schools in Allegany, Baltimore City, Montgomery, Prince George' s, and Wicomico school systems
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Culinary and food service operations training, Smarter Lunchrooms strategies, food tasting events, nutrition education, and family engagement wellness toolkit
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Allegany, Baltimore City, Montgomery, Prince George' s, and Wicomico school systems
requirements_list: Must be a middle school in one of the five targeted school systems
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Grant period was 2016 through 2019; this program is no longer actively accepting applications

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary support program from the Maryland State Department of Education's Division of Early Childhood that empowers child care providers and Local Education Agencies with technical assistance, coaching, and resources to understand and meet requirements for the Prekindergarten Expansion Grant. Push to Pre-K provides step-by-step guidance to reduce barriers and help providers secure grant funding to offer high-quality prekindergarten and school readiness services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Push to Pre-K provides technical assistance and coaching to eligible Local Education Agencies (LEAs) and child care programs (including child care centers, family child care homes, Head Start programs, Montessori schools, and faith-based programs) that are licensed or registered through MSDE. The program offers: (1) MSDE Pre-K Specialists providing step-by-step guidance on grant application process; (2) Technical assistance and coaching on meeting licensing and Maryland EXCELS quality rating requirements; (3) Resources and guidance on components of high-quality educational programs including curriculum, assessments, lesson planning, qualified teaching staff requirements, and comprehensive services; (4) Support for understanding and complying with serious health and safety regulations (capacity, child protection, prohibition of injurious treatment, supervision, group size and staffing); (5) Guidance on achieving and maintaining Maryland EXCELS Level 3 minimum rating with a 5-year plan to reach Level 5. The program supports applications for the Prekindergarten Expansion Grant, which provides competitive grant funding for LEAs and private providers to administer high-quality prekindergarten for 3- and 4-year-old children. Grant funding is based on licensed capacity at xx,xxx per slot with 180 instructional days per year and 6.5 hours daily. Funds must be used for educational programming led by qualified teaching staff implementing evidence-based curriculum aligned with Maryland Early Learning Standards.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Dr. Nykia Washington, Prekindergarten and Mixed Delivery Program Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Education Agencies (LEAs) and child care programs (including child care centers, family child care homes, Head Start programs, Montessori schools, and faith-based programs) that are licensed or registered through MSDE and seeking to implement high-quality prekindergarten programs for 3- and 4-year-old children.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical assistance and training to help providers understand and meet licensing requirements, Maryland EXCELS quality rating standards, and educational program components. Guidance on implementing evidence-based curriculum aligned with Maryland Early Learning Standards, conducting formative and summative assessments, developing developmentally appropriate lesson plans, creating well-equipped classrooms, establishing qualified teaching staff, and implementing comprehensive services for children and families.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties eligible. The Prekindergarten Expansion Grant provides funding for eligible providers throughout the State of Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Local Education Agency (LEA) or child care program that is licensed or registered through MSDE
Must hold a valid license or registration

Must not have incurred any serious health and safety violations (defined as non-compliance in capacity, child protection, prohibition of injurious treatment, supervision, or group size and staffing on two or more inspections in a 12-month period)
Must participate in Maryland EXCELS and have published rating of at least Level 3 with a plan to achieve Level 5 within five years

For Lead Teachers: Bachelor's degree in early childhood education, child development, or related field; OR bachelor's degree from another country verified as equivalent; OR bachelor's degree in unrelated field with early childhood qualifications; OR 10 years of experience (must earn associate degree by July 1, 2030) and meet minimum CLASS assessment scores (Emotional Support 5.00, Classroom Organization 5.00, Instructional Support 3.00)

For Assistant Teachers (by July 1, 2027): High school diploma and either Child Development Associate (CDA) with preschool designation, associate degree in early childhood education/child development, or 15+ years documented early childhood services experience
Program must implement evidence-based curriculum aligned with Maryland Early Learning Standards and Maryland College and Career Ready Standards
Must implement formal assessment system with both formative and summative assessments
Must maintain child-to-staff ratio of no more than 10:1
Must maintain class size of no more than 20 with minimum one lead teacher per classroom
Must provide 6.5-hour full-day instructional program
Must provide 20 hours professional learning annually for all instructional staff
Must provide developmentally appropriate lesson plans aligned to Early Learning Standards with differentiated instruction
Must provide screenings and referrals for vision, hearing, speech and language, health, and physical development
Must offer comprehensive services either directly or through coordination with local school systems or health/social services
Must maintain ongoing program evaluation to ensure continuous quality improvement
If faith-based provider: must keep explicitly religious activities separate in time/location from Pre-K instruction and voluntary
All equipment must be in good repair
Curriculum training and supports must be provided for instructional staff
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Push to Pre-K provides a series of technical assistance sessions to help providers understand grant requirements and prepare applications. Steps include: (1) Ensure your program is licensed or registered through MSDE; (2) Apply to Maryland EXCELS if not already participating by visiting marylandexcels.org and completing online application; (3) Work toward Maryland EXCELS Level 3 minimum rating by connecting with Quality Assurance Specialists and addressing licensing compliance issues; (4) Create a 5-year plan documenting pathway from Level 3 to Level 5, accreditation timeline, and professional development goals; (5) Attend Push to Pre-K training sessions on topics including licensing and Maryland EXCELS requirements, components of educational programs, grant writing with goals and outcomes, and fiscal overview; (6) Submit competitive grant application to the Prekindergarten Expansion Grant program when funding opportunity is released, including: extent of need, evidence of impact, goals and outcomes aligned with kindergarten readiness, key personnel and resumes, program location(s) and staffing plan, Maryland EXCELS status and plan, plan of operation, evaluation and dissemination plan, collaboration and sustainability plan, project timeline, detailed budget and budget narrative, and supporting appendices. Support available through Quality Assurance Specialists embedded in licensing offices statewide, Program Coordinators from Johns Hopkins Partnership, and self-service resources including Maryland EXCELS Toolkit, rating checklists, Quick Guides in English/Spanish, and video tutorials.

structured_extraction.program_description: A technical assistance and grant support program that helps child care providers expand their services and access state prekindergarten funding. The program provides guidance on meeting grant requirements and simplifies the application process for Pre-K grants through the support of Pre-K Specialists.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Push to Pre-K provides access to state prekindergarten funding through grants. Pre-K Specialists provide step-by-step guidance through the application process and help providers meet grant requirements to expand their child care services. Funding amounts and specific terms are detailed in the Grant Information Guide. Applicants should review the Grant Information Guide (GIG), verify organizational eligibility, assess technical expertise and financial capacity, and ensure stakeholder support before applying.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers seeking to expand their business and access state prekindergarten funding.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Expanding child care services to include prekindergarten programs funded by the state.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a licensed or license-exempt child care provider
Must meet state requirements for prekindergarten programs
Must have read and understood the Grant Information Guide (GIG)
Organization must be eligible based on eligibility criteria in the GIG
Organization must have the technical expertise, personnel, and financial capacity to successfully provide services as described in the GIG
All organizational stakeholders must be supportive of applying for this grant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Pre-K Specialists guide applicants through every step of the application process. Before beginning the application, applicants should use the Grant Consideration Checklist to verify they can answer 'yes' to key questions: (1) Have I read and understood the Grant Information Guide? (2) Is my organization eligible based on GIG eligibility criteria? (3) Does my organization have the technical expertise, personnel, and financial capacity to provide services as described? (4) Are all stakeholders supportive of applying for this grant? Visit PushToPreK.com or earlychildhood.marylandpublicschools.org for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants that support service delivery coordination at the local level, administered through Local Early Childhood Advisory Councils (ECACs) with support from PDG B-5 funds.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Service delivery coordination at the local level
