Must be opening a child care program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Office of Child Care Regional Licensing Office or contact Angelia L. Bell at abell@marylandpublicschools.org or 410-713-3430 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: The Judith P. Hoyer Early Child Care and Education Enhancement Program (Judy Center Early Learning Hubs)
structured_extraction.program_description: Comprehensive hubs where families engage in learning experiences with children from prenatal through age 5 and access support services. Judy Centers use a multigenerational approach to prepare children for success in school and life by empowering families as their children's primary teachers. The program provides developmental screenings, family learning activities, parenting classes, connections to adult education and workforce development, evidence-based home visiting, and case management with service coordination. The program also provides grants to child care providers for accreditation and staff professional development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Judy Centers are comprehensive, integrated, full-day and full-year early care and education programs. Services include: developmental screenings and assessments; family learning activities and engagement centered on a multigenerational approach; parenting classes and training workshops; connections to adult education and workforce development programs; evidence-based family and child playgroups (minimum 2 per week required); referrals for services and supports (80,367 referrals made in FY2024); early intervention identification; evidence-based home visiting; and case management with families and service coordination with community partners. Full-day services are defined as not less than seven hours or more than 12 hours per day. Judy Centers operate year-round and provide meals during school day, school breaks, weekends, and after-school hours. Health-related services include referrals for dental, vision, and hearing screenings; mental health assessments; physical growth and nutritional assessments; and connections to health insurance and WIC programs. The program also offers grants to child care providers for accreditation and professional development programs for staff.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Kaymi Plank, Judy Center Program Manager; Nancy Garcia, Judy Center Specialist (Spanish language assistance)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children from prenatal through age 5 who live within the school zone where a Judy Center is located. Services prioritize underserved and historically underserved communities, particularly families in Title I school zones. Also serves child care providers who serve at-risk children from birth to age six.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support services and learning experiences for young children and families, including developmental assessments, parent training, connections to community resources, early intervention, adult education and workforce development opportunities, health-related referrals, meals, transportation, case management, and family support services. Grants to child care providers support accreditation and professional development programs for staff.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Judy Center Early Learning Hubs are grant-funded programs located in elementary schools across the state of Maryland. Judy Centers serve children who live within the school zone where the Judy Center is located. As of FY2024, there are 86 Judy Center sites across Maryland. At least one Judy Center is located in each of the 24 Maryland jurisdictions. The program is expanding by nine sites annually through 2025, then 18 sites annually from 2026-2030 as part of the Blueprint for Maryland's Future.
requirements_list: Children must be from prenatal through age 5 (though program focus extends through kindergarten)
Children must live within the school zone where the Judy Center is located
Families must engage with the Judy Center at least 12 times during the fiscal year to be considered served, or be enrolled in formal partner programs
Children with disabilities and their families are fully included with services coordinated through IEP (Individualized Education Program) and IFSP (Individualized Family Service Plan)
All early care and education programs in partnership with the Judy Center must be accredited or pursuing accreditation
Services prioritize Title I and high-needs schools in underserved communities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your closest Judy Center Early Learning Hub directly. Families do not formally apply; they are welcomed to engage with services in their school's designated Judy Center. For general information about the program, contact the Judy Center Program Manager at 410-767-0675 or the Judy Center Specialist (Spanish language assistance available) at 410-767-0785. Each Judy Center location maintains a Steering Committee that meets at least six times annually to coordinate services and partnerships. Contact information for individual Judy Center coordinators by school location is available in the program's contact list.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Ticket to Work program connects people with disabilities who receive Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) with the Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) or community-based Employment Networks (EN). DORS works with participants to develop an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) and provide services including training, career counseling, vocational rehabilitation, job placement, job coaching, benefits counseling, and ongoing support services to help achieve and maintain employment. The program protects participants from Continuing Disability Reviews as long as their Ticket is in use with DORS or an Employment Network and they meet Social Security Administration timely progress requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DORS provides free vocational rehabilitation services to help participants with disabilities achieve employment. Services include development of an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE), job training, career counseling, job placement assistance, job coaching, benefits planning, and ongoing support services necessary to achieve work goals. The program includes built-in work incentives that allow participants to try working without immediately losing benefits, earn more money, and keep health insurance (Medicare for at least 93 months after start of earnings, or Medicaid through the Employed Individuals with Disabilities program). After employment is achieved and the DORS case closes, participants are connected with a partner Employment Network for continued employment support. The program is free and voluntary with no cost to participants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People with disabilities aged 18-64 who receive Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services to support employment achievement and maintenance, including job training, career counseling, vocational rehabilitation, job placement, job coaching, benefits counseling, and ongoing employment support. Program includes work incentives to help individuals maintain health insurance benefits and preserve cash benefits if employment is not sustainable.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide.
requirements_list: Receive Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI)
Be between 18 and 64 years old
Have a valid Ticket to Work assigned to DORS or have DORS sign an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE)
Be making good progress toward employment goals to maintain Continuing Disability Review protection
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the DORS Ticket Coordinator at 410-554-9460 or Ticket.DORS@maryland.gov to learn about the program and request services. Participation is voluntary and there is no cost. DORS staff will work with you to develop an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) outlining services and employment goals. Your Ticket becomes "In Use" when you sign the IPE and start receiving services from DORS. If your Ticket to Work is already assigned to another Employment Network, DORS will coordinate services with that provider. After you obtain employment and your DORS case closes, Social Security will send you a letter explaining how to assign your Ticket to another agency for continued support if desired.

structured_extraction.program_description: A reimbursement program that provides financial support to child care providers based on tiered levels of program quality and participation in the Maryland EXCELS quality rating system. Reimbursement payments range from 10% to 44% depending on the age of the child, type of care, and the program's Maryland EXCELS check level rating.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tiered reimbursement payments ranging from 10% to 44% based on Maryland EXCELS check level (3, 4, or 5), age of child (under 2 or 2 and over), type of care (family child care or center), and program ratings. Additional State Family Payment available for programs at levels 3, 4, or 5 accepting Child Care Subsidy. Providers may use tier payments to: offset costs for families receiving Child Care Subsidy, provide salary and benefits enhancements for staff, or make quality improvements to their programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers and centers serving children through school-age care and public pre-kindergarten programs participating in Maryland EXCELS
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for operating child care programs that meet quality standards, with provider discretion to offset family costs, enhance staff salaries and benefits, or make quality improvements
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland child care providers with published Maryland EXCELS ratings at level 3, 4, or 5
requirements_list: Program must have a published Maryland EXCELS rating at level 3, 4, or 5
Program must be accepting Child Care Subsidy
Program must participate in Maryland EXCELS quality rating system
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Providers apply through the Maryland EXCELS quality rating system by meeting established standards for their program type and achieving a published rating at level 3, 4, or 5. Programs are automatically enrolled in tiered reimbursement once they meet quality requirements and accept Child Care Subsidy. Contact the Program Coordinator assigned to the program, a Maryland EXCELS Quality Assurance Specialist, or the Division of Early Childhood Development Help Desk for questions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Title IV, Part B Nita M. Lowey 21st Century Community Learning Centers (CCLC) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program creates community learning centers that provide students with academic enrichment opportunities and services designed to complement their regular school programs. Community learning centers offer literacy instruction and related educational development programs for families of participating students. The program targets students and families who attend schools eligible for Title I schoolwide programs or schools serving high percentages of students from low-income families. Out-of-school time (OST) programs occur before school, after school, during the summer, and on Saturdays to keep students safe, assist working families, and improve academic achievement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded to eligible organizations to establish and operate community learning centers. Grant awards are level funded at 100% of the original award for all three years of programming, contingent on the availability of funding and satisfactory performance. Total funds available: $22.6 million (FY25). Grantees must meet or exceed 85% of the proposed level of students served and demonstrate adequate progress toward achieving all measurable objectives. Grantees are expected to attend bi-monthly networking meetings where the Maryland State Department of Education provides technical assistance, peer-to-peer support, and resources based on grantee needs. Grant funds must be expended in the grant year they were awarded; MSDE does not allow carryover of unobligated funds into the following grant year. Funds support academic enrichment opportunities, educational services, literacy instruction, and related educational development programs for students and their families, including core academic subject instruction, arts and music education, tutoring, mentoring, technology education, drug and violence prevention programs, and counseling services.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, August 29, 2025
structured_extraction.contact_name: Reginald Burke, Executive Director, Office of Federal Programs
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local education agencies, community-based organizations, faith-based organizations, institutions of higher education, for-profit corporations, and consortiums of two or more eligible entities that provide services to students and families attending Title I schools or schools serving high percentages of low-income students.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Academic enrichment opportunities, educational services, literacy instruction, related educational development programs, salaries and fringe benefits for OST staff, professional development and trainings, consultants and evaluators, classroom materials and supplies, remedial and enrichment activities, core academic subject instruction, arts and music education, entrepreneurial education and college/career readiness programs, tutoring and mentoring programs, programs for limited English proficient students, recreational activities, technology and telecommunications education, expanded library services, drug and violence prevention programs, counseling programs, and character education programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services must be provided to students and families primarily attending Title I eligible schools or schools serving a high percentage of students from low-income families. Schools eligible to receive services include: Title I schools serving at least 40% of students from low-income families, high schools with graduation rates less than 67%, and other schools determined by the LEA to need intervention and support. Comparable opportunities must be provided for both public and private school students in the area served by the grant.
requirements_list: Services must target students and families attending Title I eligible schools or schools serving high percentages of low-income students
Organizations must provide both student academic enrichment and family literacy instruction programs
Grantees must attend bi-monthly networking meetings for technical assistance
Grantees must attend required out-of-school (OST) national and regional conferences, MSDE grantee meetings and trainings
Grantees must meet or exceed 85% of the proposed level of students served as indicated in the original application or Grant Renewal Application
Grantees must demonstrate adequate progress toward achieving all measurable objectives
Eligible organizations include non-profit agencies, city or county government agencies, faith-based organizations, institutions of higher education, and for-profit corporations
A consortium of two or more agencies or organizations may apply
Grantees must submit required documentation timely, including monitoring components, corrective actions, monthly reimbursement reports, and detailed local narrative evaluation reports
Grantees must maintain and submit Government Performance and Results Act (GPRA) data to the U.S. Department of Education 21 Annual Performance Report database by established deadlines
Grantees must participate fully in statewide evaluation activities
Grantees must comply with all applicable state statutory and regulatory requirements
Grantees must provide evidence of compliance with federal, state, and local fire, health, zoning codes, and safety standards

Non-LEA subrecipients operating in non-public school facilities must submit all required licenses and certifications for health and safety including Use and Occupancy (U&O) permits and current Fire Inspection reports per operating site

Programs must provide minimum hours: School Year Programs require at least 12 hours per week for 25 weeks OR 4 hours on Saturdays only for 25 weeks, with at least 4 hours of academic programming per week OR 1 hour per Saturday for 25 weeks; Summer Programs require at least 80 hours with at least 32 hours on-site for academic and enrichment programming
Academic enrichment programs must be based on evidence-based research meeting Every Student Succeeds Act (ESSA) evidence criteria
Grant funds must be expended in the grant year awarded; no carryover of unobligated funds is permitted
Final expenditure reports are due 60 days after end of grant period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations submit grant renewal applications electronically through Qualtrics for their respective cohort (Fiscal Year 2024 or 2025). The renewal application requires submission of programmatic and fiscal outcome data for the prior grant award period and a grants management plan for review in consideration for continued funding. Applications must include Performance Goals and Indicators, Evaluation Plan, Management Plan, and Partner Plan as exhibits. MSDE reviews the grant renewal application and year performance data including Start-up reports, Critical Elements Monitoring stages, timely reimbursement invoice submissions, and total number of amendments. Upon review, subgrantees approved for continued funding receive a risk assessment level (1-5) reflected on the Notification of Grant Award (NOGA). Customer Service Support Sessions are available to assist with the application process. Applications are submitted by the stated deadline (August 29, 2025 for FY26). MSDE uses standards in the Uniform Guidance to impose specific or 'high risk' conditions on applicants selected for funding based on history of compliance, performance goal achievement, and other factors.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that approves training providers and processes payments for training services in the early childhood field.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approves training providers and facilitates payment for approved training courses for child care professionals.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Training providers and child care professionals
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and continuing education programs for child care providers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: A program designed to assist child care professionals participating in the Maryland Child Care Credential Program at Level Two or higher with the costs of training and professional development through training vouchers and reimbursement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides two types of assistance: (1) Training Vouchers - issued to participants for approved Core of Knowledge Training, pre-service courses, and registration at local, state, and national child care conferences. Eligible participants can receive up to $400 each year as long as funds are available. The voucher is presented to the organization/trainer for payment. (2) Training Reimbursement - issued to credentialed child care providers for approved training successfully completed not more than 180 days (6 months) before application submission. Reimbursement can only be issued to the individual provider, not to centers or organizations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care professionals participating in the Maryland Child Care Credential Program at Level Two or higher.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Approved Core of Knowledge Training, pre-service courses (including child growth and development, infant-toddler care, preschool curriculum, school-age curriculum, director administration, family child care training, communication courses, and college courses), and registration at local, state, and national child care conferences.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide.
requirements_list: Must be participating in the Maryland Child Care Credential Program at Level Two or higher
For training vouchers: must be able to upload required documents with each application on Maryland OneStop
For training reimbursement: training must have been completed not more than 180 days (6 months) before application submission
Upon successful completion of training, must provide transcripts, grade slip, certificate, or documentation from instructor indicating successful completion
For national conference attendance: must obtain CEUs or submit conference certificate and booklet with workshop titles and trainer signatures
If training is not completed without good cause, voucher amount must be repaid and no additional vouchers will be issued
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted online through Maryland OneStop. Participants must complete the Application for Training Voucher and Reimbursement and upload required documents with each application. Incomplete applications will not be processed. Online application instructions are available at earlychildhood.marylandpublicschools.org. For approved training opportunities, visit www.marylandfamilynetwork.org under Training>For Child Care Providers>Search. After training completion, submit proof of completion (transcripts, grade slip, certificate, or instructor documentation). For training vouchers, the organization/trainer submits the voucher to the Credentialing Branch for payment. For reimbursement, payment is issued directly to the credentialed child care provider.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides vouchers and reimbursements for child care providers to cover training and professional development costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides vouchers and reimbursements to help child care providers cover the costs of professional training and education.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and professional development costs

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides eligible child care providers up to $400 each year to cover the cost of approved training, conferences, and college coursework to support professional development and credential advancement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Providers receive up to $400 each year. Training vouchers cover the cost of pre-service training, conferences, and approved college coursework and are submitted before training occurs. Training reimbursements cover the cost of approved Core of Knowledge training (minimum 2 clock hours), pre-service training, conferences, and approved college coursework and are submitted within 180 days after training completion. The training organization or provider submits documentation to receive payment from the program. Applicants will receive notification of approval or denial via email within 30 days of application submission. If approved, applicants download their training voucher from the Maryland OneStop portal, sign it, and forward it to the trainer/training organization. After training completion, applicants upload their certificate of successful completion to the Maryland OneStop portal for the Office of Child Care-Workforce Advancement Branch.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted beginning December 29, 2025. Training vouchers must be applied for at least 60 days before the conference or training. Training reimbursements must be applied for within 180 days of training completion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-licensed child care providers who hold a Maryland Child Care Credential at Level 2 or higher, or who held such a credential that expired between July 1, 2024 and August 30, 2025.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Approved Core of Knowledge training, pre-service training, registration at statewide and national child care conferences, and approved college coursework in child development, early childhood materials and methods, special education, administration and management of child care programs, infants and toddlers, school-age children, health and safety and nutrition, and language and literacy. Not eligible for training that has not been approved by MSDE, training fees paid to others, association membership fees, or CDA credential or renewal fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must hold a Maryland Child Care Credential at Level 2 or higher
Alternative: credential expired between July 1, 2024 and August 30, 2025
Training must be approved by MSDE according to COMAR 13A.14.09
For training vouchers: application must be submitted at least 60 days before training or conference
For training reimbursements: application must be submitted within 180 days of training completion
Training must have taken place less than 181 days before application date for reimbursement
Pre-service training must be a minimum of 2 clock hours for reimbursement
Must provide documentation of training completion (certificate, transcript, or grade slip)
For national conferences: must provide conference certificate and booklet with workshop titles and trainer signatures
Activities must demonstrate professional growth and be related to the child care field
Activities must give back to the child care community and/or improve quality of child care programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the application form online through the Maryland OneStop platform. For training vouchers, submit at least 60 days before the training or conference with required documentation. For training reimbursements, submit within 180 days of training completion with proof of payment and certificate of successful completion. Applicants will receive notification of approval or denial via email within 30 days of application submission. If approved, applicants log into Maryland OneStop, go to their dashboard, click into the application submission, scroll to the bottom, locate the section titled 'MSDE Approved Training Voucher', and download the PDF voucher. Applicants then sign and forward the voucher to the trainer/training organization to complete training registration. After training completion, applicants return to their Maryland OneStop portal, go to their dashboard, select the application, scroll to the 'Verification of Training Completion' section at the bottom, click 'Choose File' to upload the certificate of completion, and press 'Submit'. The certificate is submitted to the Office of Child Care-Workforce Advancement Branch. For activities not listed on the PAU matrix, applicants must complete the Professional Activity Unit (PAU) Approval Form with all required information and documentation, which will be reviewed and assigned PAUs (1 to 3) within 60 days of receipt with notification sent via email.

structured_extraction.program_description: VCAMP is a virtual mentoring and support service for consumers on the autism spectrum attending college. This remote mentoring program helps students on the autism spectrum transition into and navigate college while developing self-advocacy and social skills.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Virtual mentoring and support services for college students on the autism spectrum. VCAMP is completely online and available to students attending either a two-year or four-year college in Maryland or out of state. The program provides weekly online individual sessions with DORS Autism Services staff and weekly VCAMP online group sessions. Students learn about college transition, supports available on campus (such as Disability Support Services and academic tutoring), time management and organizational skills, self-advocacy and social skills, appropriate grooming and hygiene skills, and other skills needed to successfully navigate the college environment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: College students on the autism spectrum not participating in the Pathways program
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Virtual mentoring and support for college success
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to individuals attending in-state or out-of-state two- or four-year colleges
requirements_list: Be a DORS participant on the Autism spectrum
Have an approved Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) that includes college
Work towards an industry-recognized college degree or certification from a two-year or four-year college where the in-person DORS Pathways program is not available
Meet with DORS Autism Services staff for weekly online sessions
Attend weekly VCAMP online group sessions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your DORS Counselor or local office for more information or request DORS Services via the provided QR code

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that reimburses businesses for employee wages while they train qualified job seekers hired through the Department of Rehabilitation Services. Employers can access short-term training (up to one month) with up to 100% salary reimbursement, or long-term training (up to four months) with gradually decreasing reimbursement as the employee becomes more skilled.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employers receive wage reimbursement for training qualified DORS job seekers. Short-term on-the-job training (one month duration) provides up to 100% salary reimbursement. Long-term on-the-job training (up to four months duration) offers gradually decreasing reimbursement as the employee becomes more skilled and independent. Payment is processed through DORS within approximately 30 days of invoice receipt.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland businesses interested in hiring and training qualified job seekers through DORS
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wage reimbursement for employee salaries during the training period
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Regional DORS offices serve: Region 1 (Garrett, Allegany, Washington, Frederick, Carroll); Region 2 (Anne Arundel, Calvert, Caroline, Charles, Cecil, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester); Region 3 (Baltimore City); Region 5 (Baltimore, Harford, Howard); Region 6 (Prince George's, Montgomery); Office for Blindness & Vision Services (statewide).
requirements_list: Complete DORS Provider/Vendor Application form
Attach Federal IRS Employer Identification Number (EIN) or Social Security Number
Provide relevant business licenses, certifications, and insurance certificates if required
Hire a qualified DORS job seeker
Employee must be referred by DORS
Provide written authorization from DORS before services are rendered
Submit invoices with required information including bill-to address, remit-to address, Federal Tax ID, invoice date, and description of services
Register for electronic payment (recommended)
Comply with COMAR 13A.11.01.17(A)(4) and 13A.11.01.16(B)(4) regarding payment from consumers
Disclose any outstanding tax or other liabilities to State or federal government
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the DORS Provider/Vendor Application form and submit with all required supporting documentation to the Director, DORS Business Support Services, 2301 Argonne Drive, Baltimore, MD 21218-1696. Include Internal Revenue Service Form W-9 and copies of any required licenses, certifications, and insurance certificates. DORS will contact the applicant within 30 days of receiving the completed application and all required information. Upon approval, become an approved provider/vendor. Obtain written authorization from your local DORS Business Services Representative before providing any services. Submit invoices with required information for payment, which is processed within approximately 30 days. Vendors are encouraged to register for electronic payment at www.marylandtaxes.gov/divisions/gad/eft-program.php for faster payment processing.

structured_extraction.program_description: A two-part training program for individuals with little or no work experience or who have been out of the workforce for an extended period. The program develops skills needed to succeed in the workplace through community-based activities and classroom sessions at DORS WTC campus in Baltimore.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program consists of two six-week courses that can be taken together or separately. Work Readiness 1 includes career exploration, soft skills development, financial management, organizational skills, self-determination and self-awareness, interpersonal skills and teamwork, workplace preparation and communication, and job retention through videos, lectures, guest speakers, worksite tours, and job shadowing. Work Readiness 2 focuses on customer service, workplace ethics, conflict management, resume writing, job descriptions, mock interviews, and managing your online footprint, with real-world work experience through volunteer work at community worksites. Both courses are six weeks long and include classroom instruction and community-based activities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with disabilities who have little or no work experience or have been out of the workforce for an extended period.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Classroom instruction, community-based activities, worksite training, volunteer work experiences, and job shadowing to develop employment readiness skills.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available through the DORS WTC campus in Baltimore, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be able to function in a classroom setting (Work Readiness 1)
Must be able to fully participate in all individual and group activities (Work Readiness 1)
Must have capability and desire to participate in competitive employment (Work Readiness 2)
Must be able to spend half of each day volunteering at a community worksite with drop-in support only (Work Readiness 2)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals can contact their DORS Counselor or local office for more information or request DORS services. Individuals can enroll in Work Readiness 1 and 2 together or as stand-alone programs through the Workforce Training Center.

structured_extraction.program_description: Program designed to support the development and advancement of child care professionals and improve the quality of child care providers and facilities across Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Support and assistance to help child care providers and facilities improve quality and advance their careers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers and facilities in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional development, training, and quality improvement for child care providers and facilities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Workforce Advancement Branch for information on available support and assistance programs.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides services to individuals with disabilities who want to live more independently at home and in their community. It is for people whose main goal is not employment. It includes the Independent Living Older Blind Program (ILOB), which teaches people age 55 and older with vision loss how to become independent in their homes and communities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education, Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers independent living services to help individuals with disabilities be more independent at home and in the community. It includes the Independent Living Older Blind Program (ILOB), which provides independent living skills training to help individuals age 55 or older with vision loss maintain independence in their homes and communities. ILOB services include: training in managing personal care and household tasks; labeling and organizing personal care items, clothing, appliances and medications; safe cooking techniques; orientation and mobility training; Braille instruction; use of assistive technology; referral to community peer support groups and other services; and introduction to community resources such as NFB-NEWSLINE and resources at the Maryland State Library for the Blind and Print Disabled. ILOB rehabilitation specialists provide assessment and training in the client's home.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities who want to live more independently. The ILOB component specifically serves individuals age 55 and older with vision loss.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Independent living skills training, including safe cooking techniques, managing personal care and household tasks, orientation and mobility training, Braille instruction, use of assistive technology, and connection to community resources and peer support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through DORS offices throughout Maryland, including rural counties. Regional OBVS offices serve: Baltimore (Baltimore City, Baltimore, Cecil, Howard, Harford Counties at 410-261-2954); Wheaton (Allegany, Carroll, Frederick, Garrett, Montgomery, Washington Counties at 301-949-3750); Annapolis (Anne Arundel, Calvert, Caroline, Charles, Dorchester, Kent, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester Counties at 410-974-7604).
requirements_list: Must be an individual with a disability.
The primary goal should be independent living, not employment.
For the Independent Living Older Blind Program (ILOB), applicant must be age 55 or older and have vision loss as the primary disability.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To learn more about independent living services, contact the Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council (MSILC). For ILOB services, complete the Request DORS Services form or contact your local DORS office or one of the regional OBVS offices. You will be contacted to set up an intake meeting where eligibility will be determined. Rehabilitation specialists will work with you to provide personalized assessment and training in your home.

structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides nutritionally balanced, low-cost, or free lunches to children each school day. School meals include expanded access to fresh fruits, vegetables, whole-grain menu items, with reduced sodium and saturated fat content. The program helps schools and residential child care facilities provide lunches to students, covering the cost of making the meals.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education, Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reimburses schools with federal dollars for meals that comply with USDA nutrition standards. Students receive lunches at no charge or at reduced price depending on eligibility. Children from families with incomes at or below 130 percent of the federal poverty level receive free meals. Children from families with incomes between 130 and 185 percent of the federal poverty level receive reduced-price meals. All children determined as eligible in the reduced-price category receive free meals due to state funding under the Maryland Cares for Kids Act. Income eligibility guidelines are updated annually (effective July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2024: free meals for household of 1 at $18,954 annual income; reduced-price meals at $26,973 annual income, with adjustments for larger household sizes).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children in Maryland public schools and participating private schools and residential childcare institutions. Eligibility includes children from families with incomes at or below 130 percent of the federal poverty level for free meals, or between 130 and 185 percent for reduced-price meals. Children in Head Start or Even Start programs, categorically eligible children, homeless or foster children, and children receiving Medicaid also qualify.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: School meal provision meeting USDA nutrition standards. Meals must comply with Maryland Nutrition Standards for all foods sold in school, including specific requirements for calories, sodium, fat, and sugar content. Funds help cover the cost of producing meals for students.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All 24 Maryland public school systems and 22 non-profit private schools and residential childcare institutions participate in the program.
requirements_list: School must comply with USDA nutrition standards and Maryland Nutrition Standards for all foods sold in school
School must participate in the National School Lunch Program

Food must be whole grain-rich (at least 50% whole grain by weight or whole grain as first ingredient) OR have fruit, vegetable, dairy product, or protein food as first ingredient OR be a combination containing at least 1/4 cup fruit and/or vegetables
Snack/side dishes must not exceed 200 calories and 200mg sodium
Entrees must not exceed 350 calories and 480mg sodium
Total fat must not exceed 35% of calories; saturated fat must be less than 10% of calories
Sugar must comprise 35% or less of total weight of serving

Beverages must comply with specific standards: plain water unlimited; low-fat/non-fat milk limited to 8 fl oz (elementary) or 12 fl oz (middle/high school); 100% fruit/vegetable juice limited to 8 fl oz (elementary) or 12 fl oz (middle/high school); soda and caffeine not allowed

Policy applies to all foods and beverages sold on school campus from 12:01 am through 30 minutes after end of school day, including cafeteria a la carte items, vending machines, school stores, and fundraising activities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Children qualify for free or reduced-price meals through: attending a Community Eligibility Provision school, attending a school participating in Maryland Meals for Achievement, enrollment in Head Start or Even Start, categorical eligibility through participation in federal assistance programs, direct certification through Medicaid participation, or income eligibility based on household income and family size as outlined in the annual Income Eligibility Guidelines. Schools evaluate household income by comparing reported income to the published Income Eligibility Guidelines for the appropriate frequency and household size. When household reports income sources at more than one frequency, annualize all income and compare to annual guidelines.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program administered by the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland that provides gap financing to small businesses seeking to locate or expand in Allegany, Garrett, and Washington counties. The program creates a revolving pool of money where businesses repay loans and funds are redeployed to make additional loans, supporting job creation and business expansion in the Appalachian region. The program has been in operation since 1980.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides gap financing loans from $10,000 to $400,000. A bank or other private lender must fund at least 50% of the project. Interest rates are tied to the prime interest rate. Loan terms are up to 5 years for working capital and up to 15 years for fixed assets like real estate. Borrowers repay loans and the money is returned to the revolving loan fund to make additional loans, creating an ongoing financial tool.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, including corporations, partnerships, and sole proprietorships, seeking to locate or expand in Allegany, Garrett, or Washington County in western Maryland's Appalachian region. Intended for businesses that cannot get all their needed funding from traditional lenders.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business acquisition and expansion, land and building costs, buying machinery and equipment, start-up costs, and working capital.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in Allegany, Garrett, or Washington County to be eligible.
requirements_list: Business must be small and seeking to locate or expand.
Project must create or save jobs.
A business plan is required.
A private lender must fund at least 50% of the total project cost.
Applicant must provide a denial letter from the primary lender for 100% of the project, along with their approval to finance a majority of the project.
One job must be created or retained for every $30,000 borrowed within the first 36 months of the loan.
A minimum equity injection of 10% is generally required for start-up businesses.
Personal guaranties of the debt are required from all owners with 20% or greater interest.
Applicants must provide a completed personal financial statement and 3 years of both business and personal tax returns.
A $250 non-refundable application fee is required.
Approved borrowers are assessed a 1.5% loan origination fee at closing.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses work with Summit Financing Solutions and participate with banks and other lenders to obtain gap financing. First, create a business plan and determine your funding needs. Second, apply for a loan from a private bank to determine how much they will finance. Third, complete the program's application form and submit it with the required documents and application fee.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program that encourages landowners to agree not to develop their land for ten years. In exchange, landowners receive protection from nuisance complaints, eligibility to sell development rights through MALPF, and a property tax credit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners receive a property tax credit for enrolling their agricultural land in a ten-year preservation district agreement, including county property tax credits for farmland, farm buildings, and a partial tax credit for the home. The program also provides protection from nuisance complaints through the Right to Farm Ordinance (official county acknowledgement that farming is the preferred use of the land), and makes landowners eligible to sell Development Rights Easements to the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF). The district agreement runs with the land for at least ten years and remains in effect even if the property is sold or transferred during that period.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Washington County Planning Department - Agricultural Land Preservation
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners in Washington County who want to preserve their land from development for ten years.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land preservation through development restrictions for ten years. The program does not provide direct funds but rather offers tax credits and legal protections for preserving agricultural land.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, outside water and sewer service areas, and outside growth areas.
requirements_list: Land must be agricultural property
Minimum 50 acres stand-alone or 20 acres if contiguous to other districts
Minimum 50% of soil classes I, II, and III
Land must be outside water and sewer service areas
Land must be outside of growth areas
Landowner must voluntarily enter into the district agreement
Land must not be developed or subdivided for industrial, commercial, or residential use except for certain personal eligibility options
Land must be kept in agricultural use for a minimum period of ten years
Landowner agrees not to divide the land without county written approval
Landowner agrees not to construct non-agricultural buildings or structures without county approval
Soil erosion and water quality practices contained within an approved soil conservation plan must be implemented
No trash or rubbish may be dumped on the property except materials for regular agricultural use
No signs or billboards except for signs smaller than four feet square for property name, home-based occupation, or sale/rental
Agreement must be notarized and recorded in county land records
All titled landowners must sign the agreement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested landowners must complete the Agricultural District Intake Form and the Agricultural Preservation District Agreement documents. These completed forms must be submitted to the Washington County Department of Planning & Zoning. The agreement must be notarized and recorded in the land records of Washington County. Once all current titled landowners have signed the agreement, it is recorded in the County Land Records and the district is established. The agreement becomes effective upon recordation. After ten years, the agreement may be terminated by submitting a written request and having all current titled landowners sign and return a Release and Termination document, which must then be recorded in the County Land Records.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded program that provides grants to eligible entities for projects related to economic opportunities, workforce development, critical infrastructure, natural and cultural assets, and leadership and community capacity building in Appalachia.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are provided for projects in five strategic areas: Economic Opportunities (entrepreneurial and business development), Ready Workforce (education, skills, and health improvements), Critical Infrastructure (broadband, transportation, water and wastewater systems), Natural and Cultural Assets (community and economic development leveraging heritage), and Leadership and Community Capacity (building skills of leaders and organizations). Priority projects include Technology Development, Broadband, Education and Workforce Development, Tourism, Energy, Recovery Ecosystems, and Traditional Infrastructure. Grants require a 50 percent match, with matching funds identified and committed at the time of application. Projects must demonstrate measurable outcomes and/or economic impact using ARC's acceptable performance measures.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY27 Project Submission (Preliminary Project Description) is April 3, 2026; formal application due November 15, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible entities in Washington County seeking to fund projects that advance economic development, workforce readiness, infrastructure improvements, cultural asset preservation, or community leadership capacity in Appalachia.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects related to economic opportunities, workforce development, critical infrastructure (including broadband, transportation, and water/wastewater systems), natural and cultural assets, and leadership and community capacity building. Projects must be consistent with ARC 2024 Strategy Statement priorities and one of five ARC Investment Goals: Building Appalachian Businesses, Building Appalachia's Workforce Ecosystem, Building Appalachia's Infrastructure, Building Regional Culture and Tourism, or Building Community Leaders and Capacity.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland. Projects must be in Appalachia and demonstrate measurable outcomes and/or economic impact.
requirements_list: 50 percent match funding must be identified and committed at time of application
Projects must demonstrate measurable outcomes and/or economic impact using ARC's acceptable performance measures
Submit Preliminary Project Description form
Submit ARC Project Budget and Funding Sources form

Projects must fall within one of five ARC Investment Goals: Building Appalachian Businesses, Building Appalachia's Workforce Ecosystem, Building Appalachia's Infrastructure, Building Regional Culture and Tourism, or Building Community Leaders and Capacity

Priority given to projects consistent with ARC 2024 Strategy Statement including Technology Development, Broadband, Education and Workforce Development, Tourism, Energy, Recovery Ecosystems, and Traditional Infrastructure
Project must align with State Strategic Goals and Objectives 2024-2028
All outputs and outcomes must be quantifiable with associated numeric values
Project should reference plans and/or economic documents showing it is part of an overall plan for stimulating economic development
Applicant must describe organizational capacity to administer a federal grant, including recent awards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Preliminary Project Description and ARC Project Budget and Funding Sources forms to the Office of Grant Management by April 3, 2026. Forms must include project description, goals and objectives aligned with ARC Investment Goals and State objectives/strategies, performance measures with quantifiable outputs and outcomes, organizational capacity information, and all matching fund sources with commitment letters. Projects are reviewed and ranked by Washington County Commissioners. County-ranked projects are submitted to Tri-County Council for Western Maryland for regional ranking. Top-ranking projects receive an invitation letter in early Fall to submit a formal grant application to the Appalachian Regional Commission, with the formal application due November 15, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: A charitable gaming program that allows qualified organizations to conduct bingo games in Washington County. Organizations must obtain a permit from county commissioners and comply with regulations regarding permitted uses of proceeds, prize limitations, and operational requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program allows nonprofit organizations to conduct bingo games as a fundraising activity. County commissioners review applications to verify the charitable purpose and intended use of proceeds. Nonprofit organizations are exempt from annual permit fees. For-profit operations are prohibited. Prize limits are set at a maximum of $1,000 per game for money prizes, merchandise prizes, or a combination thereof.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations seeking to conduct bingo games as a charitable fundraising activity in Washington County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The bingo proceeds must be used for charitable purposes as specified in the permit application. For-profit use of proceeds is prohibited.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: Organization must be a nonprofit
Bingo must be conducted for a charitable purpose, not for profit
A permit must be obtained from the county commissioners before conducting bingo
County commissioners must review and approve the charitable purpose and intended use of receipts
Prize limits must not exceed $1,000 per game for money, merchandise, or combined prizes
Full application required if applicant is new, organization officers have changed, or more than two years have elapsed since last full application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit either the full Bingo Application or Temporary Bingo Application Short Form to the Washington County Grant Management office. structured_extraction.program_description: Washington County provides financial support to charitable organizations within Washington County that provide services which improve the community and quality of life for Washington County citizens. The program implements a prioritized approach to funding local non-profits based on specific community needs, with emphasis on efficient use of funds and achieving results-based programmatic outcomes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants are awarded to eligible non-profit organizations. For Fiscal Year 2027, the Board of County Commissioners has allocated $1,200,000 in available funding distributed across priority service areas: Families and Children ($494,400), Domestic Violence ($386,400), Arts & Cultural ($135,600), Seniors ($136,800), Recreation ($33,600), and Other ($13,200). Grant awards are disbursed in four quarterly installments (25% each quarter) starting July 2026. All funds must be expended between July 1, 2026, and June 30, 2027. Administrative costs may not exceed 15% of the total amount requested. Eligible expenses include operating and capital expenses/projects that can be completed within the one-year funding period.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Tuesday, January 6, 2026, by 3:00pm
structured_extraction.contact_name: Carsten Ahrens, Senior Grant Manager; Maria Kramer, Director
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charitable organizations providing services that improve the community and quality of life for Washington County citizens, including services in priority areas: Families/Children, Domestic Violence, Cultural, Seniors, Recreation, and Other community services
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To support charitable organizations providing services that improve the community and quality of life for Washington County citizens. Funds may be used for operating expenses, capital expenses, and projects. Funds cannot be used to benefit an individual or to fund an endowment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County. Organization must have an office located within Washington County and provide services within Washington County.
requirements_list: Organization must be included on the Board of County Commissioners 'Recognized Non-Profit List' (Section 1-108 of the Code of Public Local Laws)
Organization must be a charitable non-profit recognized by the Internal Revenue Service as a 501(c)(3) with 'Valid' status

Organization must be incorporated as a business entity with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) and be 'In Good Standing' at the time of application submission with proof provided
Organization must have an office in and provide services within Washington County
Organization must have a recent audit (preferably) or detailed financial statement
Application must be submitted during the published application window by the established deadline
Organization must not have unpaid liens, judgments, or past due obligations to the Washington County Treasurer or any other government entity
Organization must not have submitted applications for the same program under more than one service priority area (multiple applications for different programs are permitted)
Administrative costs may not exceed 15% of the total amount requested
Submission must be signed by an authorized representative of the organization
Organization must be in good standing with the State of Maryland at time of submission
Grant proposal must impact at least one of the prioritized service areas
Letters of support are highly encouraged
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations on the Recognized Non-Profit List receive a Notice of Funding Availability with application procedures and deadlines. The Office of Grant Management makes available online application guidelines, requirements, and forms on or about December 1, 2025. Applicants must complete the Community Organization Funding application packet including: Overview, Statement of Need, Past Performance, Organizational Capacity and Staffing Plan, Program Plan, Collaborations/Partnerships, letters of support, budget spreadsheet, IRS 501(c)(3) determination letter, SDAT proof of good standing, recent audit or financial statement, most recent IRS Form 990, and W-9/Vendor Remittance Form (if applicable). Application packets must contain six hard paper copies (unsecured with staples, binder clips, or rubber bands, no bound covers or tab dividers) and one electronic PDF copy. Hard copies should be placed in a manila envelope and mailed or dropped off at the Office of Grant Management, 100 West Washington Street, Room 1601, Hagerstown, MD 21740. Electronic copy must be emailed to cahrens@washco-md.net and cc jmackereth@washco-md.net with the PDF titled with organization name. All applications and attachments must be submitted by the deadline; applications received after the deadline will not be accepted. The COF Committee, consisting of OGM representatives and five members appointed by the BOCC, reviews and ranks applications using a scoring rubric with criteria: Application Submission (10 points), Statement of Need (20 points), Past Performance (5 points), Organizational Capacity and Staffing (10 points), Program Plan (30 points), Collaborations/Partnerships (10 points), and Budget/Narrative (15 points) for a maximum of 100 points. Additional factors considered include total funding allocated, amount per priority area, geographic distribution, and previous program performance. Applicants will be notified in writing when the budgetary process is complete. Technical assistance workshops are offered on December 2nd at 9:00-10:30am or 3:00-4:30pm via Zoom with limited in-person option.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants distributed from cannabis sales tax revenue and cannabis business conversion fees to support community-based initiatives. Funds must supplement, not replace, existing local government funding for programs and services.

Easement restrictions remain effective in perpetuity.

Once the easement is sold, it remains effective in perpetuity
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners with an existing FSA CREP Contract can apply for the easement program through the County's Land Preservation Office. Once the easement is sold, it remains permanently effective.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides qualifying businesses with State income tax credits and local real property tax credits in return for job creation and capital investments made in the designated Enterprise Zones.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State Income Tax Credits: Qualifying businesses receive tax credits based on new jobs created. For most new jobs, the credit is a one-time maximum of $1,000. For economically disadvantaged employees certified by Maryland Department of Labor, credits are $3,000 the first year, $2,000 the second year, and $1,000 the third year. Employees must work at least 35 hours per week, earn at least 150% of federal minimum wage, spend at least 50% of working time in the Zone, and be employed for at least 6 consecutive months. Local Real Property Tax Credits: Property owners receive 10 years of credits on real property with capital investments. Credits are 80% of property taxes on increased assessment for years 1-5, declining to 30% in year 10. Commercial Building Excise Tax Exemption: New construction in Enterprise Zones is exempt from commercial building excise taxes.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No specific deadline
structured_extraction.program_audience: New and existing for-profit businesses making job creation and capital investments in designated Enterprise Zones, including manufacturing, warehousing, research and development, corporate offices, service industries, and retail businesses (with restrictions).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: State income tax credits for job creation and local real property tax credits for capital improvements such as new construction, building additions, and renovations in designated Enterprise Zones.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Three designated Enterprise Zones in Washington County: (1) City of Hagerstown/Washington County Enterprise Zone (approximately 4,000 acres, including Hopewell Valley Industrial Park, Washington County Business Park, CSX Valley Park, City of Hagerstown Business Park, and Central Business District); (2) Town of Hancock Enterprise Zone (1,500 acres surrounding the Town of Hancock from Pennsylvania border to Potomac River). Designation dates: Hagerstown-Washington County Zone - December 15, 1982; Hancock Zone - December 15, 1995.
requirements_list: Business must be located in a designated Enterprise Zone

For State Income Tax Credits (Job Creation): Minimum of 1 new job in Central Business District or 1 new job in Hancock Zone; minimum of 5 new jobs outside Central Business District in Hagerstown-Washington County Zone

For Real Property Tax Credits: Minimum of $5,000 capital investment in Central Business District or Hancock Zone; minimum of $50,000 capital investment outside Central Business District in Hagerstown-Washington County Zone
New jobs must be created after the Enterprise Zone designation date (Hagerstown-Washington County: Dec 15, 1982; Hancock: Dec 15, 1995)
Employees must work at least 35 hours per week
Employees must earn at least 150% of federal minimum wage
Employees must spend at least 50% of working time in the Enterprise Zone or in activities directly related to the Zone business
Employees must be employed for at least 6 consecutive months to qualify for tax credit
For disadvantaged employees, must be certified by Maryland Department of Labor
Retail businesses eligible only if located in Hancock Enterprise Zone or Central Business District of Hagerstown-Washington County Zone
For property tax credits, business must be proprietorship, partnership, or corporation
Property must be certified to Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation during the calendar year construction is completed
Property tax credit application must be submitted prior to project completion and issuance of User/Occupancy Permits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Determine the property is in an Enterprise Zone by contacting Washington County Department of Business Development. 2. Verify business meets minimum eligibility criteria for jobs or capital investment. 3. For Property Tax Credits: Submit Request for Enterprise Zone Qualification form to DBD before project completion and issuance of User/Occupancy Permits. 4. For Income Tax Credits: After hiring new employees, submit Qualification form and 'New Jobs Created' form listing employees to DBD. 5. For disadvantaged employee credits, contact Maryland Job Service Office at 301-393-8200 or visit 14 North Potomac Street, Hagerstown for employee screening and certification. 6. DBD sends approval letter to applicant and copies to appropriate local and state agencies. 7. For property tax credits, credits automatically appear on Washington County and Town of Hancock tax bills in July; City of Hagerstown issues credit voucher. 8. For income tax credits, claim on Maryland Tax Form 500CR with approval letter from DBD when filing annual tax return.

structured_extraction.program_description: Tax credits available for property owners who undertake approved historic preservation work on their properties located in Washington County historic districts. The program offers stackable credits up to 70% of qualified rehabilitation expenses through county (25%), state (20%), federal (20%), and additional exterior work (5%) credits.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Washington County Historic Properties Tax Credit provides a reduction in county property taxes for qualified rehabilitation expenses on eligible historic structures. The program offers a 25% county tax credit for rehabilitation, restoration, or preservation work that minimizes destruction of historic fabric with thoughtful and sympathetic design. An additional 5% tax credit is available for exterior work on new construction attached to existing historic structures. Qualifying Rehabilitation Expenses (QREs) include roof repair/replacement, chimney repair/replacement, window restoration, storm doors/windows, masonry re-pointing, structural repairs, architectural/engineering/consulting fees, and tool/equipment rental. Unused credits can be carried over for up to 5 years or until expended. The program is stackable with state (20%), federal (20%), and additional exterior credits (5%), providing up to 70% possible total credits. Application for the county credit must be submitted before work starts.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application must be submitted before work begins; no specific annual deadline
structured_extraction.contact_name: Washington County Department of Planning and Zoning; Historic District Commission
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential and commercial property owners with historic properties in Washington County historic districts seeking to undertake preservation, restoration, or renovation work
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified Rehabilitation Expenses (QREs) for historic preservation and rehabilitation work including roof repair/replacement, chimney repair/replacement, window restoration, storm doors/windows, masonry re-pointing, structural repairs, architectural/engineering/consulting fees, and tool/equipment rental on eligible historic structures
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, specifically properties: (1) within the Antietam Overlay (AO1 or AO2) district; (2) that are contributing structures to surveyed and adopted Historic Rural Villages (Antietam, Cavetown, Fairplay, Highfield, Leitersburg, Pen Mar, Ringgold, Rohrersville, Sandy Hook, or Tilghmanton); (3) with the Historic Preservation (HP) Overlay applied through a rezoning process; or (4) that are contributing structures within towns listed on the National Register of Historic Places with appropriate zoning and design guidelines. Properties must be documented on the Maryland Inventory of Historic Properties.
requirements_list: Property must be located in a designated historic district, Antietam Overlay zone, Historic Rural Village, or eligible municipality with appropriate zoning
Property must be documented on the Maryland Inventory of Historic Properties
Work must be approved by the Historic District Commission before rehabilitation begins
Applicant must follow the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation and the Washington County Design Guidelines for Historic Structures
Work must minimize destruction of historic fabric with thoughtful and sympathetic design
For structures under Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) Easement, a copy of the easement document must be included with the application
Property owners with MHT Easements must comply with easement holder review requirements
Applicant is responsible for compliance with all Federal, State, and local laws including zoning, building, safety codes, licensing, permitting, and environmental requirements
Application must be submitted and approved before work begins; work started prior to approval may not be eligible for tax credit
Itemized documentation of all expenses with invoices/receipts and proof of payment is required for Part 3 certification
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process consists of three parts: Part I (Evaluation of Significance) - submitted during project planning phase to determine if the structure qualifies; owners of properties with Historic Preservation (HP) Overlay do not need to complete Part I unless there is a question about overlay inclusion. Part II (Description of Rehabilitation) - submitted before work begins for review by staff and Historic District Commission to ensure conformance with Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation and County Design Guidelines; must be approved before any work starts. Part III (Certification of Completed Work) - submitted after project completion with itemized expenses, invoices, receipts, proof of payment, and project photos for HDC review of eligible expenses and determination that work was completed as approved. Completed projects may be inspected by HDC representatives. Applications and supporting documents should be mailed to: Washington County Historic District Commission, c/o Washington County Department of Planning & Zoning, 747 Northern Avenue, Hagerstown, MD 21742, or emailed to askplanning@washco-md.net. All application parts require signatures done using Digital ID, printed and wet signed, or digitized original handwritten signatures. If applicant is not the fee-simple owner, an Owner's Representative Affidavit must be included. Upon HDC approval, the credit amount is forwarded to the Treasurer's Office for property bill updates.

Projects must generate overnight stays in the County

Projects must reach a broad segment of the community
Projects must seek multiple sources of support rather than rely solely on Hotel Rental Tax Funding
