structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Requests can be made throughout the fiscal year and are contingent on available funding. Applications can be accessed from the County's website under the Office of Grant Management, submitted by email, or printed and mailed in. All applications are received by the Office of Grant Management (OGM). The OGM will: (1) determine if the applicant is qualified to receive funding; (2) determine if the event or project is qualified to receive funding; (3) determine if the request meets the funding goals of the County Commissioners and the purpose of the Hotel Rental Tax Funding; (4) for requests of $25,000 and below, approve or deny the request with the concurrence of the County Administrator; (5) for requests of more than $25,000, process the application and forward it to the County Administrator for review, and upon favorable review the County Commissioners will hear the request; and (6) notify the applicant in writing of approval or denial. All organizations receiving grant funding must complete a Hotel Rental Tax Grant Report with supporting documentation (budget itemizations and/or receipts) within 60 days of project completion.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program created to accelerate land preservation easement purchases and provide an attractive option for agricultural landowners. Owners of qualifying agricultural land can sell an Agricultural Preservation Easement to the County and receive payment through an Installment Purchase Agreement over ten years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County purchases Development Rights Easements on agricultural land and pays the landowner through an Installment Purchase Agreement. To date, over 1,500 acres (1,507 acres) have been preserved with more than $6.1 million ($6,110,000) in funding. Payments are made over a period of ten years: ten percent of the principal is paid at settlement along with interest, and ten percent of the principal is paid annually for the remaining nine years. The Agreement includes a fixed interest rate. The easement applies to the entire contiguous acreage of the land less one acre per existing dwelling on the property.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners in Washington County who meet the minimum qualifications and want to sell their Development Rights Easements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are used to purchase Development Rights Easements on the entire contiguous acreage of agricultural land (less one acre per existing dwelling on the property).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County
requirements_list: Property must be agricultural land meeting minimum qualifications
Owner must own the entire contiguous acreage
Easement applies to entire contiguous acreage of the land less one acre per existing dwelling on the property
Program is very competitive and dependent on current economic climate
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: An owner of qualifying agricultural land makes application to sell an Agricultural Preservation Easement to the County. Once the landowner agrees to the County's offer, an Installment Purchase Agreement is written that includes the total amount of money, terms, and fixed interest rate.

structured_extraction.program_name: LMB ENOUGH Capacity Building Fiscal Year 2026
structured_extraction.program_description: Grant funding to support innovative programs that improve healthcare access and transportation services for seniors, individuals with disabilities, and low-income households with children who face mobility barriers in underserved communities of Washington County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $10,000.00 to $40,000.00 per award. The total funding pool is $74,000.00 with plans to award 1 to 3 grants. The performance period runs from May 15, 2026, through September 30, 2026. Funds can support non-emergency medical transportation services, expansion of existing volunteer driver programs or specialized transit services, and last-mile solutions to connect residents in underserved areas to healthcare and transportation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, March 6, 2026, at 3:00pm
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations and local government agencies providing services to Washington County residents
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for non-emergency medical transportation services (direct transport to primary care, dialysis, mental health services, or pharmacy pickups), expansion of existing volunteer driver programs or specialized transit services, and last-mile solutions to connect residents in underserved areas to healthcare and transportation services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must provide services exclusively to residents of Washington County, Maryland. Priority given to projects addressing underserved communities within the county not currently reached by public transit.
requirements_list: Be a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization or local government entity
Be in Good Standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Provide services exclusively to residents of Washington County, Maryland
Demonstrate proven track record of fiscal responsibility and programmatic impact
Propose projects addressing at least one priority area: Non-Emergency Medical Transportation (NEMT), Expansion of Existing Networks, or Last-Mile Solutions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application electronically with all required documents to cahrens@washco-md.net by Friday, March 6, 2026, at 3:00pm. Required documents include: Application Submission Form, program budget (including funds not supplied by Washington County), letters of support, 501(c)(3) nonprofit determination letter, and proof of Good Standing with SDAT (screenshot of current SDAT page).

structured_extraction.program_name: MARBIDCO Next Generation Farmland Acquisition (Next Gen) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides down payment assistance to beginning farmers and young agricultural entrepreneurs purchasing properties that qualify for the County's Agricultural District program. The program offers buyers fifty-one percent of a land-only Fair Market Value appraisal of the property for purchase assistance, capped at five hundred thousand dollars.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides down payment assistance equal to 51% of the land-only Fair Market Value appraisal of the property for purchase, capped at $500,000. After real estate settlement, the landowner must actively pursue a different permanent easement through an approved program and enroll in the County's Agricultural District program within seven years. If after seven years no permanent easement is procured, the land becomes preserved through a MARBIDCO permanent easement. The application process takes approximately six months to complete.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Young and beginning farmers and buyers of agricultural properties that qualify for the County's Agricultural District program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are used as down payment assistance for the purchase of agricultural properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County
requirements_list: Property must qualify for the County's Agricultural District program
Buyer must provide a signed sales contract for the farm
Buyer must work with the County's Land Preservation Office to complete the application
After settlement, landowner must actively pursue a different permanent easement through an approved program and enroll in the County's Agricultural District program within seven years
Application process takes approximately six months to complete
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Buyers must provide a signed sales contract for the farm and fill out the application in conjunction with the County's Land Preservation Office. The completed application is then submitted to MARBIDCO. The process takes roughly six months to complete.

structured_extraction.program_name: MARBIDCO Small Acreage Next Gen (SANG) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides down payment assistance for the purchase of small farms ranging from ten to forty-nine acres in size. This program works similarly to the Next Gen program but differs because there is no seven-year pursuit of a permanent easement after settlement. Instead, the property is considered permanently preserved by MARBIDCO at the time of real estate settlement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides down payment assistance for the purchase of small farms between ten and forty-nine acres in size. Upon real estate settlement, the property is considered permanently preserved by MARBIDCO, eliminating the need for a seven-year pursuit of a permanent easement as required in the Next Gen program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Young and beginning farmers and buyers of small agricultural properties between ten and forty-nine acres in Washington County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are used as down payment assistance for the purchase of small farms between ten and forty-nine acres.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County
requirements_list: Property must be a small farm between ten and forty-nine acres in size
Buyer must meet program eligibility requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested buyers should reach out to the County's Department of Planning & Zoning to inquire about and apply for the SANG program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that preserves high-ranking agricultural properties through the Purchase of Development Rights (PDR) easements. Properties are ranked based on soil quality, proximity to other easements, agricultural operation intensity, and proximity to growth areas and Priority Preservation Areas. Once an easement is purchased, the restrictions remain effective in perpetuity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program purchases Development Rights Easements from qualifying agricultural properties. To date, over 17,000 acres (17,008 acres) have been permanently protected with more than $49 million ($49,855,542) in funding. Applicants are ranked competitively each cycle year, with applications accepted in Spring and approved by the County Commissioners prior to July 1st. Easement restrictions remain in perpetuity.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted in Spring each cycle year, submitted to MALPF prior to July 1st
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners in Washington County with high-ranking agricultural properties who are enrolled in the County's Agricultural Land Preservation District program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are used to purchase Development Rights Easements on agricultural properties, permanently preserving the land from development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County
requirements_list: Property must be enrolled in the County's Agricultural Land Preservation District program
Property must meet minimum qualifications based on soil quality, proximity to other easements, agricultural operation intensity, and proximity to growth areas and Priority Preservation Areas
Applicants are ranked competitively
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted in the Spring of each cycle year. Properties are ranked by the local Agricultural Land Preservation Advisory Board, approved by the County Commissioners, and then sent to MALPF prior to July 1st.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Economic Development Assistance Authority and Fund (MEDAAF)
structured_extraction.program_description: A state financing program offering six different assistance capabilities to help businesses and jurisdictions with economic development projects. The program provides loans, grants, and loan guarantees to support strategic economic development opportunities and local economic needs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MEDAAF offers six financing capabilities: (1) Significant Strategic Economic Development Opportunities providing loans up to $10 million or 20 percent of current fund balance; (2) Local Economic Development Opportunity providing loans up to $5 million or grants/conditional loans up to $2 million with local jurisdiction participation; (3) Direct Assistance to Local Jurisdictions providing up to $3 million (or more for qualified distressed counties) for land acquisition, infrastructure, fixed assets, leasehold improvements, feasibility studies, and economic development plans; (4) Regional or Local Revolving Loan Fund grants of $250,000 annually with local matching funds required; (5) Special Purposes Loans for specific state initiatives including Brownfield Revitalization, Seafood and Aquaculture, Animal Waste, Arts and Entertainment, and Child Care Center programs; (6) Economic Development Opportunities Fund (Sunny Day Fund) requiring minimum capital investment of five times the state assistance amount. Assistance cannot exceed 70 percent of total project costs with limited exceptions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses located in priority funding areas and eligible industries; local jurisdictions
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Economic development projects including land acquisition, infrastructure improvements, fixed asset acquisition, leasehold improvements, feasibility studies, and economic development plans
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in a priority funding area. Applicants are restricted to eligible industry sectors.
requirements_list: Business must be located in a priority funding area
Business must operate in an eligible industry sector
Assistance cannot exceed 70 percent of total project costs with limited exceptions
For Local Economic Development Opportunity, local jurisdiction must sponsor the business and participate with guarantee, direct loan, or grant equal to at least 10 percent of state assistance
For Regional or Local Revolving Loan Fund grants, local government must provide matching funds
For Economic Development Opportunities Fund, applicants must have strong balance sheet and be creditworthy, and projects must be consistent with state's strategic economic development plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants work with DBED to determine eligibility and apply for specific MEDAAF capabilities based on their project needs.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state program that facilitates capital access for economic development projects by issuing private activity revenue bonds and providing credit insurance to reduce lender risk.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MIDFA offers Industrial Revenue Bonds (taxable bonds for fixed asset financing and tax-exempt bonds for non-profit organizations, manufacturing facilities, and certain solid waste projects) and credit insurance programs. Conventional credit insurance covers up to 80 percent of transactions, not to exceed $2.5 million (up to 90 percent for export transactions). Bond program credit insurance covers up to 100 percent of bonds, not to exceed $7.5 million of taxable or tax-exempt bonds. In certain rural areas with qualifying high unemployment, MIDFA offers linked deposits where a certificate of deposit is provided to the lender as a funding source to enable below-market-rate loans to eligible small businesses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses seeking long-term capital financing for fixed assets; 501(c)(3) non-profit organizations; manufacturing facilities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Fixed asset financing; infrastructure projects; solid waste projects (for tax-exempt bonds)
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Priority Funding Areas; certain rural areas with qualifying high unemployment for linked deposits program
requirements_list: Project must be located in Priority Funding Area
Tax-exempt bonds limited to 501(c)(3) non-profit organizations, manufacturing facilities, and certain solid waste projects
Federal tax law restrictions apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants work with MIDFA through participating financial institutions to structure Industrial Revenue Bonds or credit insurance arrangements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A transportation service that helps elderly people and individuals with disabilities meet their transportation needs. The program provides general purpose transportation for eligible individuals who cannot use fixed-route buses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants purchase vouchers at reduced rates, saving at least 50% compared to regular taxi fares. Vouchers come in various denominations and can be used to pay registered taxi providers for rides. Participants can purchase a set number of vouchers per month. Vouchers expire June 30 each year but unused vouchers can be used later in the same year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People age 60 or older and individuals with disabilities who cannot use Washington County Transit fixed-route buses
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General purpose transportation for eligible seniors and people with disabilities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be age 60 or older OR have a disability
Must be unable to utilize Washington County Transit fixed-route buses for one or more reasons
If under age 60, must have application certified by a healthcare professional acknowledging disability
Must have an annually updated application on file
Must reapply annually by June 30
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Washington County Transit office to request an application by mail, or pick one up in person at 1000 West Washington Street, Hagerstown, MD. If under age 60, have a healthcare professional certify your disability on the application. Mail or drop off the completed application at the WCT office (faxes not accepted). You will be notified by mail of your eligibility. Once approved, purchase vouchers at the WCT office or by mail using checks, money orders, or credit cards. Call any registered provider to schedule rides and pay the driver with your vouchers.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state program enacted to focus on Maryland's best natural, agricultural, historical, and cultural areas and most significant rural landscapes. The program encourages local governments and private land trusts to identify Rural Legacy Areas and competitively apply for funds to protect areas vulnerable to sprawl development that can weaken natural resources and the economic value of farming, forestry, recreation, and tourism.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program purchases easements from willing landowners to protect areas vulnerable to sprawl development. To date, more than 9,400 acres (9,421 acres) have been permanently protected with approximately $28.5 million ($28,499,083) in funding. Easement restrictions remain effective in perpetuity.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Qualifying landowners can apply prior to February 1st of each cycle year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Willing landowners in designated Rural Legacy Areas surrounding the Towns of Sharpsburg, Keedysville, Boonsboro and the Rural Villages of St. James, Lappans, Fairplay, Rohrersville, and Gapland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are used to purchase easements from willing landowners to permanently protect agricultural, natural, historical, and cultural areas from sprawl development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County Rural Legacy Areas, including areas surrounding the Towns of Sharpsburg, Keedysville, Boonsboro and the Rural Villages of St. James, Lappans, Fairplay, Rohrersville, and Gapland.
requirements_list: Property must be located within a specified Rural Legacy Area boundary
Landowner must be willing to sell an easement

Applications ranked based on property size, number of development rights, proximity to other permanent easements, agricultural characteristics, historic characteristics, and environmental characteristics
Program is very competitive
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Qualifying landowners can apply for the program prior to February 1st of each cycle year. Applications are ranked based on varying property characteristics and submitted to the Maryland Department of Natural Resources.

structured_extraction.program_description: Comprehensive tax incentives and financial assistance programs designed to support business development, expansion, and job creation in Washington County, including tax credits, loans, grants, and workforce training support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Washington County offers multiple tax incentive programs including: (1) Job Creation & Capital Investment Real Property Tax Credits ranging from 6-15 years (52% years 1-2, 39% years 3-4, 26% years 5-6 for Section 4a; 30% years 1-2, 20% years 3-4, 10% years 5-6 for Section 4b; 100% years 1-5, 75% years 6-10, 50% years 11-15 for Section 4c); (2) New Jobs Tax Credit providing 6-year credits at 52% years 1-2, 39% years 3-4, 26% years 5-6; (3) Research & Development Equipment Tax Exemption exempting R&D equipment from County Business Personal Property Tax; (4) Manufacturing Machinery & Equipment Tax Exemption; (5) Business Inventory Tax Exemption; (6) Pad-Ready Site Commercial Stimulus Program offering 3-year tax credits at 0.4% of construction costs; (7) Brownfield Revitalization Incentive Program (BRIP) providing 50-70% real property tax credits for 5 years (up to 10 years in Enterprise Zones); (8) C-PACE loans for energy efficiency and renewable energy projects with up to 100% fixed-rate financing and 20-year payback periods. City of Hagerstown offers additional programs: Hagerstown Revolving Loan Fund up to $200,000 or 80% of project cost (microenterprise loans up to $5,000), CDBG Microenterprise Grants, and Invest Hagerstown Grants ranging from $5,000-$250,000. Workforce training grants up to $4,500 per worker available through Western Maryland Consortium. Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Program provides tax credits and financial incentives for hiring apprentices.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses, non-profits, and individuals seeking to establish, expand, or relocate operations in Washington County; businesses in manufacturing, construction, and other industries; companies interested in energy efficiency and clean energy projects; small businesses and microenterprises; job seekers and businesses seeking workforce training.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business expansion and relocation; capital improvements; equipment and machinery purchases; building construction and renovation; land improvements; façade enhancements; code compliance; working capital; energy efficiency and renewable energy projects; research and development; inventory; employee recruitment, training, and retention; job creation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland; City of Hagerstown (for city-specific programs); Foreign Trade Zone #255 locations including Hagerstown Regional Airport, Williamsport, Hopewell Valley, Lakeside Corporate Center at Cascade, and Hancock; Enterprise Zones including Hagerstown-Washington County Enterprise Zone (nearly 5,000 acres) and Town of Hancock Enterprise Zone (1,500 acres); Priority Funding Areas for certain programs.
requirements_list: Job Creation & Capital Investment (Section 4a): Minimum 1,500 sq ft new/expanded premises; at least 1 new permanent full-time employee during 12-month period
Job Creation & Capital Investment (Section 4b): Minimum 2,500 sq ft; at least 5 additional new permanent full-time employees during 24-month period
Job Creation & Capital Investment (Section 4c): $10M in capital improvements; create 100 new permanent full-time employees
New Jobs Tax Credit: Minimum 10,000 sq ft expansion; at least 25 new permanent full-time positions; 50% of new jobs must pay at least 135% of average weekly wage; must be in Priority Funding Area
BRIP: Site must qualify for cleanup program; must be owned by inculpable person; must be in participating jurisdiction
C-PACE: Commercial property or non-profit organization; project must involve energy efficiency, renewable energy, or water conservation

CDBG Microenterprise Grant (City of Hagerstown): Located in City of Hagerstown corporate boundaries; 5 or fewer total employees including owner; private for-profit business; in good standing with City and State; in compliance with all City regulations; established and operating for at least 12 months (or provide business plan and business counseling consultation)

Hagerstown Revolving Loan Fund: Organized as proprietorship, partnership, LLC, or corporation; business sales less than $5M annually for last 2 years; credit check required; non-refundable application fee
Hagerstown Revolving Loan Fund Job Requirements: For each $35,000 or fraction thereof borrowed, one full-time job must be created or retained within 2 years from loan closing

Invest Hagerstown Programs: Private developer partnership; projects must address vacant/underutilized properties; 2:1 match required from developer; for homeownership programs, property must be built prior to 1960 and vacant 12 months, or be conversion of rental to owner-occupied
Pad-Ready Site Commercial Stimulus Program: Approved parcel; new improvement must meet construction cost thresholds
Enterprise Zone Program: Located within designated Enterprise Zone boundaries; qualified business status; job creation and capital investment requirements
Maryland Apprenticeship & Training Program: Participating business; apprentice employee
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications vary by program. For tax credit programs (Job Creation & Capital Investment, New Jobs Tax Credit, BRIP, Pad-Ready Site Commercial Stimulus), businesses should contact the Washington County Department of Business Development and Economic Development at (240) 313-2280 or visit www.washco-md.net/business-development. City of Hagerstown programs (Revolving Loan Fund, CDBG Microenterprise Grants, Invest Hagerstown) have specific application requirements and forms available online. C-PACE applications are processed through Abacus Property Solutions in coordination with the Maryland Clean Energy Center; contact (240) 313-2280 for facilitation. Western Maryland Consortium (Debora Gilbert, 301-791-3164, dgilbert@westmdcon.org) handles workforce training grant applications. Maryland Apprenticeship & Training Program inquiries go through Jennifer Runkles, Western MD Apprenticeship & Training Navigator, at 443-615-4758 or jennifer.runkles@maryland.gov. For Enterprise Zone program, contact Washington County Department of Business Development and Economic Development.

structured_extraction.program_name: Job Creation and Capital Investment Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides up to a fifteen year tax credit on the County portion of real estate taxes for qualified businesses that either expand or locate in Washington County and meet specific investment and job creation thresholds. The program includes three tiers based on investment and job creation levels, offering varying credit durations and rates. It helps attract new companies and supports existing companies that expand in Washington County.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County Department of Business Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Real property tax credits on the increased assessed property value for eligible businesses that expand or locate in Washington County. The program offers three tiers: TIER ONE (1,500 sq. ft. and 5 new FTEs within 12 months) provides 3 years of credits at 55%, 40%, 25%; TIER TWO (2,500 sq. ft. and 25 new FTEs within 24 months) provides 6 years of credits at 55%, 55%, 40%, 40%, 25%, 25%; TIER THREE ($20M investment and 200 new FTEs within 24 months, with 80% of FTEs paid 200% of Maryland State minimum wage) provides 15 years of credits at 75% for the first five years, then reduced by 5% annually over the next 10 years until it reaches 25%. Lessors must reduce the amount of taxes for which an eligible business entity is contractually liable by the amount of the tax credit for which the business qualifies.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling, before occupying space or hiring employees
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified for-profit businesses that expand or locate in Washington County and meet specific investment and job creation thresholds. Businesses in Enterprise Zones are not eligible for this program and must apply under the Enterprise Zone Program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applies to real estate taxes on increased assessed property value of newly constructed, renovated, expanded, or previously unoccupied properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County. Businesses in Enterprise Zones are not eligible for this program and must apply under the Enterprise Zone Program.
requirements_list: Meet specific investment thresholds (Tier 1: 1,500 sq. ft., Tier 2: 2,500 sq. ft., Tier 3: $20M investment)
Meet specific job creation thresholds (Tier 1: 5 new FTEs within 12 months, Tier 2: 25 new FTEs within 24 months, Tier 3: 200 new FTEs within 24 months)
For Tier 3, 80% of all new FTEs must be paid 200% of Maryland State minimum wage
Either expand or locate in Washington County
Property must be newly constructed, renovated, expanded, or previously unoccupied and can be owned or leased
Apply before occupying space or hiring employees
Create required FTEs within 12 months for Tier 1 or 24 months for Tiers 2 and 3
Submit Annual Employment and Certification Report by February 1 each year
Continue to meet all applicable program requirements each year to receive the tax credit
Cannot have received a tax credit or exemption for the same property during the same taxable year under any other state or county law
Businesses in Enterprise Zones are not eligible for this program
Lessor must reduce tenant's tax liability by the amount of tax credit if property is leased
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit a letter of intent on company letterhead to the Washington County Department of Business and Economic Development before acquiring or occupying a new space. 2. Complete and submit the official Job Creation and Capital Investment Real Property Tax Credit application with required information including company details, property information, and project details. 3. Notify DBED upon construction completion and provide square footage documentation. 4. Receive certification from Washington County Department of Business and Economic Development (DBED). 5. Create required full-time employees within the specified timeframe (12 months for Tier 1, 24 months for Tiers 2 and 3). 6. Submit Annual Employment and Certification Report by February 1 each year, including employee information (name, last four digits of SSN or ID, home city and state, employment dates, annual salary, hours worked, and benefits information). Note: Businesses are strongly encouraged to engage with DBED early in their planning process. Failure to apply before hiring or occupying new premises may result in ineligibility for the tax credit.
